tree_species_normalized.description: Canonicalized tree species reference rows: expose species_scientific_name upper-cased for matching and include fall_color. One row per species_scientific_name.

tree_records_cleaned.name: tree_records_cleaned
tree_records_cleaned.body_sql:
-- View body: normalized/cleaned tree census records across years 1995-2015
SELECT
  -- carry a stable id per record
  recordid AS tree_id,

  -- canonicalized Latin name: trim and uppercase; prefer spc_latin, fall back to species
  UPPER(TRIM(COALESCE(spc_latin, species, ''))) AS latin_name_up,

  -- canonicalized common name: trim; prefer spc_common, fall back to species (lower/regular case preserved)
  TRIM(COALESCE(spc_common, species, '')) AS common_name,

  -- normalized status: map common variants to 'alive', 'dead', or 'unknown'
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(status)) IN ('dead', 'deceased', 'removed', 'cut down') THEN 'dead'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(status)) IN ('alive', 'live', 'ok', 'healthy', 'stable') THEN 'alive'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(status)) IN ('stump', 'gone') THEN 'dead'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(status)) IN ('', 'unknown', 'unk', 'n/a', 'na', NULL) THEN 'unknown'
    ELSE 'unknown'
  END AS status_normalized,

  -- census_year: derive from _TABLE_SUFFIX when available and numeric; else NULL
  SAFE_CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS census_year

FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '1995' AND '2015'
tree_records_cleaned.description: Normalized/cleaned tree census records: canonicalize Latin and common names (trim, uppercase Latin name), normalize status values (alive/dead/unknown) and ensure planting_year or census_year is present as integer when available. Does not aggregate — one row per tree record.

species_counts_1995_2015.name: species_counts_1995_2015
species_counts_1995_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key: uppercase latin name to serve as grain
  UPPER(s.spc_latin) AS latin_name_up,
  -- carry a representative common name (most common in data could vary; here using MAX to pick a non-null)
  MAX(s.spc_common) AS common_name,
  -- 1995 counts
  SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '1995' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_1995,
  SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '1995' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS alive_1995,
  SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '1995' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dead_1995,
  -- 2015 counts
  SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS total_2015,
  SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS alive_2015,
  SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dead_2015,
  -- differences (2015 minus 1995)
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '1995' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS INT64) AS diff_total_2015_minus_1995,
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '1995' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'alive' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS INT64) AS diff_alive_2015_minus_1995,
  SAFE_CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN _TABLE_SUFFIX = '1995' AND LOWER(s.status) = 'dead' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS INT64) AS diff_dead_2015_minus_1995
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tree_census_*` AS s
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX IN ('1995','2015')
GROUP BY
  latin_name_up
species_counts_1995_2015.description: Reshaped view that pivots counts for two reference years (1995 and 2015) per Latin name: contains total, alive, and dead counts for each of the two years and the differences (2015 minus 1995). Does not apply top-k filtering.

citibike_2016_trips_normalized.name: citibike_2016_trips_normalized
citibike_2016_trips_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  tripduration,
  starttime,
  start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  ROUND(start_station_latitude, 3) AS start_latitude_r3,
  ROUND(start_station_longitude, 3) AS start_longitude_r3,
  end_station_id,
  end_station_name,
  ROUND(end_station_latitude, 3) AS end_latitude_r3,
  ROUND(end_station_longitude, 3) AS end_longitude_r3
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM starttime) = 2016
citibike_2016_trips_normalized.description: All Citi Bike trips occurring in calendar year 2016 with cleaned/normalized start and end station coordinates rounded to 3 decimals, and with relevant columns for route definition and duration.

citibike_routes_agg.name: citibike_routes_agg
citibike_routes_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Rounded origin coordinates (3 decimal places)
  ROUND(t.start_station_latitude, 3) AS start_latitude_r3,
  ROUND(t.start_station_longitude, 3) AS start_longitude_r3,
  -- Rounded destination coordinates (3 decimal places)
  ROUND(t.end_station_latitude, 3) AS end_latitude_r3,
  ROUND(t.end_station_longitude, 3) AS end_longitude_r3,
  -- Aggregates: count of trips and average trip duration (seconds)
  COUNT(1) AS bike_trip_count,
  AVG(t.tripduration) AS avg_bike_duration,
  -- Representative start_station_id for the route: choose ANY_VALUE to keep a stable representative id
  ANY_VALUE(CAST(t.start_station_id AS STRING)) AS start_station_id_repr
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york.citibike_trips` t
WHERE
  -- Exclude rows with NULL coordinates or durations to keep aggregates meaningful
  t.start_station_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND t.start_station_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND t.end_station_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND t.end_station_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND t.tripduration IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  start_latitude_r3,
  start_longitude_r3,
  end_latitude_r3,
  end_longitude_r3
citibike_routes_agg.description: Aggregated metrics per Citi Bike route defined by rounded origin and destination coordinates (3 decimals): count of trips and average bike duration. One row per route origin/destination coordinate combination and also include representative start_station_id values for later station name resolution.

yellow_taxi_2016_durations_by_rounded_co.name: yellow_taxi_2016_durations_by_rounded_coords
yellow_taxi_2016_durations_by_rounded_co.body_sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(pickup_latitude, 3) AS pickup_latitude_r3,
  ROUND(pickup_longitude, 3) AS pickup_longitude_r3,
  ROUND(dropoff_latitude, 3) AS dropoff_latitude_r3,
  ROUND(dropoff_longitude, 3) AS dropoff_longitude_r3,
  COUNT(*) AS taxi_trip_count,
  AVG(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND)) AS avg_taxi_duration
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2016'
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) >= 0
GROUP BY
  pickup_latitude_r3,
  pickup_longitude_r3,
  dropoff_latitude_r3,
  dropoff_longitude_r3
yellow_taxi_2016_durations_by_rounded_co.description: Aggregated taxi trip metrics for 2016 from yellow taxi tables: average taxi trip duration in seconds and trip count, grouped by pickup and dropoff coordinates rounded to 3 decimals.

citibike_trips_2018_cohort.name: citibike_trips_2018_cohort
citibike_trips_2018_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry original trip-level columns (as requested)
  tripduration,
  starttime,
  stoptime,
  start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  end_station_id,
  end_station_name,
  bikeid,
  usertype,
  birth_year,
  gender,
  -- synthetic trip_id to define grain (one row per trip)
  CONCAT(CAST(starttime AS STRING), "-", CAST(bikeid AS STRING), "-", CAST(start_station_id AS STRING), "-", CAST(end_station_id AS STRING)) AS trip_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_citibike.citibike_trips`
WHERE
  -- lift literals out: 2018 calendar year in source timezone (starttime is DATETIME)
  starttime >= DATETIME('2018-01-01') AND starttime < DATETIME('2019-01-01')
citibike_trips_2018_cohort.description: All citibike trips whose start time is within the 2018 calendar year (>= 2018-01-01 and < 2019-01-01) in the source timezone, preserving original trip-level columns.

yellow_trips_valid_metrics.name: yellow_trips_valid_metrics
yellow_trips_valid_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  -- duration in seconds, computed from timestamps; NULL if either timestamp is NULL
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_datetime IS NULL OR dropoff_datetime IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64)
  END AS trip_duration_seconds,
  -- duration in minutes as floating point (seconds / 60.0)
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_datetime IS NULL OR dropoff_datetime IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_DIVIDE(CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS FLOAT64), 60.0)
  END AS trip_duration_minutes,
  -- positive_duration flag: TRUE when duration in seconds > 0
  CASE
    WHEN pickup_datetime IS NULL OR dropoff_datetime IS NULL THEN FALSE
    ELSE TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
  END AS positive_duration
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
-- lift date range filtering out of the view; callers should restrict _TABLE_SUFFIX as needed
yellow_trips_valid_metrics.description: Normalized trip-level metrics computed from raw yellow trips: trip duration in seconds and minutes, and a boolean/flag for positive duration. Keeps one row per trip.

taxi_zones_borough.name: taxi_zones_borough
taxi_zones_borough.description: Taxi zone metadata including zone_id and borough to allow spatial join of trips to borough names.

yellow_trips_with_brooklyn_filter.name: yellow_trips_with_brooklyn_filter
yellow_trips_with_brooklyn_filter.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry core trip timestamps and measures
  t.pickup_datetime AS pickup_datetime,
  t.dropoff_datetime AS dropoff_datetime,
  t.passenger_count AS passenger_count,
  t.trip_distance AS trip_distance,
  -- carry location ids for joinability
  t.pickup_location_id AS pickup_location_id,
  t.dropoff_location_id AS dropoff_location_id,
  -- compute duration minutes from timestamps (lift any literals out of the view)
  TIMESTAMP_DIFF(t.dropoff_datetime, t.pickup_datetime, SECOND) / 60.0 AS trip_duration_minutes,
  -- boroughs from joined zone lookups (nullable if no match)
  pz.borough AS pickup_borough,
  dz.borough AS dropoff_borough,
  -- unique_trip_id grain: compose stable identifier from pickup/dropoff timestamps + vendor + locations + passenger_count
  -- keep deterministic and carry enough info to be unique per trip row
  CONCAT(
    SAFE_CAST(t.data_file_year AS STRING), "_",
    SAFE_CAST(t.data_file_month AS STRING), "_",
    SAFE_CAST(t.pickup_datetime AS STRING), "_",
    SAFE_CAST(t.dropoff_datetime AS STRING), "_",
    IFNULL(t.vendor_id, "v"), "_",
    IFNULL(t.pickup_location_id, "pl"), "_",
    IFNULL(t.dropoff_location_id, "dl")
  ) AS unique_trip_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*` AS t
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS pz
ON
  t.pickup_location_id = pz.zone_id
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS dz
ON
  t.dropoff_location_id = dz.zone_id
WHERE
  -- No literal borough/date/passenger/distance/duration filters here per instructions;
  -- this view is intended to be filtered later to require both boroughs = 'Brooklyn' and to apply date, passenger_count, trip_distance, and positive-duration filters.
  TRUE
yellow_trips_with_brooklyn_filter.description: Denormalized trip-level rows joining normalized yellow trips to pickup and dropoff taxi zones; intended to be filtered later to require both pickup and dropoff borough = 'Brooklyn' and to apply date, passenger_count, trip_distance, and positive-duration filters.

yellow_taxi_trips_raw_filtered.name: yellow_taxi_trips_raw_filtered
yellow_taxi_trips_raw_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  fare_amount,
  tip_amount,
  tolls_amount,
  mta_tax,
  total_amount,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
  AND passenger_count > 0
  AND trip_distance IS NOT NULL AND trip_distance >= 0
  AND fare_amount IS NOT NULL AND fare_amount >= 0
  AND tip_amount IS NOT NULL AND tip_amount >= 0
  AND tolls_amount IS NOT NULL AND tolls_amount >= 0
  AND mta_tax IS NOT NULL AND mta_tax >= 0
  AND total_amount IS NOT NULL AND total_amount >= 0
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(0) IS NOT NULL -- no-op to keep consistent style
  AND dropoff_datetime > pickup_datetime
yellow_taxi_trips_raw_filtered.description: Row-level filtered cohort of yellow taxi trip records from the sharded tlc_yellow_trips tables for the relevant date range, applying basic data validity filters (non-negative monetary and distance fields, passenger_count > 0, dropoff after pickup) but not applying borough/zone exclusions or final date-window bounds beyond shard selection.

taxi_pickup_zones_with_boroughs.name: taxi_pickup_zones_with_boroughs
taxi_pickup_zones_with_boroughs.description: Mapping of taxi zone ids to canonical zone_name and borough using the taxi zone geometry reference; one row per taxi zone (zone_id).

trips_with_tip_rate_and_category.name: trips_with_tip_rate_and_category
trips_with_tip_rate_and_category.body_sql:
SELECT
  tz.borough AS pickup_borough,
  tz.zone_name AS pickup_zone_name,
  t.pickup_location_id,
  t.pickup_datetime,
  t.tip_amount,
  t.total_amount,
  -- tip_rate as a percent number (e.g. 12.5 for 12.5%)
  CASE
    WHEN t.total_amount IS NULL OR t.total_amount = 0 THEN 0
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC)
  END AS tip_rate,
  CASE
    WHEN t.total_amount IS NULL OR t.total_amount = 0 THEN 'no tip'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) < 5 THEN 'Less than 5%'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) >= 5
         AND SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) < 10 THEN '5% to 10%'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) >= 10
         AND SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) < 15 THEN '10% to 15%'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) >= 15
         AND SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) < 20 THEN '15% to 20%'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) >= 20
         AND SAFE_CAST(t.tip_amount / t.total_amount * 100 AS NUMERIC) < 25 THEN '20% to 25%'
    ELSE 'More than 25%'
  END AS tip_category
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*` AS t
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS tz
ON
  t.pickup_location_id = tz.zone_id
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'
trips_with_tip_rate_and_category.description: Per-trip computation of tip_rate (percent) with total_amount = 0 treated as tip_rate = 0, and assignment of tip_category based on tip_rate buckets: 'no tip', 'Less than 5%', '5% to 10%', '10% to 15%', '15% to 20%', '20% to 25%', 'More than 25%'. Keeps one row per trip with pickup borough attached; does not perform final aggregation counts.

taxi_zone_geography.name: taxi_zone_geography
taxi_zone_geography.body_sql:
SELECT
  zone_id AS location_id,
  NULLIF(TRIM(zone_name), '') AS zone,
  NULLIF(TRIM(borough), '') AS borough
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom`
taxi_zone_geography.description: Canonical mapping of taxi zone id to its geography (borough and zone name). One row per taxi zone id, with normalized borough and zone fields and NULLs handled consistently.

yellow_taxi_trips_clean.name: yellow_taxi_trips_clean
yellow_taxi_trips_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through original timestamps and pickup location for joinability
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  pickup_location_id,
  -- canonical numeric types and renamed/kept columns as requested
  CAST(passenger_count AS INT64) AS passenger_count,
  CAST(trip_distance AS NUMERIC) AS trip_distance,
  CAST(fare_amount AS NUMERIC) AS fare_amount,
  CAST(tip_amount AS NUMERIC) AS tip_amount,
  CAST(tolls_amount AS NUMERIC) AS tolls_amount,
  CAST(mta_tax AS NUMERIC) AS mta_tax,
  CAST(total_amount AS NUMERIC) AS total_amount,
  -- tip_rate computed as tip_amount / fare_amount when fare_amount > 0 else NULL
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS NUMERIC) > 0 THEN SAFE_DIVIDE(SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS NUMERIC), SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS NUMERIC))
    ELSE NULL
  END AS tip_rate
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- keep only rows with a pickup zone for later geographic joins
  pickup_location_id IS NOT NULL
  -- basic temporal consistency: dropoff after pickup
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime > pickup_datetime
  -- passenger count must be positive
  AND SAFE_CAST(passenger_count AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(passenger_count AS INT64) > 0
  -- numeric monetary and distance fields must be non-negative (allow zero)
  AND (trip_distance IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS NUMERIC) >= 0)
  AND (fare_amount IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS NUMERIC) >= 0)
  AND (tip_amount IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS NUMERIC) >= 0)
  AND (tolls_amount IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(tolls_amount AS NUMERIC) >= 0)
  AND (mta_tax IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(mta_tax AS NUMERIC) >= 0)
  AND (total_amount IS NOT NULL AND SAFE_CAST(total_amount AS NUMERIC) >= 0)
yellow_taxi_trips_clean.description: Cleaned yellow taxi trip rows with canonical numeric types and data-quality filters applied (non-negative monetary and distance fields, positive passenger_count, dropoff > pickup). Keeps only trips that have a non-null pickup_location_id for later geographic join. Does not apply date-range literals so it remains reusable.

pickup_borough_trip_counts.name: pickup_borough_trip_counts
pickup_borough_trip_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  tz.borough AS pickup_borough,
  COUNT(1) AS total_trips,
  SUM(CASE WHEN t.tip_amount = 0 OR t.tip_amount IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_tip_trips
FROM `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*` AS t
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS tz
  ON t.pickup_location_id = tz.zone_id
-- NOTE: lift any date-range filtering out of the view; callers should filter on _TABLE_SUFFIX or pickup_datetime.
-- Also callers may apply additional cleaning (e.g., positive trip distance/duration) when querying the view.
GROUP BY tz.borough
pickup_borough_trip_counts.description: Aggregate trip-level counts per pickup borough for cleaned yellow taxi trips joined to taxi zone geography. Produces total trips and trips with tip_rate = 0 per pickup borough. Date-range and other question-specific time windowing should be applied when querying this view.

taxi_trip_rows_cleaned.name: taxi_trip_rows_cleaned
taxi_trip_rows_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carrier id as provided (keep as string)
  vendor_id,
  -- ensure timestamps; some shards already have TIMESTAMP, but guard against NULLs
  SAFE_CAST(pickup_datetime AS TIMESTAMP) AS pickup_datetime,
  SAFE_CAST(dropoff_datetime AS TIMESTAMP) AS dropoff_datetime,
  -- passenger_count may be NULL; keep as INT64 when possible
  SAFE_CAST(passenger_count AS INT64) AS passenger_count,
  -- trip_distance as NUMERIC (meters->miles not needed; field already miles)
  SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS NUMERIC) AS trip_distance,
  -- canonicalize pickup/dropoff location ids as strings (some shards use numbers or strings)
  SAFE_CAST(pickup_location_id AS STRING) AS pickup_location_id,
  SAFE_CAST(dropoff_location_id AS STRING) AS dropoff_location_id,
  -- fare-related fields cast to NUMERIC and NULL-safe
  SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS NUMERIC) AS fare_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS NUMERIC) AS tip_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tolls_amount AS NUMERIC) AS tolls_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(mta_tax AS NUMERIC) AS mta_tax,
  SAFE_CAST(total_amount AS NUMERIC) AS total_amount,
  -- indicate source by table suffix to keep rows joinable and traceable
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS trip_id_source_table
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023'

UNION ALL

SELECT
  vendor_id,
  SAFE_CAST(pickup_datetime AS TIMESTAMP) AS pickup_datetime,
  SAFE_CAST(dropoff_datetime AS TIMESTAMP) AS dropoff_datetime,
  SAFE_CAST(passenger_count AS INT64) AS passenger_count,
  SAFE_CAST(trip_distance AS NUMERIC) AS trip_distance,
  SAFE_CAST(pickup_location_id AS STRING) AS pickup_location_id,
  SAFE_CAST(dropoff_location_id AS STRING) AS dropoff_location_id,
  SAFE_CAST(fare_amount AS NUMERIC) AS fare_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tip_amount AS NUMERIC) AS tip_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(tolls_amount AS NUMERIC) AS tolls_amount,
  SAFE_CAST(mta_tax AS NUMERIC) AS mta_tax,
  SAFE_CAST(total_amount AS NUMERIC) AS total_amount,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS trip_id_source_table
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_green_trips_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2014' AND '2023'
taxi_trip_rows_cleaned.description: Canonicalized, row-level taxi trip records from yearly shard tables with normalized column names and basic type/NULL handling. This produces one row per trip with parsed pickup and dropoff timestamps, numeric fare-related fields cast to numeric, and canonical pickup/dropoff location IDs.

taxi_trip_filters_cohort.name: taxi_trip_filters_cohort
taxi_trip_filters_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  fare_amount,
  tip_amount,
  tolls_amount,
  mta_tax,
  total_amount
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_green_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- date shard selector: lift literal bounds out of view (caller should add WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2014' AND '2023' or similar)
  TRUE
  -- intrinsic non-null / quality filters
  AND vendor_id IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND passenger_count IS NOT NULL
  AND trip_distance IS NOT NULL
  AND fare_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND tip_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND tolls_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND mta_tax IS NOT NULL
  AND total_amount IS NOT NULL
  -- positive numeric fields where appropriate
  AND passenger_count > 0
  AND trip_distance > 0
  AND fare_amount >= 0
  AND total_amount >= 0
  -- nonzero duration and dropoff after pickup
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT
  vendor_id,
  pickup_datetime,
  dropoff_datetime,
  passenger_count,
  trip_distance,
  pickup_location_id,
  dropoff_location_id,
  fare_amount,
  tip_amount,
  tolls_amount,
  mta_tax,
  total_amount
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_yellow_trips_*`
WHERE
  -- date shard selector: lift literal bounds out of view (caller should add WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2011' AND '2023' or similar)
  TRUE
  -- intrinsic non-null / quality filters
  AND vendor_id IS NOT NULL
  AND pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND passenger_count IS NOT NULL
  AND trip_distance IS NOT NULL
  AND fare_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND tip_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND tolls_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND mta_tax IS NOT NULL
  AND total_amount IS NOT NULL
  -- positive numeric fields where appropriate
  AND passenger_count > 0
  AND trip_distance > 0
  AND fare_amount >= 0
  AND total_amount >= 0
  -- nonzero duration and dropoff after pickup
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(dropoff_datetime, pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
taxi_trip_filters_cohort.description: Filtered cohort of taxi trips meeting intrinsic trip-level quality and predicate conditions (time bounds, positive/nonnull numeric fields, nonzero duration, passenger_count and trip_distance thresholds, and dropoff after pickup). This is a reusable cohort definition without top-k or ordering.

taxi_zones.name: taxi_zones
taxi_zones.body_sql:
SELECT
  zone_id AS location_id,
  zone_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom`
taxi_zones.description: Taxi zone reference table mapping location IDs to human-readable zone names and related geographic metadata. One row per location (zone) id.

trip_enriched_with_zones_and_metrics.name: trip_enriched_with_zones_and_metrics
trip_enriched_with_zones_and_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.zone_name AS pickup_zone_name,
  d.zone_name AS dropoff_zone_name,
  CAST(TIMESTAMP_DIFF(t.dropoff_datetime, t.pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS INT64) AS trip_duration_seconds,
  CASE
    WHEN t.trip_distance IS NULL OR TIMESTAMP_DIFF(t.dropoff_datetime, t.pickup_datetime, SECOND) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(t.trip_distance * 3600.0 / TIMESTAMP_DIFF(t.dropoff_datetime, t.pickup_datetime, SECOND) AS FLOAT64)
  END AS driving_speed_mph,
  CASE
    WHEN t.total_amount = 0 OR t.total_amount IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(100.0 * IFNULL(t.tip_amount, 0) / t.total_amount AS FLOAT64)
  END AS tip_rate_percent,
  t.total_amount
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.tlc_green_trips_*` AS t
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS p
    ON t.pickup_location_id = p.zone_id
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.new_york_taxi_trips.taxi_zone_geom` AS d
    ON t.dropoff_location_id = d.zone_id
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2014' AND '2023'
  AND t.pickup_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND t.dropoff_datetime IS NOT NULL
  AND TIMESTAMP_DIFF(t.dropoff_datetime, t.pickup_datetime, SECOND) > 0
  AND t.total_amount IS NOT NULL
  AND t.total_amount <> 0
trip_enriched_with_zones_and_metrics.description: Denormalized trip rows joined to pickup and dropoff zone names with computed trip-level metrics: trip_duration_seconds, driving_speed_mph, tip_rate_percent. Excludes rows that would cause division-by-zero for tip rate (total_amount = 0) or zero-duration. This view is a prepared wide relation suitable for top-k selection.

stations_canonical.name: stations_canonical
stations_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- prefer station_id when present and non-empty, else build fallback key
  CASE
    WHEN station_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(station_id) <> '' THEN station_id
    ELSE CONCAT(TRIM(station_name), '||', TRIM(IFNULL(complex_id, '')))
  END AS station_id,
  station_name,
  complex_id,
  borough_name,
  -- canonical_station_key must be unique per logical station (use same logic as station_id fallback)
  CASE
    WHEN station_id IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(station_id) <> '' THEN station_id
    ELSE CONCAT(TRIM(station_name), '||', TRIM(IFNULL(complex_id, '')))
  END AS canonical_station_key
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.stations`
WHERE
  borough_name IS NOT NULL
stations_canonical.description: Canonicalized set of subway stations with a stable station identifier. For each row produce a single station record using stations.station_id when present; if station_id is NULL or empty, fall back to the combination of station_name and complex_id to identify the station. Include borough_name and station_name for later joins and filtering. Exclude rows where borough_name IS NULL.

station_entrance_ada_flags.name: station_entrance_ada_flags
station_entrance_ada_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- entrance identifier: compose from station name + entrance coordinates to ensure uniqueness per entrance row
  CONCAT(station_name, '|' , CAST(entrance_lat AS STRING), '|' , CAST(entrance_lon AS STRING)) AS entrance_id,
  station_name,
  sc.complex_id,
  entry,
  ada_compliant,
  entrance_lat AS latitude,
  entrance_lon AS longitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_entrances` se
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.new_york_subway.station_complexes` sc
ON
  -- join by station_name to bring complex_id; keep left to preserve entrances without complex mapping
  se.station_name = sc.complex_name
WHERE
  -- filter to entrances that are relevant for ADA-entry qualification:
  -- keep only entrances that are actual entry points (entry = TRUE) and that have explicit ADA compliance flag (TRUE or FALSE)
  entry IS TRUE
  AND ada_compliant IS NOT NULL
station_entrance_ada_flags.description: Row-level set of station entrances filtered to only those entrance records relevant for ADA-entry qualification. Keep entrance rows with boolean flags for entry and ada_compliant (no aggregations).

bikeshare_stations_canonical.name: bikeshare_stations_canonical
bikeshare_stations_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations`
WHERE
  latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  station_id, latitude, longitude
bikeshare_stations_canonical.description: Canonicalized station reference rows with numeric latitude/longitude columns suitable for geodesic calculations. Keeps one row per station_id and ensures latitude and longitude are cast to consistent numeric types and excludes rows with NULL coordinates.

valid_bikeshare_trips.name: valid_bikeshare_trips
valid_bikeshare_trips.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id,
  t.bike_number,
  t.start_station_id,
  t.end_station_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips` AS t
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations` AS s_start
ON
  t.start_station_id = s_start.station_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations` AS s_end
ON
  t.end_station_id = s_end.station_id
WHERE
  t.start_station_id IS NOT NULL
  AND t.end_station_id IS NOT NULL
valid_bikeshare_trips.description: Subset of bikeshare_trips where start and end station ids are present (not NULL) and represent actual station identifiers (existence will be enforced by joining to stations). Preserves one row per trip.

trip_station_coordinates.name: trip_station_coordinates
trip_station_coordinates.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id,
  t.bike_number,
  t.start_station_id,
  t.end_station_id,
  s_start.latitude AS start_latitude,
  s_start.longitude AS start_longitude,
  s_end.latitude AS end_latitude,
  s_end.longitude AS end_longitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips` AS raw_trips
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations` AS stations
  ON TRUE
-- Use the existing normalized/filtered views if available; otherwise derive valid trips and canonical stations inline.
-- Build valid trips (keep required columns) by filtering trips with non-null station ids and trip_id
JOIN (
  SELECT trip_id, bike_number, start_station_id, end_station_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
  WHERE trip_id IS NOT NULL
    AND start_station_id IS NOT NULL
    AND end_station_id IS NOT NULL
) AS t
  ON t.trip_id = raw_trips.trip_id
-- Canonicalize stations: pick station_id, latitude, longitude from stations table
JOIN (
  SELECT station_id, latitude, longitude
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations`
) AS s_start
  ON s_start.station_id = t.start_station_id
JOIN (
  SELECT station_id, latitude, longitude
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_stations`
) AS s_end
  ON s_end.station_id = t.end_station_id
trip_station_coordinates.description: Join each valid trip to the canonical station coordinates for its start and end stations, producing one row per trip with start/end latitudes and longitudes for distance calculation. Does not compute distances yet.

bikeshare_trips_filtered.name: bikeshare_trips_filtered
bikeshare_trips_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id AS id,
  start_date,
  duration_sec
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
WHERE
  start_date IS NOT NULL
  AND duration_sec IS NOT NULL
bikeshare_trips_filtered.description: Filter bikeshare trips to rows with non-null start_date and non-null duration_sec. This produces the cohort of valid trips for further time-based processing.

bikeshare_trips_ranked_within_ym.name: bikeshare_trips_ranked_within_ym
bikeshare_trips_ranked_within_ym.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(t.trip_id AS INT64) AS id,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', t.start_date) AS year_month,
  t.start_date AS start_date_pst,
  t.duration_sec AS duration_sec,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', t.start_date) ORDER BY t.start_date ASC, t.trip_id ASC) AS row_number_asc,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', t.start_date) ORDER BY t.start_date DESC, t.trip_id DESC) AS row_number_desc,
  COUNT(1) OVER (PARTITION BY FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', t.start_date)) AS count_in_ym
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips` AS t
bikeshare_trips_ranked_within_ym.description: Within each year_month, rank trips by chronological start_date to identify ordering (earliest to latest). Include a row number and reverse row number per year_month to support selecting first and last trips.

bikeshare_trips_ym_aggregates.name: bikeshare_trips_ym_aggregates
bikeshare_trips_ym_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- year_month in format YYYY-MM (derived from start_date)
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', start_of_month) AS year_month,
  -- count of trips in the year_month
  COUNT(*) AS count_in_ym,
  -- minimum duration in seconds
  MIN(duration_sec) AS min_duration_sec,
  -- maximum duration in seconds
  MAX(duration_sec) AS max_duration_sec
FROM (
  SELECT
    -- normalize start_date to first day of month at midnight UTC for grouping
    TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(start_date, MONTH) AS start_of_month,
    duration_sec
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco.bikeshare_trips`
)
GROUP BY
  start_of_month
ORDER BY
  start_of_month
bikeshare_trips_ym_aggregates.description: Compute per year_month aggregates (count, min duration_sec, max duration_sec) to support summary metrics for each year_month.

station_region_lookup.name: station_region_lookup
station_region_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id AS station_id,
  s.region_id AS region_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info` AS s
station_region_lookup.description: Mapping of bikeshare station identifiers to their region metadata (one row per station). Canonicalizes the station->region relationship for joining trips to regions.

trips_with_month_and_minutes.name: trips_with_month_and_minutes
trips_with_month_and_minutes.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM t.end_date) AS month,
  t.subscriber_type AS subscriber_type,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(t.duration_sec, 60) AS minutes
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
trips_with_month_and_minutes.description: Normalize trip rows to attach calendar month (1-12) extracted from end_date and compute trip duration in minutes (duration_sec/60). Preserves one row per trip.

stops_base.name: stops_base
stops_base.description: Canonicalized stops table with one row per stops.stop_id; preserves stop_id, stop_name and any canonical fields required for joins (no question-specific literals).

stop_times_with_stops.name: stop_times_with_stops
stop_times_with_stops.body_sql:
SELECT
  st.trip_id AS trip_id,
  st.stop_id AS stop_id,
  st.stop_sequence AS stop_sequence,
  st.arrival_time AS arrival_time,
  st.departure_time AS departure_time,
  s.stop_name AS stop_name
FROM `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_transit_muni.stop_times` AS st
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_transit_muni.stops` AS s
  ON CAST(st.stop_id AS STRING) = s.stop_id
stop_times_with_stops.description: Denormalized stop_times joined to stops (by stop_id) producing one row per stop_times record with stop_name included for filtering and time columns for later aggregation.

bike_trips_raw.name: bike_trips_raw
bike_trips_raw.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  start_station_id,
  start_station_name,
  start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude,
  end_station_id,
  end_station_name,
  end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude,
  duration_sec,
  NULL AS trip_distance
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
WHERE
  trip_id IS NOT NULL
  AND start_station_name IS NOT NULL
  AND start_station_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND start_station_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_name IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND end_station_longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND duration_sec IS NOT NULL
bike_trips_raw.description: Raw bike trip rows selected from the bikeshare_trips table with essential non-null fields required for downstream processing (start/end station names and coordinates, start/end station ids if present, trip duration in seconds, and any recorded trip distance if available). This filters out rows with NULLs in these key columns so later steps can assume coordinates and duration exist.

bike_trip_geodesic_distances.name: bike_trip_geodesic_distances
bike_trip_geodesic_distances.body_sql:
SELECT
  trip_id,
  start_station_name,
  end_station_name,
  start_station_latitude,
  start_station_longitude,
  end_station_latitude,
  end_station_longitude,
  duration_sec,
  ST_DISTANCE(
    ST_GEOGPOINT(start_station_longitude, start_station_latitude),
    ST_GEOGPOINT(end_station_longitude, end_station_latitude)
  ) AS distance_m
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
bike_trip_geodesic_distances.description: Compute the straight-line (geodesic) distance in meters between each trip's start and end station coordinates and normalize/standardize distance and duration fields for speed calculations.

bikeshare_stations_points.name: bikeshare_stations_points
bikeshare_stations_points.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  lat,
  lon,
  ST_GEOGPOINT(lon, lat) AS station_point
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_bikeshare.bikeshare_station_info`
WHERE
  lat IS NOT NULL
  AND lon IS NOT NULL
  AND station_id IS NOT NULL
bikeshare_stations_points.description: One row per bikeshare station with a canonical geographic point and cleaned station identifier; exclude stations missing latitude or longitude.

sfpd_incidents_points.name: sfpd_incidents_points
sfpd_incidents_points.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(si.unique_key AS INT64) AS unique_key,
  si.latitude AS latitude,
  si.longitude AS longitude,
  ST_GEOGPOINT(si.longitude, si.latitude) AS incident_point
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.san_francisco_sfpd_incidents.sfpd_incidents` si
WHERE
  si.latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND si.longitude IS NOT NULL
sfpd_incidents_points.description: One row per police incident with a canonical geographic point and cleaned incident identifier; exclude incidents missing latitude or longitude.

neighborhood_geometries.name: neighborhood_geometries
neighborhood_geometries.description: One row per San Francisco neighborhood containing the neighborhood name and its polygon geometry for spatial containment tests.

countries_midyear_population_2020.name: countries_midyear_population_2020
countries_midyear_population_2020.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.country_code AS country_code,
  m.midyear_population AS midyear_population,
  m.country_name AS country_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS m
WHERE
  m.year = 2020
  -- Ensure canonical "Both sexes" rows if dataset contains sex-specific rows;
  -- keep rows where midyear_population is not null to produce one row per country_code.
  AND m.midyear_population IS NOT NULL
countries_midyear_population_2020.description: Rows of countries' midyear total population for the year 2020 (one row per country-code), keeping canonical country identifiers and population value. This filters the midyear_population table to year = 2020 but does not perform any further aggregation beyond one row per country_code (if the source has multiple sex rows, the canonicalization step should ensure a single 'Both sexes' row is present).

age_specific_population_both_sexes.name: age_specific_population_both_sexes
age_specific_population_both_sexes.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  age,
  population
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific`
WHERE
  year = 2020
  AND sex = 'Both sexes'
age_specific_population_both_sexes.description: Age-specific midyear population rows for both sexes (or the table's combined-sex rows) for year 2020, one row per country_code and age. This filters midyear_population_agespecific to year = 2020 and sex = 'Both sexes' and includes age and population for each country and age.

population_under_age_by_country.name: population_under_age_by_country
population_under_age_by_country.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.country_code,
  SUM(a.population) AS population_under_age_min_max
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific` AS a
WHERE
  a.age BETWEEN @min_age AND @max_age
GROUP BY
  a.country_code
population_under_age_by_country.description: For each country_code, aggregate sum of age-specific population for a specified age range (one row per country_code). This represents a reusable grouped measure: total population for ages within a provided bound (e.g., 0–19) using the age_specific_population_both_sexes rows as input.

midyear_population_5yr_age_sex_agegroup_.name: midyear_population_5yr_age_sex_agegroup_rows
midyear_population_5yr_age_sex_agegroup_.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code AS country_code,
  year AS year,
  starting_age AS starting_age,
  ending_age AS ending_age,
  midyear_population AS population,
  total_flag AS total_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_5yr_age_sex`
WHERE
  total_flag = 'A'

semantic_filters.total_flag: indicates age-group rows (exclude overall total rows)

midyear_population_5yr_age_sex_agegroup_.description: Select the rows from the 5-year age-sex midyear population table that represent age-group population records (exclude total/aggregate rows) and keep age boundaries and country/year identifiers. This is a row-level cohort of age-group records.

country_year_population_shares.name: country_year_population_shares
country_year_population_shares.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.country_code AS country_code,
  m.country_name AS country_name,
  m.year AS year,
  -- population_under_age: lift threshold literal out of the view; users should substitute TARGET_AGE when querying this view.
  -- Here we compute population under TARGET_AGE by summing age-specific population rows with age < @TARGET_AGE.
  SUM(a.population) AS population_under_age,
  m.midyear_population AS total_population,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(a.population), m.midyear_population) * 100.0 AS percentage_under_age
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population` AS m
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.midyear_population_agespecific` AS a
ON
  m.country_code = a.country_code
  AND m.year = a.year
-- Note: the threshold age must be provided at query time as a parameter named TARGET_AGE.
-- To keep the view reusable we do not hardcode the age here; callers should filter age < @TARGET_AGE.
WHERE
  a.age < @TARGET_AGE
GROUP BY
  m.country_code,
  m.country_name,
  m.year,
  m.midyear_population
country_year_population_shares.description: Join aggregated under-age population to total midyear population per country and year, computing the share/percentage of population under the target age. Keeps country identifiers and numeric measures for downstream ranking/filtering.

country_basic_info.name: country_basic_info
country_basic_info.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  country_name,
  country_area
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.country_names_area`
WHERE
  country_code IS NOT NULL
country_basic_info.description: One row per country with its canonical name and area (cleaned); selects country_code, country_name, and country_area from the country-area lookup table and filters out rows with NULL country_code.

country_net_migration_by_year.name: country_net_migration_by_year
country_net_migration_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  year,
  net_migration
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.birth_death_growth_rates`
WHERE
  country_code IS NOT NULL
  AND year IS NOT NULL
country_net_migration_by_year.description: One row per country-year providing the net_migration rate (net number of migrants per 1,000 population) for that year from the birth/death/growth rates table; retains country_code, year, and net_migration and excludes rows with NULL country_code or NULL year.

countries_with_area_above_threshold.name: countries_with_area_above_threshold
countries_with_area_above_threshold.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code AS country_code,
  country_area AS country_area
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.country_names_area`
countries_with_area_above_threshold.description: Cohort of countries whose area exceeds a configurable threshold; one row per country (country_code) with its area. This is a filterable cohort (threshold applied later).

country_year_net_migration_with_name.name: country_year_net_migration_with_name
country_year_net_migration_with_name.body_sql:
SELECT
  nm.country_code AS country_code,
  COALESCE(cb.country_name, nm.country_name) AS country_name,
  cb.country_area AS country_area,
  nm.year AS year,
  nm.net_migration AS net_migration
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.birth_death_growth_rates` AS nm
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_international.country_names_area` AS cb
ON
  nm.country_code = cb.country_code
country_year_net_migration_with_name.description: Denormalized one-row-per country-year combining net migration rates with country basic info (name and area) by joining country_net_migration_by_year to country_basic_info on country_code. Used to apply year and area filters and to select display columns.

country_level_rows.name: country_level_rows
country_level_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  location_key,
  country_name,
  aggregation_level,
  cumulative_confirmed,
  cumulative_recovered
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  aggregation_level = 0
country_level_rows.description: Select rows that represent country-level observations from the raw covid19_open_data table (filter by aggregation_level indicating country granularity). Keep all date and cumulative metrics for further processing.

country_date_numeric_normalized.name: country_date_numeric_normalized
country_date_numeric_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  location_key,
  -- canonicalize country name by trimming and using NULLIF to avoid empty strings
  NULLIF(TRIM(country_name), '') AS country_name,
  -- ensure numeric cumulative_confirmed: cast if needed, coalesce NULL to 0
  COALESCE(CAST(cumulative_confirmed AS INT64), 0) AS cumulative_confirmed,
  -- ensure numeric cumulative_recovered: cast if needed, coalesce NULL to 0
  COALESCE(CAST(cumulative_recovered AS INT64), 0) AS cumulative_recovered
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  -- restrict to country-level rows if aggregation_level is provided (lifted literal)
  aggregation_level = 0
country_date_numeric_normalized.description: Normalize and cast numeric cumulative fields and canonicalize country name; ensure cumulative_confirmed and cumulative_recovered are numeric and handle NULLs (e.g., coalesce to 0) so they are safe for arithmetic.

country_date_recovery_rate.name: country_date_recovery_rate
country_date_recovery_rate.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  location_key,
  country_name,
  cumulative_confirmed,
  cumulative_recovered,
  CASE
    WHEN cumulative_confirmed IS NULL OR cumulative_confirmed = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_DIVIDE(cumulative_recovered, cumulative_confirmed) * 100
  END AS recovery_rate_percentage
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
country_date_recovery_rate.description: Compute per-country, per-date derived measures including recovery_rate_percentage = (cumulative_recovered / cumulative_confirmed) * 100. Do not apply top-k or date filters here; keep one row per country-date.

us_covid19_daily_rows.name: us_covid19_daily_rows
us_covid19_daily_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  country_name,
  new_confirmed,
  cumulative_confirmed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  country_name = 'United States'
  AND aggregation_level = 0
us_covid19_daily_rows.description: All daily rows for the United States from the covid19_open_data table (a cohort filtered to the country). Do not apply date range or ordering here; keep one row per date-region entry.

cleaned_daily_confirmed_metrics.name: cleaned_daily_confirmed_metrics
cleaned_daily_confirmed_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical date (already DATE in source). If coming as string elsewhere, CAST would be used.
  CAST(t.date AS DATE) AS date,
  t.country_name AS country_name,
  -- Normalize new_confirmed: ensure numeric and exclude non-numeric / NULL by returning NULL when not numeric.
  -- The source `new_confirmed` in original table is INT64, but may be NULL; additionally accept numeric strings if present in other sources.
  SAFE_CAST(
    -- prefer numeric column if present
    COALESCE(
      -- if coming from a numeric-normalized view this is already numeric; keep as is
      CAST(NULLIF(CAST(t.new_confirmed AS STRING), '') AS NUMERIC),
      -- fall back to cumulative difference if new_confirmed missing and cumulative available in same day and prior day (not computed here)
      NULL
    ) AS INT64
  ) AS new_confirmed,
  -- Normalize cumulative_confirmed similarly: ensure INT64 and expose only non-null numeric values
  SAFE_CAST(
    NULLIF(CAST(t.cumulative_confirmed AS STRING), '') AS INT64
  ) AS cumulative_confirmed
FROM (
  -- prefer already-normalized country_date_numeric_normalized if available, else fall back to country_level_rows, else to raw table
  SELECT date, country_name, new_confirmed, cumulative_confirmed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
) AS t
WHERE
  -- Expose only rows where cumulative_confirmed is a non-null numeric value.
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(CAST(t.cumulative_confirmed AS STRING), '') AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
cleaned_daily_confirmed_metrics.description: Normalize and type-clean the daily confirmed-case metrics: ensure date is a proper date, and canonicalize new_confirmed and cumulative_confirmed to numeric types, exposing only non-null numeric values (do not apply question-specific date bounds here).

daily_growth_rate_per_day.name: daily_growth_rate_per_day
daily_growth_rate_per_day.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  country_name,
  new_confirmed,
  cumulative_confirmed,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(new_confirmed, NULLIF(cumulative_confirmed, 0)) AS growth_rate
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  aggregation_level IS NOT NULL
daily_growth_rate_per_day.description: Compute the growth rate for each date-country row as new_confirmed divided by cumulative_confirmed. This produces one row per date-country with the numeric growth_rate measure; do not limit by date range or top-k here.

country_covid_national_day.name: country_covid_national_day
country_covid_national_day.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_name,
  country_code,
  date,
  aggregation_level,
  cumulative_confirmed
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_open_data.covid19_open_data`
WHERE
  aggregation_level = 0
country_covid_national_day.description: One row per country-date at national aggregation level from the COVID-19 Open Data table, filtered to national-level rows. Does not hard-code any specific date so it can be reused for other dates.

worldbank_country_population.name: worldbank_country_population
worldbank_country_population.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  country AS country_name,
  year_2018
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
WHERE
  country_code IS NOT NULL
worldbank_country_population.description: One row per country containing World Bank population indicators including the 2018 population. Keeps raw year_2018 population value for joins and calculations.

jhu_daily_summary_by_location.name: jhu_daily_summary_by_location
jhu_daily_summary_by_location.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_region,
  province_state,
  admin2,
  date,
  confirmed,
  deaths,
  recovered
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.summary`
WHERE
  country_region IS NOT NULL
  AND date IS NOT NULL
  AND (province_state IS NOT NULL OR admin2 IS NOT NULL)
jhu_daily_summary_by_location.description: All raw rows from the JHU CSSE summary table representing reported COVID-19 counts per reporting location (province/state/admin2) and date, filtered to keep non-null key fields. This is a cleaned subset/cohort of the JHU summary table for later aggregation by country and date.

country_confirmed_by_date.name: country_confirmed_by_date
country_confirmed_by_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_region,
  date,
  SUM(confirmed) AS confirmed_total
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_jhu_csse.summary`
GROUP BY
  country_region,
  date
country_confirmed_by_date.description: Aggregated daily confirmed case totals at the country (country_region) and date level, summing all reporting-location rows (province/state/admin2) from the JHU summary subset. Keeps one row per country and date for use in joins and time-specific filters.

world_bank_population_by_country_clean.name: world_bank_population_by_country_clean
world_bank_population_by_country_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through canonical country and code
  country AS country,
  country_code AS country_code,

  -- normalize year_2019 and year_2018 population columns:
  -- treat NULL or missing values as NULL (consistently); if non-positive treat as NULL
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(year_2019, 0) AS INT64) AS year_2019,
  SAFE_CAST(NULLIF(year_2018, 0) AS INT64) AS year_2018,

  -- source_table_row_id: compose stable identifier from dataset + country_code (keeps view joinable)
  CONCAT('bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country:', COALESCE(country_code, country)) AS source_table_row_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country`
world_bank_population_by_country_clean.description: Canonicalized World Bank population rows per country and country_code with available year population columns. Normalizes country naming, treats missing year columns consistently, and exposes per-row population values for relevant years (e.g., year_2019). This view does not perform cross-row summation; it provides cleaned population rows to be aggregated later.

us_state_and_county_basic_normalized.name: us_state_and_county_basic_normalized
us_state_and_county_basic_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- date: use state date when available; for county rows use county date. Keep as DATE.
  CAST(s.date AS DATE) AS date,
  -- state name standardized from state table when present; for county rows prefer county table's state_name to preserve original row-level value
  COALESCE(c.state_name, s.state_name) AS state_name,
  -- county: use county name from counties table; for state-level rows emit NULL to keep grain consistent (one row per date/state/county) — but requirement is one row per date/state_name/county, so include county from counties table; state rows will have NULL county
  c.county AS county,
  -- carry county_fips_code from county table; states dataset does not have county_fips_code so keep NULL for state-level rows
  c.county_fips_code AS county_fips_code,
  -- confirmed_cases: use county confirmed when present, else state confirmed_cases; cast to INT64
  CAST(COALESCE(c.confirmed_cases, s.confirmed_cases) AS INT64) AS confirmed_cases
FROM
  -- left join counties to states on state_name and date to keep both row types; keep all county rows and all state rows by performing FULL JOIN emulation via UNION ALL is not allowed in single SELECT body, so use RIGHT/LEFT joins and UNION logic avoided — instead produce a combined set by selecting from counties and states with matching keys using FULL OUTER JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states` AS s
FULL OUTER JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties` AS c
ON s.date = c.date AND s.state_name = c.state_name
WHERE
  -- limit to the 50 states + DC by filtering states present in the us_states table (this keeps only those canonical states). Exclude territories by relying on presence in us_states.
  COALESCE(s.state_name, c.state_name) IS NOT NULL
  AND COALESCE(s.state_name, c.state_name) IN (
    'Alabama','Alaska','Arizona','Arkansas','California','Colorado','Connecticut','Delaware',
    'District of Columbia','Florida','Georgia','Hawaii','Idaho','Illinois','Indiana','Iowa',
    'Kansas','Kentucky','Louisiana','Maine','Maryland','Massachusetts','Michigan','Minnesota',
    'Mississippi','Missouri','Montana','Nebraska','Nevada','New Hampshire','New Jersey',
    'New Mexico','New York','North Carolina','North Dakota','Ohio','Oklahoma','Oregon',
    'Pennsylvania','Rhode Island','South Carolina','South Dakota','Tennessee','Texas','Utah',
    'Vermont','Virginia','Washington','West Virginia','Wisconsin','Wyoming'
  )

semantic_filters.state_name: IN (50 US states + District of Columbia)

us_state_and_county_basic_normalized.description: Canonical normalized rows for U.S. states and U.S. counties with consistent column names and types, limited to the 50 U.S. states plus District of Columbia. Standardize state and county identifiers and include date and confirmed_cases as cleaned numeric/date types. Keep one row per source row (no aggregation).

state_daily_new_cases.name: state_daily_new_cases
state_daily_new_cases.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  state_name,
  confirmed_cases,
  LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date) AS previous_date_confirmed_cases,
  confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY state_name ORDER BY date) AS daily_new_cases
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_states`
state_daily_new_cases.description: Per-state, per-date new confirmed COVID-19 cases computed as the difference between confirmed_cases on the date and the previous date for the same state. Only one row per state+date; do not filter out NULL/negative here (filtering applied later).

county_daily_new_cases.name: county_daily_new_cases
county_daily_new_cases.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  state_name,
  county,
  county_fips_code,
  confirmed_cases,
  LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY COALESCE(county_fips_code, CONCAT(state_name, '||', county)) ORDER BY date) AS previous_date_confirmed_cases,
  confirmed_cases - LAG(confirmed_cases) OVER (PARTITION BY COALESCE(county_fips_code, CONCAT(state_name, '||', county)) ORDER BY date) AS daily_new_cases
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_nyt.us_counties`
county_daily_new_cases.description: Per-county (identified by county name and state or county_fips_code if available), per-date new confirmed COVID-19 cases computed as the difference between confirmed_cases on the date and the previous date for the same county. One row per county+date; do not filter out NULL/negative here (filtering applied later).

sub_region_1_weekly_cohort.name: sub_region_1_weekly_cohort
sub_region_1_weekly_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  date,
  country_region,
  country_region_code,
  sub_region_1,
  symptom_anosmia
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_sub_region_1_weekly`
WHERE
  country_region = 'United States'
  AND sub_region_1 IN UNNEST(@sub_region_1_list)
sub_region_1_weekly_cohort.description: Filter the weekly sub-region-1 symptom search table to rows that belong to the United States and to sub-region-1 values of interest; keep original weekly date and symptom columns intact (row-level cohort selection).

country_weekly_symptom_rows.name: country_weekly_symptom_rows
country_weekly_symptom_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_region AS country_region,
  country_region_code AS country_code,
  date AS date,
  symptom_anxiety AS symptom_anxiety,
  symptom_depression AS symptom_depression,
  sub_region_1 AS sub_region_1,
  sub_region_2 AS sub_region_2
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_country_weekly`
WHERE
  -- keep only top-level country rows: no subregions populated
  (IFNULL(sub_region_1, '') = '')
  AND (IFNULL(sub_region_2, '') = '')
country_weekly_symptom_rows.description: Select weekly symptom metric rows at the top-level country granularity (exclude subregions). Keep original weekly date, country identifiers, and symptom fields; do not aggregate. This filters to rows that represent the country (i.e., no sub_region_1 or sub_region_2).

normalize_symptom_values.name: normalize_symptom_values
normalize_symptom_values.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key identifiers
  country_region AS country_region,
  country_region_code AS country_code,
  -- normalize date: prefer YYYY-MM-DD strings or DATE type; keep as STRING for view consistency
  CAST(IFNULL(date,
       NULL) AS STRING) AS date,
  -- Normalize symptom_anxiety:
  -- source columns across tables use different names/types; coerce common string/float patterns to FLOAT64
  -- treat "", "NA", "null", "NULL" as NULL
  SAFE_CAST(
    NULLIF(LOWER(TRIM(IFNULL(
      -- try several likely columns/aliases in source rows; prefer numeric columns if present
      CAST(symptom_anxiety AS STRING),
      '' ))), '') AS FLOAT64) AS symptom_anxiety,
  -- Normalize symptom_depression similarly; note some sources may use 'symptom_depression' naming
  SAFE_CAST(
    NULLIF(LOWER(TRIM(IFNULL(
      CAST(symptom_depression AS STRING),
      '' ))), '') AS FLOAT64) AS symptom_depression
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_country_daily`
normalize_symptom_values.description: Normalize and cast symptom value fields for consistent numeric types and canonical missingness. Produce cleaned numeric symptom_anxiety and symptom_depression and ensure date and country identifiers are present.

period_country_weekly_averages.name: period_country_weekly_averages
period_country_weekly_averages.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_region,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', period_start) AS period_start,
  PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', period_end) AS period_end,
  AVG(CAST(symptom_anxiety AS FLOAT64)) AS avg_anxiety,
  AVG(CAST(symptom_depression AS FLOAT64)) AS avg_depression
FROM (
  SELECT
    country_region,
    -- assumption: weekly source uses ISO week range in `date` like 'YYYY-MM-DD_to_YYYY-MM-DD'
    -- lift date-range parsing out of view by expecting two literals: start/end strings extracted here
    -- try to handle common formats: if `date` is single week-start string, treat as both start and end
    CASE
      WHEN INSTR(date, '_to_') > 0 THEN SPLIT(date, '_to_')[OFFSET(0)]
      WHEN INSTR(date, ' to ') > 0 THEN SPLIT(date, ' to ')[OFFSET(0)]
      ELSE date
    END AS period_start,
    CASE
      WHEN INSTR(date, '_to_') > 0 THEN SPLIT(date, '_to_')[OFFSET(1)]
      WHEN INSTR(date, ' to ') > 0 THEN SPLIT(date, ' to ')[OFFSET(1)]
      ELSE date
    END AS period_end,
    symptom_anxiety,
    symptom_depression
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.covid19_symptom_search.symptom_search_country_weekly`
)
GROUP BY country_region, period_start, period_end
period_country_weekly_averages.description: Aggregate weekly rows into period-level averages of symptom_anxiety and symptom_depression per country and period. Should compute average using available non-null values and produce one row per country_period combination.

vaccine_facility_cohort.name: vaccine_facility_cohort
vaccine_facility_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  facility_place_id,
  facility_sub_region_1,
  facility_sub_region_2,
  facility_sub_region_2_code,
  facility_country_region,
  facility_country_region_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all`
WHERE
  facility_country_region = 'United States'
  AND facility_sub_region_1 IS NOT NULL
  AND facility_sub_region_1 != ''
  AND facility_sub_region_2 IS NOT NULL
  AND facility_sub_region_2 != ''
  AND facility_sub_region_2_code IS NOT NULL
  AND facility_sub_region_2_code != ''
vaccine_facility_cohort.description: Select vaccine facility rows for facilities in the United States and with a defined sub-region 1 (state) and sub-region 2 (county). Keep identifying columns needed for grouping and deduplication (including place id, state, county name, county code, and country).

county_vaccine_site_counts.name: county_vaccine_site_counts
county_vaccine_site_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  vf.facility_sub_region_2 AS facility_sub_region_2,
  vf.facility_sub_region_2_code AS facility_sub_region_2_code,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vf.facility_place_id) AS vaccine_site_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_vaccination_access.facility_boundary_us_all` AS vf
WHERE
  vf.facility_sub_region_2 IS NOT NULL
  AND vf.facility_sub_region_2_code IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  vf.facility_sub_region_2,
  vf.facility_sub_region_2_code
county_vaccine_site_counts.description: Aggregate distinct vaccine facility_place_id counts per county (based on facility_sub_region_2 and facility_sub_region_2_code), producing one row per county name/code with the count of unique sites.

acs_county_population_and_median_age.name: acs_county_population_and_median_age
acs_county_population_and_median_age.body_sql:
SELECT
  geo_id,
  -- county_name and state_name are not provided as separate fields in the ACS table;
  -- the ACS geo_id for counties is like "0500000US{state}{county}". To keep the view reusable
  -- we expose geo_id and leave name parsing outside the view. Here we place NULLs so columns exist.
  NULL AS county_name,
  NULL AS state_name,
  total_pop,
  median_age
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2020_5yr`
acs_county_population_and_median_age.description: One row per county from the 2020 5-year ACS with the county GEOID, county name, state name, total population and median age; does not apply the population > 50000 filter so it can be reused.

usafacts_county_covid_daily.name: usafacts_county_covid_daily
usafacts_county_covid_daily.body_sql:
SELECT
  county_fips_code,
  date,
  confirmed_cases,
  deaths
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.covid19_usafacts.summary`
usafacts_county_covid_daily.description: Daily COVID-19 summary per county from the USAFacts summary table including county_fips_code, date, confirmed_cases, and deaths; no date filter applied so it can be reused for other dates.

zipcode_area_canonicalized.name: zipcode_area_canonicalized
zipcode_area_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- normalize zipcode to 5-digit string (trim, take first 5 if longer)
  SUBSTR(TRIM(zipcode), 1, 5) AS zipcode,
  zipcode_geom,
  CAST(area_land_meters AS INT64) AS area_land_meters,
  CAST(area_water_meters AS INT64) AS area_water_meters,
  CAST(area_land_miles AS FLOAT64) AS area_land_miles,
  CAST(area_water_miles AS FLOAT64) AS area_water_miles,
  CAST(latitude AS FLOAT64) AS latitude,
  CAST(longitude AS FLOAT64) AS longitude,
  state_code,
  state_name,
  city,
  county
FROM `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area`
WHERE zipcode IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(zipcode) != ''
zipcode_area_canonicalized.description: Canonicalized projection of zipcode_area geometries and attributes with normalized zipcode (5-digit), numeric lat/lon, area fields cast to consistent types, and removal of rows with NULL zipcode.

population_by_zip_2010_gender_filtered.name: population_by_zip_2010_gender_filtered
population_by_zip_2010_gender_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode AS zipcode,
  gender AS gender,
  population AS population
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2010'
  AND zipcode IS NOT NULL
  AND gender IN ('male', 'female')
population_by_zip_2010_gender_filtered.description: Rows from 2010 population_by_zip shards filtered to include only records with gender equal to 'male' or 'female' and with non-NULL zipcode, preserving raw population values and zipcode-level identifiers.

zipcode_within_distance_to_point.name: zipcode_within_distance_to_point
zipcode_within_distance_to_point.body_sql:
SELECT
  za.zipcode AS zipcode,
  za.zipcode_geom AS zipcode_geom,
  za.latitude AS latitude,
  za.longitude AS longitude
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area` AS za
WHERE
  -- Lifted literals: :center_latitude, :center_longitude, :distance_meters
  -- Keep rows whose centroid is within the specified distance (meters) of the point.
  ST_DWithin(
    ST_GeogPoint(za.longitude, za.latitude),
    ST_GeogPoint(@center_longitude, @center_latitude),
    @distance_meters
  )
zipcode_within_distance_to_point.description: Subset of zipcode_area rows that are within a configurable distance (meters) of a given geographic point; preserves zipcode and geometry for downstream joins. (This subgoal defines the proximity cohort; the actual point and distance are parameters applied later.)

census_tract_area_membership_zip.name: census_tract_area_membership_zip
census_tract_area_membership_zip.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- census tract geo_id (carry through original id so view is joinable)
  t.geo_id AS geo_id,
  -- ZIP code from ZIP boundary table; prefer exact match between ZCTA geo_id and ZIP code
  z.zip_code AS zip_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.zcta_2019_5yr` AS t
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
ON
  -- Many ACS ZCTA tables use geo_id formatted like '86000US123456' or 'ZCTA5 12345'.
  -- Match by extracting a 5-digit zip substring from the ACS geo_id when present,
  -- otherwise fall back to matching numeric suffixes. This is a best-effort string-based mapping.
  REGEXP_EXTRACT(t.geo_id, r'([0-9]{5})$') = z.zip_code
WHERE
  -- keep only rows where we could determine a 5-digit zip code to form a membership
  REGEXP_EXTRACT(t.geo_id, r'([0-9]{5})$') IS NOT NULL
census_tract_area_membership_zip.description: Mapping of census tracts to ZIP-code areas (ZIP code geography). One row per census tract indicating membership in a ZIP area. This canonical mapping should be used to restrict tracts to those associated with a given ZIP code. If a direct mapping table is unavailable, this relation may be a best-effort derivation using geo_id patterns or an external spatial join.

census_tract_change_metrics_2011_2018.name: census_tract_change_metrics_2011_2018
census_tract_change_metrics_2011_2018.body_sql:
SELECT
  ct.geo_id AS geo_id,
  ct.tract_name AS tract_name,
  -- population and median_income come from the unified per-year table: census_bureau_acs.censustract_YYYY_5yr
  -- lift year literals out of the view (2011 and 2018)
  SAFE_CAST(p2011.total_pop AS FLOAT64) AS population_2011,
  SAFE_CAST(p2018.total_pop AS FLOAT64) AS population_2018,
  SAFE_CAST(p2018.total_pop - p2011.total_pop AS FLOAT64) AS population_absolute_change,
  -- percent change: (2018 - 2011) / NULLIF(2011,0) * 100 ; use NULLIF to avoid div by zero
  CASE
    WHEN p2011.total_pop IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN p2011.total_pop = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE (p2018.total_pop - p2011.total_pop) / NULLIF(p2011.total_pop, 0) * 100
  END AS percent_population_change,
  SAFE_CAST(p2011.median_income AS FLOAT64) AS median_income_2011,
  SAFE_CAST(p2018.median_income AS FLOAT64) AS median_income_2018,
  SAFE_CAST(p2018.median_income - p2011.median_income AS FLOAT64) AS median_income_absolute_change
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2011_5yr` AS p2011
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr` AS p2018
ON p2011.geo_id = p2018.geo_id
-- bring tract name and geo_id from the national census tracts geometry table where available to ensure consistent tract naming
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.us_census_tracts_national` AS ct
ON p2011.geo_id = ct.geo_id
census_tract_change_metrics_2011_2018.description: Per-tract change metrics computed between 2011 and 2018 using population and median income from the unified per-year relation. Produces absolute and percent changes and preserves the original year values. Does not apply final filters or rankings.

census_tract_rankings_within_area.name: census_tract_rankings_within_area
census_tract_rankings_within_area.body_sql:
SELECT
  m.geo_id AS geo_id,
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY z.zip_code ORDER BY m.percent_population_change DESC) AS rank_percent_population_change_2011_2018,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY z.zip_code ORDER BY ABS(m.median_income_absolute_change) DESC) AS rank_median_income_absolute_change_2011_2018
FROM
  `census_tract_change_metrics_2011_2018` AS m
JOIN
  `census_tract_area_membership_zip` AS z
ON
  m.geo_id = z.geo_id
census_tract_rankings_within_area.description: Per-tract ranking metrics computed within a specified spatial cohort (e.g., all tracts mapped to a particular ZIP code). Produces ranks for percent population change (descending) and for absolute median income change (descending). Does not apply top-K cutoffs; it assigns dense ranks or standard ranks as appropriate for later filtering.

zip_codes_within_distance.name: zip_codes_within_distance
zip_codes_within_distance.body_sql:
SELECT
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  z.zip_code_geom AS zip_code_geom
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
WHERE
  -- Lifted literals: use @center_lat, @center_lon (FLOAT) and @distance_meters (FLOAT) as query parameters when selecting from this view.
  -- The view returns zip polygons whose geometries are within @distance_meters of the point at (@center_lon, @center_lat).
  ST_DWithin(
    z.zip_code_geom,
    ST_GEOGPOINT(CAST(@center_lon AS FLOAT64), CAST(@center_lat AS FLOAT64)),
    CAST(@distance_meters AS FLOAT64)
  )
zip_codes_within_distance.description: All ZIP Code polygon rows whose geometries lie within a given distance of an arbitrary point. This selects ZIP Code geometries for later spatial joins.

team_season_records.name: team_season_records

distinct_venues_with_capacity.name: distinct_venues_with_capacity
distinct_venues_with_capacity.body_sql:
SELECT
  venue_name,
  venue_city,
  venue_state,

FROM (
  -- Venues from mbb_pbp_sr
  SELECT

  WHERE venue_capacity IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- Venues from mbb_teams (current teams)
  SELECT
    venue_name,
    venue_city,
    venue_state,
    venue_capacity
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_teams`
  WHERE venue_capacity IS NOT NULL

    venue_name,
    venue_city,
    venue_state,
    venue_capacity
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_teams_games_sr`
  WHERE venue_capacity IS NOT NULL

    venue_name,

    venue_capacity
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_games_sr`
  WHERE venue_capacity IS NOT NULL
)
-- Canonicalize: one row per venue_name + city + state, choose the MAX non-null capacity reported
GROUP BY venue_name, venue_city, venue_state, venue_capacity
HAVING TRUE
distinct_venues_with_capacity.description: All distinct venue records that have a non-null capacity, canonicalizing venue name and location from any table that records venue metadata. One row per unique venue (by name and city/state when available) with its reported capacity and optional location fields.

pbp_shot_events_normalized_coords.name: pbp_shot_events_normalized_coords
pbp_shot_events_normalized_coords.body_sql:
SELECT
  game_id,
  event_id,
  team_id,
  shot_type,
  event_coord_x,
  event_coord_y,
  -- Normalize coordinates so that all shots are represented as if attacking the same basket.
  -- Convention: make adj_x measure distance from the left baseline (in inches) toward the right; 
  -- if team is attacking the opposite basket in that period, reflect x across court width (1128 inches).
  -- Use period to determine sides: assume team attacks "left" basket in odd periods (1,3,5...) and "right" in even periods (2,4,6...).
  CASE
    WHEN event_coord_x IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN MOD(COALESCE(period,1),2) = 1 THEN event_coord_x
    ELSE 1128 - event_coord_x
  END AS adj_x,
  -- For y (distance from top sideline), normalize similarly: keep same orientation (no reflection) but ensure bounds.
  CASE
    WHEN event_coord_y IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN MOD(COALESCE(period,1),2) = 1 THEN event_coord_y
    ELSE event_coord_y
  END AS adj_y,
  -- Normalize shot result into boolean made flag: prefer shot_made field when present; 
  -- fallback: infer from points_scored > 0
  CASE
    WHEN shot_made IS NOT NULL THEN shot_made
    WHEN points_scored IS NOT NULL THEN SAFE_CAST(points_scored AS INT64) > 0
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS shot_made_flag,
  scheduled_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ncaa_basketball.mbb_pbp_sr`
WHERE
  -- Keep only shot events (shot_type not null) to preserve one row per shot event
  shot_type IS NOT NULL
  AND event_id IS NOT NULL
  AND game_id IS NOT NULL
pbp_shot_events_normalized_coords.description: Compute adjusted coordinates for each shot event to a consistent basket side using event_coord_x and event_coord_y logic and normalize shot_result into a boolean made flag. Preserve one row per shot event.

historical_tournament_games_normalized.name: historical_tournament_games_normalized

  CONCAT(CAST(season AS STRING), "-", CAST(round AS STRING), "-", CAST(days_from_epoch AS STRING), "-", win_team_id, "-", lose_team_id) AS historical_game_id,
  season,
  round,
  days_from_epoch,
  game_date,
  day,
  win_market,
  win_seed,
  win_name,
  win_alias,
  win_school_ncaa,

  lose_alias,

FROM

historical_tournament_games_normalized.description: Normalized rows of historical tournament games with both winner and loser fields exposed and canonical date/day/epoch columns. One row per historical tournament game preserving all original win_* and lose_* columns for downstream mapping to a selected market.

markets_top_k.name: markets_top_k
markets_top_k.body_sql:

FROM

WHERE

markets_top_k.description: Ranking of markets by their distinct player counts to support selecting the top markets. Produces one row per market with rank and distinct_player_count for tie-breakable ordering; literal top-k selection is applied later.

feature_engineering_team_metrics.name: feature_engineering_team_metrics
feature_engineering_team_metrics.body_sql:
