feature_engineering_team_metrics.description: One-row-per team season metrics from the feature_engineering table providing pace and efficiency measures (poss_40min, pace_rating, pace_rank, pts_100poss, efficiency_rating, efficiency_rank) keyed by team name and season. Keep original team name as in feature_engineering for later joins (do not canonicalize names here).

team_name_aliases.name: team_name_aliases
team_name_aliases.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
  alias.team_alias AS team_alias
FROM (
  -- canonical school names from tournament seeds and results (school_ncaa)
  SELECT DISTINCT school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2019_tournament_seeds`
  UNION DISTINCT
  SELECT DISTINCT school_ncaa
  FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2018_tournament_results`
) AS s
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([
  -- Lifted literals / identity mapping: map school_ncaa to itself so exact matches are present.
  -- (This keeps the literal out of the view definition in downstream queries.)
  STRUCT(s.school_ncaa AS team_alias)
]) AS alias
UNION DISTINCT
-- include mappings from feature_engineering.team (primary target aliases) to tournament school_ncaa
SELECT
  seeds.school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
  fm.team AS team_alias
FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.2019_tournament_seeds` AS seeds
JOIN `data-to-insights.ncaa.feature_engineering` AS fm
  ON LOWER(TRIM(fm.team)) = LOWER(TRIM(seeds.school_ncaa))
UNION DISTINCT
-- include mappings where mbb_teams.school_ncaa matches tournament school_ncaa and provide mbb_teams.alias/name/market as aliases
SELECT
  t.school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
  t.alias AS team_alias
FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_teams` AS t
WHERE t.school_ncaa IS NOT NULL
UNION DISTINCT
SELECT
  t.school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
  t.name AS team_alias
FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_teams` AS t
WHERE t.school_ncaa IS NOT NULL
UNION DISTINCT
SELECT
  t.school_ncaa AS school_ncaa,
  t.market AS team_alias
FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mbb_teams` AS t
WHERE t.school_ncaa IS NOT NULL
UNION DISTINCT
-- include mascot market/name mappings (market corresponds to school name used elsewhere)
SELECT
  m.market AS school_ncaa,
  m.name AS team_alias
FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mascots` AS m
WHERE m.market IS NOT NULL
UNION DISTINCT
SELECT
  m.market AS school_ncaa,
  m.mascot AS team_alias
FROM `data-to-insights.ncaa.mascots` AS m
WHERE m.market IS NOT NULL
team_name_aliases.description: Mapping of canonical NCAA school names and common aliases/market names to feature_engineering.team values to support robust joins between tournament game school_ncaa and feature_engineering.team. This should include rows for school_ncaa, feature_engineering.team (alias), and any known alternate identifiers from mbb_teams or mascots if available.

qcew_county_month3_construction_by_quart.name: qcew_county_month3_construction_by_quarter_shard

Keep rows at the granularity of a single QCEW row (one row per qcew_area_fips per QCEW shard row). Do not aggregate across time here; this is a row-level cohort of QCEW observations.

allegheny_county_wm_series.name: allegheny_county_wm_series
allegheny_county_wm_series.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.series_id AS series_id,
  s.area_code AS area_code,
  s.series_title AS series_title,
  s.industry_code AS industry_code,
  s.datatype_code AS measure_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bls.wm_series` AS s
WHERE
  -- identify Allegheny County (Pittsburgh area) by area_code.
  -- LIFT county identifier literal out of the view: callers should filter by area_code = <ALLEGHENY_AREA_CODE>.
  -- For reuse, here we include common Allegheny identifiers: area_code for Allegheny County (e.g., 42003)
  s.area_code IN (42003)
  -- include series that represent "all industries" by industry_code = 0 (common BLS convention)
  AND s.industry_code = 0
  -- include series that represent average annual wages: pick datatype_code values that denote average wage measures.
  -- LIFT measure codes out of view: select common wage datatype codes such as 4 (average weekly wage) and 5 (average annual wage) where present.
  AND s.datatype_code IN (4, 5)
allegheny_county_wm_series.description: Select WM series metadata rows that identify series for Allegheny County (Pittsburgh area), including series that represent 'all industries' and average annual wages. This is a reusable cohort of series identifiers for the county and measure type.

wm_yearly_values.name: wm_yearly_values
wm_yearly_values.description: Year-level WM data values per series (one row per series per year) containing the numeric value for that series and year. This provides the yearly value field to compute year-over-year or multi-year changes for any series selected.
counter_examples: Between 1998 and 2017, for Allegheny County in the Pittsburgh area, did the average annual wages for all industries keep pace with the inflation of all consumer items, and what were the respective percentage growth rates (to two decimal places) for wages and the CPI over that period?

cpi_u_all_items_series.name: cpi_u_all_items_series
cpi_u_all_items_series.body_sql:
SELECT
  series_id,
  item_name,
  area_code,
  CONCAT(item_name, ' - ', area_name, IFNULL(CONCAT(' (series ', series_id, ')'), '')) AS series_title
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bls.cpi_u`
WHERE
  -- canonical "All items" CPI-U measure for the U.S.:
  -- item_name equals 'All items' and area_code corresponds to U.S. (area_code '000000' or area_name 'U.S. city average' / 'U.S. all items')
  -- Keep matching flexible to capture common representations; literals lifted out of view would be provided by callers.
  item_name = 'All items'
  AND (
    area_code = '000000'
    OR LOWER(area_name) LIKE '%u.s.%'
    OR LOWER(area_name) LIKE '%united states%'
    OR LOWER(area_name) LIKE '%u.s. city average%'
  )
GROUP BY series_id, item_name, area_code, area_name
cpi_u_all_items_series.description: Select CPI-U series rows that correspond to the 'All items' CPI-U measure for the U.S. (or the canonical CPI-U all-items series). Produces the series identifiers and descriptive fields to choose the correct CPI series.

bls_cpsaat18_industry_year.body_sql:

dar_non_intersectional_representation_ro.name: dar_non_intersectional_representation_rows
dar_non_intersectional_representation_ro.body_sql:
SELECT
  report_year,
  workforce,
  race_asian,
  race_black,
  race_hispanic_latinx,
  race_native_american,
  race_white,
  gender_us_women,
  gender_us_men,
  gender_global_women,
  gender_global_men
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation`
WHERE
  -- Keep rows that represent non-intersectional metrics: exclude any aggregated/category rows that are not demographic groups.
  -- Heuristic: workforce is present and not a NULL/empty label like 'Total' or similar aggregate descriptors.
  workforce IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(workforce) != ''
  -- Exclude rows that appear to be totals/aggregates by checking workforce values commonly used for aggregates.
  AND LOWER(workforce) NOT IN ('total', 'all googlers', 'all', 'company', 'overall', 'google')
dar_non_intersectional_representation_ro.description: Subset of non-intersectional representation rows from the dar_non_intersectional_representation table; keep canonical columns needed for demographic rates and metadata. This filters to rows that represent non-intersectional metrics but does not apply year or workforce-specific filters.

overall_workforce_rows.name: overall_workforce_rows
overall_workforce_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.report_year AS report_year,
  TRIM(r.workforce) AS workforce,
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(r.workforce)) IN ('overall', 'total', 'all googlers', 'all') THEN 'Overall'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(r.workforce)) LIKE '%overall%' THEN 'Overall'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(r.workforce)) LIKE '%total%' THEN 'Overall'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(r.workforce)) LIKE '%all googlers%' THEN 'Overall'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(r.workforce)) LIKE '%all%' AND LOWER(TRIM(r.workforce)) NOT LIKE '%all %' THEN 'Overall'
    ELSE TRIM(r.workforce)
  END AS workforce_canonical,
  r.race_asian AS race_asian,
  r.race_black AS race_black,
  r.race_hispanic_latinx AS race_hispanic_latinx,
  r.race_native_american AS race_native_american,
  r.race_white AS race_white,
  r.gender_us_women AS gender_us_women,
  r.gender_us_men AS gender_us_men,
  r.gender_global_women AS gender_global_women,
  r.gender_global_men AS gender_global_men
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.google_dei.dar_non_intersectional_representation` r
overall_workforce_rows.description: Normalize and canonicalize the workforce label to identify the single row representing the overall workforce. Standardize casing/trim whitespace and produce an explicit flag or canonical workforce value 'Overall' for rows that denote the whole company. Do not restrict years here.

overall_workforce_years_filter.name: overall_workforce_years_filter
overall_workforce_years_filter.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(report_year AS INT64) AS report_year,
  workforce_canonical AS workforce_canonical,
  race_asian AS race_asian,
  race_black AS race_black,
  race_hispanic_latinx AS race_hispanic_latinx,
  race_native_american AS race_native_american,
  race_white AS race_white,
  gender_us_women AS gender_us_women,
  gender_us_men AS gender_us_men,
  gender_global_women AS gender_global_women,
  gender_global_men AS gender_global_men
FROM `overall_workforce_rows`
WHERE report_year IN (2014, 2024)
  AND race_asian IS NOT NULL
  AND race_black IS NOT NULL
  AND race_hispanic_latinx IS NOT NULL
  AND race_native_american IS NOT NULL
  AND race_white IS NOT NULL
  AND gender_us_women IS NOT NULL
  AND gender_us_men IS NOT NULL
  AND gender_global_women IS NOT NULL
  AND gender_global_men IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  report_year,
  workforce_canonical,
  race_asian,
  race_black,
  race_hispanic_latinx,
  race_native_american,
  race_white,
  gender_us_women,
  gender_us_men,
  gender_global_women,
  gender_global_men
overall_workforce_years_filter.description: Filter the normalized overall workforce rows to the two report_years of interest (2014 and 2024) and exclude rows where demographic values are NULL. Produce one row per report_year with all demographic columns present.

taxi_trip_base_rows.name: taxi_trip_base_rows
taxi_trip_base_rows.body_sql:

  unique_key AS trip_id,
  trip_seconds,
  fare
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
WHERE

  AND trip_seconds IS NOT NULL

taxi_trip_base_rows.description: One row per taxi trip from the taxi_trips table with basic null-filtering on key measurement columns; keeps raw trip_seconds and fare for downstream processing.

taxi_trip_duration_minutes.name: taxi_trip_duration_minutes
taxi_trip_duration_minutes.body_sql:
SELECT
  /* key/id column carried through */
  t.trip_id,
  /* original seconds as provided */
  t.trip_seconds,
  /* normalized duration in minutes (numeric), allow NULL if trip_seconds is NULL */
  SAFE_CAST(t.trip_seconds AS NUMERIC) / 60.0 AS duration_minutes,
  /* boolean flag whether duration is within 0..3600 seconds inclusive; NULL if trip_seconds is NULL */
  CASE
    WHEN t.trip_seconds IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN t.trip_seconds BETWEEN 0 AND 3600 THEN TRUE
    ELSE FALSE
  END AS within_0_3600_seconds
FROM
  /* prefer existing base view if available; otherwise read directly from table */
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips` AS raw
JOIN
  (
    -- Derive trip_id and trip_seconds in a stable way to match expected grain.
    -- If taxi_trip_base_rows view is present in the environment, it can be used instead.
    SELECT
      unique_key AS trip_id,
      trip_seconds
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
  ) AS t
ON raw.unique_key = t.trip_id
taxi_trip_duration_minutes.description: Normalized taxi trip rows with trip duration converted to minutes (numeric) and a boolean flag for whether the duration is within the valid study range (0 to 3600 seconds). Does not apply the range filter as a hard exclusion so the normalized duration can be reused.

trips_2018_cleaned.name: trips_2018_cleaned
trips_2018_cleaned.body_sql:
SELECT
  TRIM(t.company) AS company,
  t.trip_start_timestamp,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', t.trip_start_timestamp) AS trip_month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips` AS t
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM t.trip_start_timestamp) = 2018
  AND t.company IS NOT NULL
grain: /* row-level grain: original table primary key(s) unknown; use full row as grain */
trips_2018_cleaned.description: All taxi trips that started in the 2018 calendar year with NULL companies removed and normalized company strings (trimmed). Includes a derived month label (YYYY-MM) extracted from the trip start timestamp.

company_monthly_trip_counts.name: company_monthly_trip_counts
company_monthly_trip_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  company AS company,
  -- canonical month identifier as DATE (first day of month)
  DATE_TRUNC(DATE(trip_start_timestamp), MONTH) AS trip_month,
  COUNT(1) AS trip_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.chicago_taxi_trips.taxi_trips`
GROUP BY
  company,
  trip_month
company_monthly_trip_counts.description: Monthly trip counts per company (calendar month), one row per company and month. Counts trips in that company and month.

company_monthly_consecutive_deltas.name: company_monthly_consecutive_deltas
company_monthly_consecutive_deltas.body_sql:
SELECT
  cmtc.company AS company,
  -- month_start is the first day of the current month (DATE)
  DATE_TRUNC(cmtc.trip_month, MONTH) AS month_start,
  -- month_end is the first day of the next calendar month
  DATE_ADD(DATE_TRUNC(cmtc.trip_month, MONTH), INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS month_end,
  cmtc.trip_count AS trip_count_start,
  -- lookup next month's trip_count from same aggregated source
  COALESCE(next_cmtc.trip_count, 0) AS trip_count_end,
  COALESCE(next_cmtc.trip_count, 0) - cmtc.trip_count AS trip_count_increase
FROM
  -- use existing monthly counts as the base
  `company_monthly_trip_counts` AS cmtc
LEFT JOIN
  `company_monthly_trip_counts` AS next_cmtc
ON
  cmtc.company = next_cmtc.company
  AND DATE_TRUNC(next_cmtc.trip_month, MONTH) = DATE_ADD(DATE_TRUNC(cmtc.trip_month, MONTH), INTERVAL 1 MONTH)
WHERE
  -- keep only rows where a next-month exists (per spec: "for which a next-month exists")
  next_cmtc.company IS NOT NULL
company_monthly_consecutive_deltas.description: For each company and month, compute the next calendar month's trip count and the month pair (current and next). Produces one row per company and starting month for which a next-month exists, with the increase (next - current).

crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows.name: crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows
crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows.body_sql:
SELECT

FROM

WHERE

crime_motor_vehicle_theft_rows.description: Subset of crime incidents that are motor vehicle thefts. Keeps one row per crime incident and preserves the original columns for further processing.

crime_incident_month_normalized.name: crime_incident_month_normalized
crime_incident_month_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(unique_key AS STRING) AS id,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM date) AS month
FROM `bigquery-public-data.chicago_crime.crime`
crime_incident_month_normalized.description: Normalized projection that extracts calendar year and month from the incident timestamp and keeps relevant identifying columns. One row per crime incident.

motor_vehicle_theft_incident_month.name: motor_vehicle_theft_incident_month
motor_vehicle_theft_incident_month.body_sql:
SELECT

  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.date) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM c.date) AS month
FROM

ON

motor_vehicle_theft_incident_month.description: Join of motor vehicle theft rows with their normalized year/month to produce one row per theft incident annotated with its incident year and month.

incidents_per_month.name: incidents_per_month
incidents_per_month.body_sql:
SELECT

incidents_per_month.description: Count of incidents per calendar year and month. One row per (year, month) with the incident_count metric.

crime_motor_vehicle_theft_events.name: crime_motor_vehicle_theft_events
crime_motor_vehicle_theft_events.body_sql:
SELECT

WHERE LOWER(c.primary_type) = 'motor vehicle theft'
crime_motor_vehicle_theft_events.description: One-row-per crime event filtered to motor vehicle theft incidents. Keeps original event-level columns for downstream grouping and date extraction.

crime_event_date_normalized.name: crime_event_date_normalized
crime_event_date_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(unique_key AS STRING) AS id,
  date AS date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,

FROM

crime_event_date_normalized.description: Normalize/parse the event timestamp/date column into canonical year and month integer columns for calendar grouping.

monthly_crime_counts_per_type.name: monthly_crime_counts_per_type
monthly_crime_counts_per_type.body_sql:
SELECT

trade_base_rows.name: trade_base_rows
trade_base_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  TradeReportID AS trade_id,
  -- pull primary Side if available (first element of Sides array), else NULL
  (SELECT s.Side FROM UNNEST(Sides) AS s LIMIT 1) AS Side,
  -- strategy is not present in source; lift out as NULL placeholder for downstream filtering/joins
  NULL AS strategy,
  -- intrinsic_value derived as LastPx - StrikePrice when both present; NULL otherwise
  CASE
    WHEN LastPx IS NOT NULL AND StrikePrice IS NOT NULL THEN LastPx - StrikePrice
    ELSE NULL
  END AS intrinsic_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`
WHERE
  -- require a trade identifier and a non-null transaction time to filter out invalid rows
  TradeReportID IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(TradeReportID) != ''
  AND TransactTime IS NOT NULL
trade_base_rows.description: One row per trade from the raw trade_capture_report table; filters out obviously invalid or unusable rows (e.g., rows lacking a trade identifier). This produces the base cohort of trades to be further normalized and aggregated.

raw_trade_reports.name: raw_trade_reports
raw_trade_reports.body_sql:
SELECT
  TradeReportID AS TradeReportID,
  MaturityDate AS MaturityDate,
  TargetCompID AS TargetCompID,
  Symbol AS Symbol,
  LastPx AS LastPx,
  StrikePrice AS StrikePrice,
  Sides AS Sides
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report`
WHERE
  StrikePrice IS NOT NULL
  AND TradeReportID IS NOT NULL
raw_trade_reports.description: Row-level subset of trade_capture_report containing only native rows needed for downstream processing; filters out rows that are logically invalid for price-based analysis (e.g., where StrikePrice is NULL). Does not perform projections beyond selecting necessary columns.

unnested_sides.name: unnested_sides
unnested_sides.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key/id columns from source so view stays joinable
  t.TradeReportID AS TradeReportID,
  t.MaturityDate AS MaturityDate,
  t.TargetCompID AS TargetCompID,
  t.Symbol AS Symbol,
  t.LastPx AS LastPx,
  t.StrikePrice AS StrikePrice,
  s.Side AS Side
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` AS t,
  UNNEST(t.Sides) AS s
unnested_sides.description: Explode/unnest the Sides array from trade_capture_report so there is one row per trade report per side element, preserving the parent trade identifiers and relevant price/timestamp fields.

canonical_trade_fields.name: canonical_trade_fields
canonical_trade_fields.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry a key/id column from source to keep joinable
  CAST(r.TradeReportID AS STRING) AS TradeReportID,
  -- canonical trade timestamp from MaturityDate if available, else NULL
  SAFE_CAST(r.MaturityDate AS TIMESTAMP) AS tradeTimestamp,
  -- derive algorithm name from first 4 chars of TargetCompID with canonical mappings
  CASE SUBSTR(COALESCE(r.TargetCompID, ''), 1, 4)
    WHEN 'MOMO' THEN 'Momentum'
    WHEN 'LUCK' THEN 'Feeling Lucky'
    WHEN 'PRED' THEN 'Prediction'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS algorithm,
  -- symbol passed through
  r.Symbol AS Symbol,
  -- openPrice = LastPx cast to FLOAT64 (NULL-safe)
  SAFE_CAST(r.LastPx AS FLOAT64) AS openPrice,
  -- closePrice = StrikePrice cast to FLOAT64 (NULL-safe)
  SAFE_CAST(r.StrikePrice AS FLOAT64) AS closePrice,
  -- normalize Side to canonical tradeDirection values; operate at side level using unnested_sides if present
  CASE UPPER(s.Side)
    WHEN 'LONG' THEN 'LONG'
    WHEN 'SHORT' THEN 'SHORT'
    WHEN 'BUY' THEN 'LONG'
    WHEN 'SELL' THEN 'SHORT'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS tradeDirection
FROM
  -- prefer unnested_sides view which provides one row per side; fallback to raw_trade_reports if unnested not available
  `bigquery-public-data.cymbal_investments.trade_capture_report` AS raw
LEFT JOIN
  UNNEST(raw.Sides) AS s
-- use raw as r alias for fields not in unnested subrows
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([STRUCT(
  raw.TradeReportID AS TradeReportID,
  raw.MaturityDate AS MaturityDate,
  raw.TargetCompID AS TargetCompID,
  raw.Symbol AS Symbol,
  raw.LastPx AS LastPx,
  raw.StrikePrice AS StrikePrice
)]) AS r
canonical_trade_fields.description: Normalize and canonicalize fields needed for final output: cast LastPx and StrikePrice to floats, MaturityDate to TIMESTAMP, derive algorithm name from the first four characters of TargetCompID with canonical mappings ('MOMO'->'Momentum', 'LUCK'->'Feeling Lucky', 'PRED'->'Prediction'), and normalize Side value to a canonical tradeDirection string (e.g., 'LONG' or 'SHORT' or NULL). Does not apply final sorting/limit.

latest_evaluation_group_per_state_with_e.name: latest_evaluation_group_per_state_with_expcurr
latest_evaluation_group_per_state_with_e.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key/id columns so view stays joinable
  peg.evaluation_group_sequence_number AS population_evaluation_group_id,
  peg.state_code AS state_code,
  peg.evaluation_group AS evaluation_group_sequence_number,
  -- pack the requested group columns into a STRUCT-like JSON string column (name per spec)
  TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(
    peg.evaluation_group AS evaluation_group,
    peg.evaluation_group_description AS evaluation_group_description,
    peg.state_code AS state_code,
    peg.notes AS notes,
    peg.pop_evaluation_group_created_by AS pop_evaluation_group_created_by,
    peg.pop_evaluation_group_created_date AS pop_evaluation_group_created_date,
    peg.pop_evaluation_group_created_in_instance AS pop_evaluation_group_created_in_instance,
    peg.pop_evaluation_group_modified_by AS pop_evaluation_group_modified_by,
    peg.pop_evaluation_group_modified_date AS pop_evaluation_group_modified_date,
    peg.pop_evaluation_group_modified_in_instance AS pop_evaluation_group_modified_in_instance
  )) AS population_evaluation_group_estate_cols
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_group` AS peg
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation` AS pe
ON
  peg.evaluation_group_sequence_number = pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number
  AND peg.region_or_station_code = pe.region_or_station_code
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` AS pet
ON
  pe.evaluation_sequence_number = pet.evaluation_sequence_number
  AND pet.evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'
WHERE
  -- restrict to only the latest evaluation_group_sequence_number per state among groups that have EXPCURR
  peg.evaluation_group_sequence_number = (
    SELECT ARRAY_AGG(p2.evaluation_group_sequence_number ORDER BY p2.evaluation_group_sequence_number DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)]
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_group` AS p2
    WHERE p2.state_code = peg.state_code
      AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation` AS pe2
        JOIN `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` AS pet2
        ON pe2.evaluation_sequence_number = pet2.evaluation_sequence_number
        WHERE pe2.evaluation_group_sequence_number = p2.evaluation_group_sequence_number
          AND pet2.evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'
      )
  )
latest_evaluation_group_per_state_with_e.description: For each state (population_evaluation_group.state_code) produce the latest population_evaluation_group row by evaluation_group_sequence_number, but only consider groups that have at least one linked population_evaluation -> population_evaluation_type with evaluation_type = 'EXPCURR'. This yields one candidate evaluation_group per state (the latest qualifying group).

population_evaluations_2012.name: population_evaluations_2012
population_evaluations_2012.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(pe.evaluation_sequence_number AS STRING) AS evaluation_uid,
  CAST(pet.evaluation_type_sequence_number AS STRING) AS population_evaluation_type_uid,
  pe.evaluation_description AS evaluation_description,
  p.inventory_year AS inventory_year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation` AS pe
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population` AS p
ON
  pe.evaluation_sequence_number = p.evaluation_sequence_number
  AND pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number = p.evaluation_group_sequence_number
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` AS pet
ON
  pet.evaluation_sequence_number = pe.evaluation_sequence_number
  AND pet.evaluation_group_sequence_number = pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number
WHERE
  p.inventory_year = 2012
GROUP BY
  pe.evaluation_sequence_number,
  pet.evaluation_type_sequence_number,
  pe.evaluation_description,
  p.inventory_year
population_evaluations_2012.description: All population_evaluation rows that belong to inventory year 2012; one row per population_evaluation.

evaluation_groups.name: evaluation_groups
evaluation_groups.body_sql:
SELECT
  peg.evaluation_group AS evaluation_group,
  -- carry the group's primary id as the view grain
  CAST(peg.evaluation_group_sequence_number AS STRING) AS population_evaluation_group_uid,
  peg.state_code AS state_code,
  -- bring in a representative population_evaluation_type uid (may be NULL if none)
  CAST(pet.evaluation_type_sequence_number AS STRING) AS population_evaluation_type_uid,
  peg.evaluation_group_description AS evaluation_group_description
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_group` AS peg
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation` AS pe
ON
  pe.evaluation_group_sequence_number = peg.evaluation_group_sequence_number
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population_evaluation_type` AS pet
ON
  pet.evaluation_group_sequence_number = peg.evaluation_group_sequence_number
  AND pet.evaluation_sequence_number = pe.evaluation_sequence_number
GROUP BY
  peg.evaluation_group,
  peg.evaluation_group_sequence_number,
  peg.state_code,
  pet.evaluation_type_sequence_number,
  peg.evaluation_group_description
evaluation_groups.description: Population evaluation groups (metadata) joined to their evaluations and evaluation types; one row per population_evaluation_group.

population_base.name: population_base
population_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(CONCAT(CAST(stratum_assign_sequence_number AS STRING), '_', CAST(COALESCE(phase_2_plot_number, plot_sequence_number) AS STRING)) AS STRING) AS population_id,
  inventory_year AS inventory_year,
  COALESCE(inventory_year, NULL) AS year,
  expansion_factor AS expansion_factor,
  adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot AS adjustment_factor_for_the_subplot,
  adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot AS adjustment_factor_for_the_macroplot,
  evaluation_type AS evaluation_type,
  stratum_sequence_number AS stratum_sequence_number,
  COALESCE(phase_2_plot_number, plot_sequence_number) AS plot_sequence_number,
  CAST(estimation_unit_sequence_number AS STRING) AS population_estimation_unit_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usfs_fia.population`
population_base.description: Row-level population records with canonical year and essential population fields; keep one row per population record (no aggregates). Does basic canonicalization of year using inventory_year when present.

sternaparadisaea_northern_occurrences.name: sternaparadisaea_northern_occurrences
sternaparadisaea_northern_occurrences.body_sql:
SELECT
  gbifid,
  eventdate,
  decimallatitude,
  year,
  month,
  species
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
WHERE
  species = 'Sterna paradisaea'
  AND decimallatitude > 40
sternaparadisaea_northern_occurrences.description: Subset of occurrences restricted to records of species 'Sterna paradisaea' and with decimallatitude > 40. Keeps original occurrence rows for later per-date and per-year aggregation.

occurrence_date_parts.name: occurrence_date_parts
occurrence_date_parts.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.gbifid,
  o.eventdate,
  DATE(o.eventdate) AS event_date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.eventdate) AS year,
  EXTRACT(MONTH FROM o.eventdate) AS month,
  o.decimallatitude
FROM `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences` AS o
occurrence_date_parts.description: Normalized occurrence rows with explicit extracted date parts and a canonical date (date-only) column derived from eventdate to enable grouping by calendar date and year/month-based filtering.

first_qualifying_date_per_year.name: first_qualifying_date_per_year
first_qualifying_date_per_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  MIN(eventdate) AS first_event_date,
  COUNT(1) AS daily_count
FROM (
  -- aggregate occurrences to calendar-day level per year
  SELECT
    year,
    DATE(eventdate) AS event_date_day,
    ANY_VALUE(eventdate) AS eventdate  -- preserve a representative TIMESTAMP for the day
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.gbif.occurrences`
  WHERE year IS NOT NULL
    AND eventdate IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY year, DATE(eventdate)
)
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year
first_qualifying_date_per_year.description: For each year, find the earliest calendar date (event_date) in that year that meets a yet-to-be-applied threshold on daily_count. Produces one candidate row per year with that first qualifying date and its count (threshold filter applied later).

us_states_geometries.name: us_states_geometries
us_states_geometries.body_sql:
SELECT
  geo_id AS state_id,
  state_name AS state_name,
  state_geom AS state_geom
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.states`
us_states_geometries.description: One row per U.S. state with its geometry for spatial containment tests.

na_hurricane_points.name: na_hurricane_points
na_hurricane_points.body_sql:
SELECT
  sid AS storm_id,
  name,
  basin,
  latitude,
  longitude,
  wmo_wind,
  iso_time AS obs_time
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.noaa_hurricanes.hurricanes`
WHERE
  basin = 'NA'
  AND COALESCE(name, '') != ''
  AND latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND longitude IS NOT NULL
  AND wmo_wind IS NOT NULL
na_hurricane_points.description: One row per recorded hurricane observation point in the North Atlantic basin with position and wind-speed, excluding unnamed placeholder records; keeps raw point lat/lon and wind value for spatial/counting.

port_state_membership.name: port_state_membership
port_state_membership.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.index_number AS index_number,
  s.state_id AS state_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_international_ports.world_port_index` AS p
JOIN
  `us_states_geometries` AS s
ON
  ST_CONTAINS(s.state_geom, ST_GEOGPOINT(p.port_longitude, p.port_latitude))
WHERE
  p.port_latitude IS NOT NULL
  AND p.port_longitude IS NOT NULL
port_state_membership.description: Spatial join indicating which ports (from ports_with_valid_geometry) lie within which U.S. states (from us_states_geometries); one row per port-state containment relationship.

postal_code_region_rows_clean.name: postal_code_region_rows_clean
postal_code_region_rows_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  region_name AS postal_code,
  state_name,
  COALESCE(count_qualified, 0) AS count_qualified,
  percent_covered, -- preserve NULLs per spec
  percent_qualified, -- preserve NULLs per spec
  COALESCE(number_of_panels_total, 0) AS number_of_panels_total,
  COALESCE(kw_total, 0) AS kw_total,
  COALESCE(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total, 0) AS yearly_sunlight_kwh_total,
  COALESCE(carbon_offset_metric_tons, 0) AS carbon_offset_metric_tons,
  COALESCE(existing_installs_count, 0) AS existing_installs_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`
WHERE
  state_name IS NOT NULL
postal_code_region_rows_clean.description: Canonical cleaned rows from the solar_potential_by_postal_code table: keep only rows with a non-NULL state_name and coerce NULL numeric metrics to 0 and NULL percent fields to NULL (preserve for explicit handling later). This produces one row per postal_code region.

census_tract_region_rows_clean.name: census_tract_region_rows_clean
census_tract_region_rows_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  region_name AS census_tract_id,
  state_name,
  COALESCE(count_qualified, 0) AS count_qualified,
  -- percent fields: preserve NULLs (do not coerce)
  percent_covered,
  percent_qualified,
  COALESCE(number_of_panels_total, 0) AS number_of_panels_total,
  COALESCE(kw_total, 0) AS kw_total,
  COALESCE(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total, 0) AS yearly_sunlight_kwh_total,
  COALESCE(carbon_offset_metric_tons, 0) AS carbon_offset_metric_tons,
  COALESCE(existing_installs_count, 0) AS existing_installs_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
WHERE
  state_name IS NOT NULL
census_tract_region_rows_clean.description: Canonical cleaned rows from the solar_potential_by_censustract table: keep only rows with a non-NULL state_name and coerce NULL numeric metrics to 0 and NULL percent fields to NULL (preserve for explicit handling later). This produces one row per census tract region.

state_level_aggregates_per_source.name: state_level_aggregates_per_source
state_level_aggregates_per_source.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_name,
  source_table,
  SUM(IFNULL(count_qualified, 0)) AS total_buildings_qualified,
  -- average percent_covered: NULL-safe arithmetic mean over rows (exclude NULLs from denominator)
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN percent_covered IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(IFNULL(percent_covered, 0)), SUM(CASE WHEN percent_covered IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))
  END AS avg_percent_covered,
  -- average percent_qualified: NULL-safe arithmetic mean over rows (exclude NULLs from denominator)
  CASE
    WHEN SUM(CASE WHEN percent_qualified IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(IFNULL(percent_qualified, 0)), SUM(CASE WHEN percent_qualified IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END))
  END AS avg_percent_qualified,
  SUM(IFNULL(number_of_panels_total, 0)) AS total_number_of_panels,
  SUM(IFNULL(kw_total, 0)) AS total_kw_capacity,
  SUM(IFNULL(yearly_sunlight_kwh_total, 0)) AS total_yearly_sunlight_kwh,
  SUM(IFNULL(carbon_offset_metric_tons, 0)) AS total_carbon_offset_metric_tons,
  SUM(IFNULL(existing_installs_count, 0)) AS total_existing_installs,
  -- estimated_potential_installations_adjusted:
  -- interpret as total_buildings_qualified * avg_percent_covered (treat NULL percent_covered as 0 for multiplication use)
  -- then multiply by avg_percent_qualified (treat NULL percent_qualified as 0 for multiplication use)
  -- Use total_buildings_qualified computed as SUM(IFNULL(count_qualified,0))
  (
    SUM(IFNULL(count_qualified, 0))
    * COALESCE(
        -- for multiplication uses, treat NULL percents as 0
        (SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(IFNULL(percent_covered, 0)), NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN percent_covered IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0))),
        0
      )
    * COALESCE(
        (SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(IFNULL(percent_qualified, 0)), NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN percent_qualified IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0))),
        0
      )
  ) AS estimated_potential_installations_adjusted,
  -- gap_in_potential_installations = estimated_potential_installations_adjusted - total_existing_installs (floor at 0)
  GREATEST(
    0,
    (
      SUM(IFNULL(count_qualified, 0))
      * COALESCE((SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(IFNULL(percent_covered, 0)), NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN percent_covered IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0))), 0)
      * COALESCE((SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(IFNULL(percent_qualified, 0)), NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN percent_qualified IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0))), 0)
    )
    - SUM(IFNULL(existing_installs_count, 0))
  ) AS gap_in_potential_installations,
  COUNT(1) AS region_count
FROM (
  -- postal_code source rows
  SELECT
    state_name,
    count_qualified,
    percent_covered,
    percent_qualified,
    number_of_panels_total,
    kw_total,
    yearly_sunlight_kwh_total,
    carbon_offset_metric_tons,
    existing_installs_count,
    'postal_code' AS source_table
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_postal_code`

  UNION ALL

  -- census_tract source rows
  SELECT
    state_name,
    count_qualified,
    percent_covered,
    percent_qualified,
    number_of_panels_total,
    kw_total,
    yearly_sunlight_kwh_total,
    carbon_offset_metric_tons,
    existing_installs_count,
    'census_tract' AS source_table
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.sunroof_solar.solar_potential_by_censustract`
)
GROUP BY state_name, source_table
state_level_aggregates_per_source.description: Aggregate per state and per source table (postal_code vs census_tract). Sums treat NULL numeric metric values as 0; averages of percent_covered and percent_qualified are simple (NULL-safe) arithmetic means computed over all regions in the state for that source, treating NULL percent values as 0 when used in multiplicative formulas but excluding them from the simple-average denominator per the caller's instruction to be NULL-safe (i.e., average over rows treating NULL percent as 0 for multiplication-only uses and treating NULL as 0 for sum inputs). This view produces one row per (state_name, source_table).

region_variant_aggregates.name: region_variant_aggregates
region_variant_aggregates.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- grouping key: region identifier supplied by the query using this view
  region_id,
  -- carry region boundaries through (lifted literals should be provided by caller)
  MIN(region_start) AS region_start,
  MIN(region_end) AS region_end,
  -- per-region aggregated measures over the underlying variant rows
  COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(reference_name,':', CAST(start_position AS STRING),':', reference_bases)) AS variant_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(allele_count,0)) AS total_allele_count,
  SUM(IFNULL(allele_number,0)) AS total_allele_number,
  ARRAY_AGG(DISTINCT gene_symbol IGNORE NULLS) AS distinct_gene_symbols
FROM (
  -- The caller should replace this subselect with the actual variant-level source,
  -- supplying region_id, region_start, region_end for each variant row.
  -- Example sources in this dataset include:
  --   `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v3_genomes__chr*`  (use _TABLE_SUFFIX filter to restrict shards)
  --   `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v2_1_1_genomes__chr*`
  --   `bigquery-public-data.gnomAD.v2_1_1_exomes__chr*`
  --
  -- Required columns for the aggregation below:
  --   region_id            -- grouping id for the region (STRING or INT)
  --   region_start         -- region start boundary (INT)
  --   region_end           -- region end boundary (INT)
  --   reference_name       -- contig/chromosome (STRING)
  --   start_position       -- variant start (INT)
  --   reference_bases      -- reference allele (STRING)
  --   allele_count         -- allele count at variant (INT)
  --   allele_number        -- allele number at variant (INT)
  --   gene_symbol          -- a gene symbol string (may be NULL)
  SELECT
    -- These columns must be provided by the caller; here they are placeholders.
    region_id,
    region_start,
    region_end,
    reference_name,
    start_position,
    reference_bases,
    allele_count,
    allele_number,
    gene_symbol
  FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(
    -- placeholders; in real use replace this UNNEST with real table scan
    NULL AS region_id,
    NULL AS region_start,
    NULL AS region_end,
    NULL AS reference_name,
    NULL AS start_position,
    NULL AS reference_bases,
    NULL AS allele_count,
    NULL AS allele_number,
    NULL AS gene_symbol
  )])
) AS variants
GROUP BY region_id
region_variant_aggregates.description: Aggregate measures per queried region (one row per region) computed from a set of variant rows: distinct variant count, sum of allele_count, sum of allele_number, and set/list of distinct gene symbols. This is a grouped aggregation over the variant-level inputs; region boundaries (region_id or start/end) are grouping keys.

accident_rows_sharded.name: accident_rows_sharded
accident_rows_sharded.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(state_number AS STRING), '-', CAST(consecutive_number AS STRING)) AS st_case,
  state_number,
  state_name,
  consecutive_number,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2016'
accident_rows_sharded.description: Accident records from the NHTSA accident shard tables for 2015–2016 retaining keys and state identifiers needed to deduplicate accidents and join to distraction rows.

state_population_2010_by_zip_agg.name: state_population_2010_by_zip_agg
state_population_2010_by_zip_agg.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.state_name AS state_name,
  s.state_abbreviation AS state_code,
  s.state_fips_code AS state_fips_code,
  SUM(p.population) AS state_population_2010
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.zipcode_area` z
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.utility_us.us_states_area` s
ON
  z.state_code = s.state_abbreviation
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_*` p
ON
  z.zipcode = p.zipcode
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2010'
GROUP BY
  s.state_name,
  s.state_abbreviation,
  s.state_fips_code
state_population_2010_by_zip_agg.description: State-level total population computed from 2010 ZIP-level population shard by mapping ZIPs to their state and summing 2010 population per state. Keeps state identifiers suitable for joining to accident/distract state (state_name or state_code/FIPS).

accident_core.name: accident_core
accident_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number,
  consecutive_number,
  year_of_crash,
  month_of_crash,
  CONCAT(CAST(state_number AS STRING), '-', CAST(consecutive_number AS STRING)) AS accident_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2020'
accident_core.description: One row per accident from the accidents table, providing accident identifiers and core accident date fields. This selects accident-level records (no year/month literals here) so downstream steps can filter by shard/year/month.

person_core.name: person_core
person_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number,
  consecutive_number,
  person_number,
  injury_severity
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.person_*`
person_core.description: One row per person from the persons table, providing person identifiers, injury severity, and the accident identifiers needed to join to accidents. Does not apply year-specific filtering here so it can be reused across shards.

accident_cohort_criteria.name: accident_cohort_criteria
accident_cohort_criteria.body_sql:
SELECT
  state_number,
  consecutive_number,
  year_of_crash,
  month_of_crash
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_*`
-- Note: keep year/month bounds as parameters when using this view.
-- Typical usage should add a _TABLE_SUFFIX filter, e.g.
-- WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2020'
-- and optional predicates to require valid year/month values, e.g.
-- WHERE year_of_crash IS NOT NULL AND month_of_crash BETWEEN 1 AND 12
accident_cohort_criteria.description: A reusable accident-level cohort applying common accident filters (year and month bounds are intentionally left as parameters when used). This rowset represents accidents that meet typical crash-level predicates (e.g., has valid date fields) and exposes fields for applying shard/year/month filters downstream.

person_injury_flags.name: person_injury_flags
person_injury_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(CAST(p.state_number AS STRING), '-', CAST(p.consecutive_number AS STRING)) AS accident_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_number) AS persons_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN p.injury_severity = 4 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS fatal_injury_count,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT p.person_number) > 1 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS multiple_persons_flag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.person_*` AS p
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2016'
GROUP BY
  accident_id
person_injury_flags.description: Per-accident aggregated person-level injury counts and a flag indicating whether the accident involves more than one distinct person. Also compute count of fatal injuries (injury severity code == 4) per accident and total distinct persons per accident.

accident_core_2015.name: accident_core_2015
accident_core_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.state_number AS state_number,
  a.consecutive_number AS consecutive_number,
  a.county AS county,
  a.relation_to_junction_specific_location_name AS type_of_intersection,
  a.atmospheric_conditions_1 AS atmospheric_conditions_1,
  a.functional_system AS functional_system,
  a.related_factors_crash_level_1 AS related_factors_crash_level_1,
  a.hour_of_crash AS hour_of_crash_accident
FROM `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_*` AS a
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX = '2015'
  AND a.state_number IS NOT NULL
  AND a.consecutive_number IS NOT NULL
accident_core_2015.description: One-row-per-accident core accident fields for year 2015 (canonical accident-level attributes used across outputs).

ems_and_scene_times_2015.name: ems_and_scene_times_2015
ems_and_scene_times_2015.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.state_number,
  a.consecutive_number,
  -- keep raw hour fields (as provided) for validation downstream
  -- EMS arrival at hospital hour (as-is from accident table if present)
  SAFE_CAST(a.hour_of_ems_arrival_at_hospital AS INT64) AS hour_of_ems_arrival_at_hospital,
  SAFE_CAST(a.hour_of_arrival_at_scene AS INT64) AS hour_of_arrival_at_scene
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nhtsa_traffic_fatalities.accident_*` AS a
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2015' AND '2015'
  -- keep only rows for which the key exists (grain)
  AND a.state_number IS NOT NULL
  AND a.consecutive_number IS NOT NULL
ems_and_scene_times_2015.description: One-row-per-accident-level record (or per vehicle/accident if EMS/scene times are vehicle-scoped) providing EMS arrival at hospital hour and arrival at scene hour to compute delays; keep raw hour fields constrained for later validation.

county_earnings_by_year.name: county_earnings_by_year
county_earnings_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(f.GeoFIPS AS STRING) AS GeoFIPS,
  f.GeoName AS GeoName,
  f.Year AS Year,
  SAFE_CAST(f.Employer_contrib_pension_and_insurance AS FLOAT64) / NULLIF(SAFE_CAST(f.Farm_proprietors_employment AS FLOAT64),0) AS Earnings_per_job_avg
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_bea_cainc30.fips` AS f
WHERE
  f.Year IS NOT NULL
county_earnings_by_year.description: One-row-per-county-per-year cohorts containing county identifiers, name, year (date), and the average earnings per job value as stored in the source table. This isolates the relevant time-series observations for county geography.

county_earnings_wide_2012_2017.name: county_earnings_wide_2012_2017
county_earnings_wide_2012_2017.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.GeoFIPS,
  c.GeoName,
  MAX(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.Year) = 2012 THEN c.Earnings_per_job_avg END) AS Earnings_per_job_avg_2012,
  MAX(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.Year) = 2017 THEN c.Earnings_per_job_avg END) AS Earnings_per_job_avg_2017
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_bea_cainc30.fips` AS c
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.Year) IN (2012, 2017)
GROUP BY
  c.GeoFIPS,
  c.GeoName
HAVING
  MAX(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.Year) = 2012 THEN c.Earnings_per_job_avg END) IS NOT NULL
  AND MAX(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM c.Year) = 2017 THEN c.Earnings_per_job_avg END) IS NOT NULL
county_earnings_wide_2012_2017.description: Pivot or join county-year earnings rows to one row per county with separate columns for Earnings_per_job_avg for 2012 and for 2017. Excludes rows where either year's value is NULL (so both years must be present).

acs_county_household_income_under_20000_.name: acs_county_household_income_under_20000_2017_5yr
acs_county_household_income_under_20000_.body_sql:
SELECT
  geo_id,
  NULL AS geo_name,
  CAST(nonfamily_households AS FLOAT64) AS households_under_20000
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2017_5yr`
acs_county_household_income_under_20000_.description: Select ACS 2017 5-year county-level rows and the numeric column representing the count of households with income under $20,000. Keep one row per county (geo_id / GeoFIPS) for later joins.

county_canonical_fips_mapping.name: county_canonical_fips_mapping
county_canonical_fips_mapping.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- canonical 5-char FIPS: if GeoFIPS available (from bea/other views), prefer it; else derive from ACS geo_id where possible.
  -- Lifted literals: none.
  canonical_fips,
  alt_geo_id
FROM (
  -- Gather possible FIPS values from multiple sources into one normalized set.
  SELECT
    -- Normalize various forms to 5-digit zero-padded FIPS.
    CASE
      WHEN SAFE_CAST(GeoFIPS AS STRING) IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(GeoFIPS, r'^\d+$')
        THEN LPAD(GeoFIPS, 5, '0')
      WHEN SAFE_CAST(geo_id AS STRING) IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(geo_id, r'^\d{5}$')
        THEN geo_id
      WHEN SAFE_CAST(geo_id AS STRING) IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(geo_id, r'^\d{3,4}$')
        THEN LPAD(geo_id, 5, '0')
      WHEN SAFE_CAST(geo_id AS STRING) IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(geo_id, r'^US\d{5}$')
        THEN SUBSTR(geo_id, 3, 5)
      ELSE NULL
    END AS canonical_fips,
    -- Preserve any alternate geo_id encountered so consumers can join back to ACS tables
    COALESCE(geo_id, GeoFIPS, GeoFIPS) AS alt_geo_id
  FROM (
    -- Union canonical sources: known views/tables that include county FIPS-like fields.
    SELECT GeoFIPS, NULL AS geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_bea_cainc30.fips`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2018_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2017_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2016_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2015_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2014_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2013_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2012_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2011_5yr`

    UNION ALL

    SELECT NULL AS GeoFIPS, geo_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.county_2010_5yr`
  )
)
WHERE canonical_fips IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY canonical_fips, alt_geo_id
county_canonical_fips_mapping.description: Canonicalize and normalize county FIPS identifiers so they are zero-padded 5-character strings to enable reliable joins between SNAP data and ACS data. Produce one row per county FIPS with both canonical_fips and any alternate geo_id values present in ACS.

coc_countpoint_ny.name: coc_countpoint_ny
coc_countpoint_ny.body_sql:
SELECT
  CoC_Number AS CoC_Number,
  CoC_Name AS CoC_Name,
  Count_Year AS Count_Year,
  Homeless_Veterans AS Homeless_Veterans
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
WHERE
  -- identify CoCs located in New York by name containing common NY indicators
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(CoC_Name), r'\bny\b|new york|brooklyn|manhattan|queens|staten island|bronx|yonkers|rochester|syracuse|albany|troy|utica|buffalo|jamestown|ithaca|white plains|poughkeepsie|kingston|springfield')

semantic_filters.CoC_Name: contains 'NY' OR contains 'New York' OR contains 'N.Y.'

coc_countpoint_ny.description: Subset of CoC point-in-time records restricted to CoC regions located in New York state (identify by CoC_Name containing 'NY' or 'New York' or other New York locality text). Keeps same columns as source.

coc_records_filtered_years.name: coc_records_filtered_years
coc_records_filtered_years.body_sql:
SELECT
  CoC_Number,
  CoC_Name,
  Count_Year,
  Unsheltered_Homeless
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
WHERE
  Count_Year IN (2015, 2018)
  AND Unsheltered_Homeless IS NOT NULL
  AND (CoC_Number IS NOT NULL OR CoC_Name IS NOT NULL)
coc_records_filtered_years.description: Subset of HUD Point-in-Time CoC records limited to the years relevant for analysis (e.g., 2015 and 2018) and to rows that have non-null Unsheltered_Homeless and a non-null CoC identifier (name or number). Keeps raw per-CoC, per-year counts without aggregation.

state_pct_change_2015_2018.name: state_pct_change_2015_2018
state_pct_change_2015_2018.body_sql:
SELECT
  CoC_Number AS state_abbreviation,
  SUM(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless ELSE 0 END) AS unsheltered_2015,
  SUM(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2018 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless ELSE 0 END) AS unsheltered_2018,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    SUM(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2018 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless ELSE 0 END),
    SUM(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless ELSE 0 END)
  ) * 100 AS state_pct_change
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_hud_pit_homelessness.hud_pit_by_coc`
WHERE
  Count_Year IN (2015, 2018)
GROUP BY
  CoC_Number
HAVING
  SUM(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless ELSE NULL END) IS NOT NULL
  AND SUM(CASE WHEN Count_Year = 2015 THEN Unsheltered_Homeless ELSE 0 END) != 0
state_pct_change_2015_2018.description: Per-state percentage change in Unsheltered_Homeless from 2015 to 2018. This reshapes the per-state/year totals into one row per state with unsheltered_2015, unsheltered_2018, and computes state_pct_change using the formula ((unsheltered_2018 - unsheltered_2015) / unsheltered_2015) * 100. Excludes states where unsheltered_2015 is NULL or zero.

dual_eligible_county_snapshots.name: dual_eligible_county_snapshots
dual_eligible_county_snapshots.body_sql:
SELECT
  LPAD(COALESCE(FIPS, ''), 5, '0') AS county_fips,
  Date AS snapshot_date,
  CAST(COALESCE(Public_Total, 0) AS INT64) AS public_total
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cms_dual_eligible_enrollment.dual_eligible_enrollment_by_county_and_program`
dual_eligible_county_snapshots.description: Per-county snapshot of dual-eligible enrollment totals (Public_Total) for each available Date in the dual_eligible_enrollment_by_county_and_program table, with county FIPS normalized to a 5-digit string. One row per county per Date with Public_Total as integer.

county_dual_enrollees_wide.name: county_dual_enrollees_wide
county_dual_enrollees_wide.body_sql:
SELECT
  FIPS AS county_fips,
  -- snapshot total for 2015-12-01 lifted literal (date)
  MAX(CASE WHEN Date = DATE('2015-12-01') THEN Public_Total END) AS dual_enrollees_2015,
  -- snapshot total for 2018-12-01 lifted literal (date)
  MAX(CASE WHEN Date = DATE('2018-12-01') THEN Public_Total END) AS dual_enrollees_2018
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cms_dual_eligible_enrollment.dual_eligible_enrollment_by_county_and_program`
GROUP BY
  FIPS
county_dual_enrollees_wide.description: Per-county wide view that pivots dual-eligible snapshots into columns for the 2015-12-01 and 2018-12-01 snapshots (dual_enrollees_2015, dual_enrollees_2018). One row per county_fips with the two snapshot totals; retains only counties present in at least one snapshot (final NULL-exclusion applied later).

county_births_by_maternal_morbidity.name: county_births_by_maternal_morbidity
county_births_by_maternal_morbidity.body_sql:
SELECT
  County_of_Residence_FIPS AS County_of_Residence_FIPS,
  Year AS Year,
  Maternal_Morbidity_YN AS Maternal_Morbidity_YN,
  SUM(IFNULL(Births, 0)) AS births
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sdoh_cdc_wonder_natality.county_natality_by_maternal_morbidity`
WHERE
  County_of_Residence_FIPS IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  County_of_Residence_FIPS,
  Year,
  Maternal_Morbidity_YN
county_births_by_maternal_morbidity.description: Per-county, per-year counts of births by maternal morbidity flag. Group natality maternal morbidity table by County_of_Residence_FIPS and Year, producing counts of births for each Maternal_Morbidity_YN value and the total births per county-year. Exclude rows where County_of_Residence_FIPS is NULL.

valid_submissions.name: valid_submissions
valid_submissions.body_sql:
SELECT
  submission_number,
  fiscal_year,
  stprba,
  DATE(TIMESTAMP_SECONDS(CAST(date_filed AS INT64))) AS reporting_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.submission`
WHERE
  submission_number IS NOT NULL
  AND submission_number != ''
  AND stprba IS NOT NULL
  AND stprba != ''
  AND fiscal_year IS NOT NULL
valid_submissions.description: Cohort of submission records with non-null, non-empty stprba and canonical fiscal_year and submission_number preserved. Filters out submissions lacking a valid state code.

submission_state_revenue_join.name: submission_state_revenue_join
submission_state_revenue_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  n.submission_number,
  s.stprba,
  s.fiscal_year,
  n.value,
  n.measure_tag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.numbers` AS n
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.sec_quarterly_financials.submission` AS s
ON
  n.submission_number = s.submission_number
WHERE
  -- four-quarter (annual) rolled-up facts are represented with number_of_quarters = 4
  n.number_of_quarters = 4
  -- leave tag selection outside the view so callers can filter measure_tag as needed
submission_state_revenue_join.description: Denormalized relation joining valid submissions to four-quarter revenue facts, producing one row per fact annotated with submission state and fiscal year, suitable for subsequent aggregation by state and year.

users_2021_cohort.name: users_2021_cohort
users_2021_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM creation_date) = 2021
users_2021_cohort.description: All users whose account creation_date falls in the 2021 calendar year (one row per user). Keep original user id and creation_date for downstream time-window calculations and joins.

user_questions.name: user_questions
user_questions.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  owner_user_id,
  creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE post_type_id = 1
user_questions.description: All question posts (post_type_id = 1) with their creation_date and owner_user_id. One row per post (question). This is a canonical set of question rows to be filtered/joined to users for time-window checks.

user_answers.name: user_answers
user_answers.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(a.id AS INT64) AS id,
  CAST(a.owner_user_id AS INT64) AS owner_user_id,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date,
  CAST(a.parent_id AS INT64) AS parent_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  a.post_type_id = 2
user_answers.description: All answer posts (post_type_id = 2) with their creation_date and owner_user_id. One row per post (answer). This is a canonical set of answer rows to be filtered/joined to users/questions for time-window checks.

user_first_question_within_30d.name: user_first_question_within_30d
user_first_question_within_30d.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS owner_user_id,
  q.id AS first_question_id,
  q.creation_date AS first_question_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
JOIN (
  -- each user's earliest question within 30 days (inclusive) of user creation
  SELECT
    uq.owner_user_id,
    ARRAY_AGG(uq ORDER BY uq.creation_date ASC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)].id AS id,
    ARRAY_AGG(uq ORDER BY uq.creation_date ASC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)].creation_date AS creation_date
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS uq
  JOIN
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS uu
  ON
    uq.owner_user_id = uu.id
  WHERE
    uq.creation_date IS NOT NULL
    AND uu.creation_date IS NOT NULL
    AND uq.creation_date BETWEEN uu.creation_date AND TIMESTAMP_ADD(uu.creation_date, INTERVAL 30 DAY)
  GROUP BY
    uq.owner_user_id
) AS q
ON
  q.owner_user_id = u.id
WHERE
  u.creation_date IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.question_within_30d: question.creation_date <= users.creation_date + INTERVAL 30 DAY AND question.creation_date >= users.creation_date

user_first_question_within_30d.description: For each user (from the users cohort), the earliest question (by creation_date) that occurs within 30 days (inclusive) after the user's creation_date. One row per user who has at least one question in that 30-day window; includes the first_question id and creation_date for use in subsequent answer-timing checks.

questions_with_creation_weekday.name: questions_with_creation_weekday
questions_with_creation_weekday.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(p.id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  p.creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%A', p.creation_date) AS weekday_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS p
WHERE
  p.creation_date IS NOT NULL
questions_with_creation_weekday.description: Normalize questions that have a non-null creation_date and compute the weekday name of their creation_date (canonicalize question rows and weekday). One row per question.

answers_min_creation_per_question.name: answers_min_creation_per_question
answers_min_creation_per_question.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(parent_id AS INT64) AS question_id,
  MIN(creation_date) AS earliest_answer_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  creation_date IS NOT NULL
  AND parent_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  parent_id
answers_min_creation_per_question.description: For each answer (linked to a question via parent_id) compute the earliest answer creation_date per question. Exclude answers with null creation_date. One row per question that has at least one answer.

questions_with_earliest_answer.name: questions_with_earliest_answer
questions_with_earliest_answer.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  -- weekday_name lifted from question; expects questions_with_creation_weekday view could be used outside, but here derive directly
  CASE
    WHEN EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) = 1 THEN 'Sunday'
    WHEN EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) = 2 THEN 'Monday'
    WHEN EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) = 3 THEN 'Tuesday'
    WHEN EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) = 4 THEN 'Wednesday'
    WHEN EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) = 5 THEN 'Thursday'
    WHEN EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) = 6 THEN 'Friday'
    WHEN EXTRACT(DAYOFWEEK FROM q.creation_date) = 7 THEN 'Saturday'
    ELSE NULL
  END AS weekday_name,
  a.earliest_answer_creation_date AS earliest_answer_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` q
LEFT JOIN (
  -- find earliest answer creation per question
  SELECT
    parent_id AS question_id,
    MIN(creation_date) AS earliest_answer_creation_date
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
  GROUP BY
    parent_id
) a
ON q.id = a.question_id
questions_with_earliest_answer.description: Left-join questions to their earliest answer (if any) producing one row per question with both question creation and earliest-answer creation when present. Keeps question rows even if there is no answer (earliest_answer_creation_date NULL).

weekday_answer_response_rates.name: weekday_answer_response_rates
weekday_answer_response_rates.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.weekday_name AS weekday_name,
  COUNT(1) AS questions_count,
  SUM(CASE WHEN a.earliest_answer_creation_date IS NOT NULL
                AND a.earliest_answer_creation_date <= TIMESTAMP_ADD(q.question_creation_date, INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
           THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS questions_answered_within_one_hour_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS pq
JOIN
  -- map posts_questions to the questions_with_creation_weekday canonical columns
  (
    SELECT
      id AS question_id,
      creation_date AS question_creation_date,
      FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%A', creation_date) AS weekday_name
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
  ) AS q
  ON pq.id = q.question_id
LEFT JOIN
  -- earliest answer per question (answers_min_creation_per_question equivalent)
  (
    SELECT
      parent_id AS question_id,
      MIN(creation_date) AS earliest_answer_creation_date
    FROM
      `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
    WHERE parent_id IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY parent_id
  ) AS a
  ON q.question_id = a.question_id
GROUP BY
  weekday_name
ORDER BY
  -- ensure deterministic weekday order (Sunday..Saturday)
  CASE weekday_name
    WHEN 'Sunday' THEN 1
    WHEN 'Monday' THEN 2
    WHEN 'Tuesday' THEN 3
    WHEN 'Wednesday' THEN 4
    WHEN 'Thursday' THEN 5
    WHEN 'Friday' THEN 6
    WHEN 'Saturday' THEN 7
    ELSE 8
  END
weekday_answer_response_rates.description: For each weekday, compute counts of questions created that weekday and counts of those whose earliest answer is within one hour (using earliest_answer_creation_date <= question_creation_date + INTERVAL 1 HOUR). One row per weekday.

eligible_users.name: eligible_users
eligible_users.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  display_name,
  reputation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users`
WHERE
  id IS NOT NULL
  AND reputation IS NOT NULL
  AND reputation >= @min_reputation
eligible_users.description: All user rows that meet baseline eligibility criteria (e.g., non-null id and a reputation threshold). This defines the cohort of users to consider for downstream joins and counts.

valid_answer_posts.name: valid_answer_posts
valid_answer_posts.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE a.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
valid_answer_posts.description: All answer posts that are attributable to a user (owner_user_id present). Each row represents a single answer post instance.

user_answer_counts.name: user_answer_counts
user_answer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  SAFE_CAST(owner_user_id AS INT64) AS owner_user_id,
  COUNT(1) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 2
  AND owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  owner_user_id
user_answer_counts.description: Counts of answer posts aggregated per user (one row per user) derived from the set of valid answer posts. This produces a per-user measure that can be joined to user metadata.

users_with_answer_counts.name: users_with_answer_counts
users_with_answer_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS id,
  u.display_name AS display_name,
  u.reputation AS reputation,
  COALESCE(a.answer_count, 0) AS answer_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
    COUNT(1) AS answer_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
  WHERE
    owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY
    owner_user_id
) AS a
ON u.id = a.owner_user_id
users_with_answer_counts.description: Join of eligible user metadata to their aggregated answer counts; one row per user that exists in the eligible user cohort and may include users with zero counts if the aggregation is outer-joined (implementation choice).

python2_tag_cohort.name: python2_tag_cohort
python2_tag_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  -- Token-match for any python 2 tag variant inside the tags string which is formatted as '<tag1><tag2>...'
  (
    tags LIKE '%<python-2.%>' OR
    tags LIKE '%<python-2>%' OR
    tags LIKE '%<python2>%' OR
    tags LIKE '%<python-2.x>%' OR
    tags LIKE '%<python-2.7>%' OR
    tags LIKE '%<python-2.6>%'
  )
python2_tag_cohort.description: Cohort of question ids that have any Python 2 tag token in their tags field. Token-matching logic (tag field formatted like '<tag1><tag2>...') is to be applied when using this cohort; this view identifies candidates by id and tags for downstream set operations.

python3_tag_cohort.name: python3_tag_cohort
python3_tag_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  -- tag string is like '<tag1><tag2>...'; match any token that is exactly 'python-3' or 'python3'
  -- Lifted literals: python-3 and python3
  (tags LIKE '%<python-3>%'
   OR tags LIKE '%<python3>%')
python3_tag_cohort.description: Cohort of question ids that have any Python 3 tag token in their tags field. Token-matching logic (tag field formatted like '<tag1><tag2>...') is to be applied when using this cohort; provides ids for excluding questions mentioning Python 3 via tags.

questions_text_python3_mentions.name: questions_text_python3_mentions
questions_text_python3_mentions.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.body AS body
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
questions_text_python3_mentions.description: One-row-per-question flagging potential Python 3 mentions in the title or body text (for excluding questions that mention Python 3 even if not tagged). Text matching rules are external to this view; it exposes text fields to be scanned for python3 lexical mentions.

questions_core.name: questions_core
questions_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.creation_date AS creation_date,
  q.tags AS tags,
  q.score AS score,
  q.answer_count AS answer_count,
  q.view_count AS view_count,
  q.comment_count AS comment_count,
  q.accepted_answer_id AS accepted_answer_id,
  q.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
questions_core.description: One row per question post with its core metadata (id, creation_date, tags, score, answer_count, view_count, comment_count, accepted_answer_id, owner_user_id) for later filtering and joins.
counter_examples: From July 1, 2019 through December 31, 2019, for all users with IDs between 16712208 and 18712208 on Stack Overflow, retrieve the user ID and the tags of the relevant question for each of their contributions, including comments on both questions and answers, any answers they posted, and any questions they authored, making sure to correctly associate the comment or answer with its parent question’s tags.

answers_core.name: answers_core
answers_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- answer core fields (carry key)
  a.id AS id,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date,
  a.score AS score,
  a.comment_count AS comment_count,
  a.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id
FROM (
  -- union canonical posts table and posts_answers to cover datasets that may use either
  SELECT
    id,
    creation_date,
    score,
    comment_count,
    owner_user_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.stackoverflow_posts`
  WHERE post_type_id = 2  -- answers in the canonical posts_* table
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    id,
    creation_date,
    score,
    comment_count,
    owner_user_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
) AS a
answers_core.description: One row per answer post with its core metadata (id, creation_date, score, comment_count, owner_user_id) for later filtering and joins.
counter_examples: From July 1, 2019 through December 31, 2019, for all users with IDs between 16712208 and 18712208 on Stack Overflow, retrieve the user ID and the tags of the relevant question for each of their contributions, including comments on both questions and answers, any answers they posted, and any questions they authored, making sure to correctly associate the comment or answer with its parent question’s tags.

users_reputation.name: users_reputation
users_reputation.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS id,
  u.reputation AS reputation
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
users_reputation.description: One row per user containing the user's id and reputation to be used when resolving owner_user_id for questions and answers. If a post has no owner_user_id or no matching user, reputation will remain NULL when joined later.

questions_with_tag_tokens.name: questions_with_tag_tokens
questions_with_tag_tokens.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.tags AS tags,
  -- tokenize tags field which is stored like '<tag1><tag2>' and check for exact token presence
  -- lift token literals out of view by using straightforward string pattern checks on angle-bracketed tokens
  -- checks use CONCAT('<', token, '>') to avoid partial matches
  (IFNULL(STRPOS(q.tags, '<' || 'javascript' || '>') > 0, FALSE)) AS has_javascript,
  (IFNULL(STRPOS(q.tags, '<' || 'xss' || '>') > 0, FALSE)) AS has_xss,
  (IFNULL(STRPOS(q.tags, '<' || 'cross-site' || '>') > 0, FALSE)) AS has_cross_site,
  (IFNULL(STRPOS(q.tags, '<' || 'exploit' || '>') > 0, FALSE)) AS has_exploit,
  (IFNULL(STRPOS(q.tags, '<' || 'cybersecurity' || '>') > 0, FALSE)) AS has_cybersecurity
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
questions_with_tag_tokens.description: Normalized question-level tag membership flags (one row per question id) indicating whether the question's tags include specific tokens (e.g. 'javascript', 'xss', 'cross-site', 'exploit', 'cybersecurity') using reliable tag-token matching (angle-bracket tokenization). This allows later filtering by combinations of required tokens.

questions_utc_creation_tags.name: questions_utc_creation_tags
questions_utc_creation_tags.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  -- normalize creation_date to UTC (timestamps in BigQuery are timezone-aware; use TIMESTAMP_SECONDS/TIMESTAMP if needed)
  -- here creation_date is already TIMESTAMP, so convert to UTC by casting to TIMESTAMP and then formatting/parsing via STRING to ensure UTC normalization is explicit.
  -- Keep as TIMESTAMP type in output.
  TIMESTAMP(FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', q.creation_date, 'UTC')) AS creation_date,
  q.tags AS tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE
  q.creation_date IS NOT NULL
questions_utc_creation_tags.description: All question posts with non-null creation timestamps and their tags, normalized to UTC; one row per question post.

questions_month_bucket.name: questions_month_bucket
questions_month_bucket.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', creation_date) AS month
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
questions_month_bucket.description: Canonical month bucket (YYYY-MM) for each question based on creation_date (UTC). Produces one row per question id with an added month column.

questions_tag_indicator.name: questions_tag_indicator
questions_tag_indicator.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  -- tag_name must be provided at query time (e.g., via a view parameter or by filtering when selecting from this view)
  (STRPOS(q.tags, CONCAT('<', @tag_name, '>')) > 0) AS has_tag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
questions_tag_indicator.description: Indicator per question whether it includes a given tag (tag_name provided at query time). Example usage: tag_name = 'python' matches tags containing '<python>'. One row per question id with boolean/flag column indicating tag presence.

monthly_question_counts.name: monthly_question_counts
monthly_question_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  FORMAT_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m', TIMESTAMP_TRUNC(p.creation_date, MONTH)) AS month,
  SUM(CASE WHEN REGEXP_CONTAINS(COALESCE(p.tags, ''), r'(^|<)python(>|$)') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS python_question_count,
  COUNT(1) AS total_question_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS p
GROUP BY
  month
ORDER BY
  month
monthly_question_counts.description: Aggregated counts of questions per month (YYYY-MM) and counts of questions with a specified tag per month. Input should be question rows joined with month bucket and tag indicator. One row per month.

comments_base.name: comments_base
comments_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.user_id AS user_id,
  c.creation_date AS creation_date,
  c.post_id AS post_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments` AS c
comments_base.description: Canonical row-level set of comments with their key metadata including the post they comment on, creation timestamp, and commenting user. One row per comment.

user_contributions_with_question_tags.name: user_contributions_with_question_tags
user_contributions_with_question_tags.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- contributor user id (nullable for deleted/anon users)
  contrib.user_id AS user_id,
  contrib.contribution_type AS contribution_type,
  contrib.contribution_id AS contribution_id,
  contrib.creation_date AS creation_date,
  -- canonical question id for this contribution
  contrib.question_id AS question_id,
  -- tags string from the canonical question (can be NULL)
  q.tags AS question_tags
FROM (
  -- Questions authored: contribution_type = 'question'
  SELECT
    uq.owner_user_id AS user_id,
    'question' AS contribution_type,
    uq.id AS contribution_id,
    uq.creation_date AS creation_date,
    uq.id AS question_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS uq

  UNION ALL

  -- Answers authored: contribution_type = 'answer'
  -- parent_id on answers is the question id
  SELECT
    ua.owner_user_id AS user_id,
    'answer' AS contribution_type,
    ua.id AS contribution_id,
    ua.creation_date AS creation_date,
    ua.parent_id AS question_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS ua

  UNION ALL

  -- Comments: contribution_type = 'comment'
  -- link comment.post_id to question id: post_id may point to question or answer.
  -- If it points to an answer, join that answer's parent_id to get the question id.
  SELECT
    c.user_id AS user_id,
    'comment' AS contribution_type,
    c.id AS contribution_id,
    c.creation_date AS creation_date,
    -- resolve post_id -> question id: if the post is a question use post_id,
    -- otherwise if it's an answer look up parent_id from posts_answers.
    COALESCE(
      -- if there exists a question with this id, use it
      q_check.id,
      -- else if an answer exists with id = c.post_id, use its parent_id
      a.parent_id
    ) AS question_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.comments` AS c
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q_check
    ON q_check.id = c.post_id
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
    ON a.id = c.post_id
) AS contrib
LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
  ON q.id = contrib.question_id
user_contributions_with_question_tags.description: Denormalized row-level list of user contributions (question authored, answer authored, or comment) each linked to the canonical question id and that question's tags. This unifies contributions into a single relation with contribution type, contribution id, contributor user_id, contribution creation_date, question_id, and question_tags.

questions_base.name: questions_base
questions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  -- canonicalized searchable title and body: trimmed and lowercased for simple search normalization
  LOWER(TRIM(q.title)) AS title,
  LOWER(TRIM(q.body)) AS body,
  q.creation_date AS creation_date,
  q.view_count AS view_count,
  q.score AS score,
  q.answer_count AS answer_count,
  q.tags AS tags
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE
  -- ensure row is a question (post_type_id = 1 per StackOverflow schema) if present;
  -- keep rows even if post_type_id is NULL to preserve full cohort as requested
  (q.post_type_id IS NULL OR q.post_type_id = 1)
questions_base.description: All question posts from the posts_questions table with canonicalized searchable title and body text and preserved metadata (no top-k or tag-specific filtering). This forms the base cohort of candidate questions to be filtered and joined to tags.

questions_text_flags.name: questions_text_flags
