questions_text_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  -- standalone word 'how' in title (case-insensitive). Use word boundaries via regex with Unicode-aware (?i)\bhow\b
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(COALESCE(q.title, ''), r'(?i)\bhow\b') AS has_how_in_title,
  -- standalone word 'how' in body
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(COALESCE(q.body, ''), r'(?i)\bhow\b') AS has_how_in_body,
  -- troubleshooting substrings in title (case-insensitive). Lifted literals: 'problem', 'issue', 'error', 'fail', 'not working', 'unable to', 'crash', 'exception', 'debug'
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(COALESCE(q.title, ''), r'(?i)(problem|issue|error|fail|not\\s+working|unable\\s+to|crash|exception|debug)') AS has_troubleshooting_in_title,
  -- troubleshooting substrings in body
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(COALESCE(q.body, ''), r'(?i)(problem|issue|error|fail|not\\s+working|unable\\s+to|crash|exception|debug)') AS has_troubleshooting_in_body
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
questions_text_flags.description: Normalized boolean/text flags indicating whether a question's title or body contains the standalone word 'how' (case-insensitive) and whether title or body contains any troubleshooting substrings (case-insensitive). Operates at the question row level and keeps the question id for joins.

tag_membership_exploded.name: tag_membership_exploded
tag_membership_exploded.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  tag AS tag
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(q.tags, ''), r'^<|>$', ''), '><')) AS tag
tag_membership_exploded.description: One row per (question id, individual_tag) by parsing/exploding the posts_questions.tags field into individual tag tokens. Includes only tag token text (no counts) to enable exact-match tag-based filters later.

stack_overflow_questions_base.name: stack_overflow_questions_base
stack_overflow_questions_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  title,
  body,
  tags,
  view_count,
  post_type_id,
  creation_date,
  owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  post_type_id = 1
  AND view_count IS NOT NULL
stack_overflow_questions_base.description: Base cohort of StackOverflow posts that are questions (post_type_id = 1) from the posts_questions table, excluding rows with NULL view_count. This is a row-level filter only; do not apply any tag or text matching here.

how_question_text_filter.name: how_question_text_filter
how_question_text_filter.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.body AS body,
  (
    -- case-insensitive word-boundary 'how' in title
    REGEXP_CONTAINS(q.title, r'(?i)\bhow\b')
    -- OR title starts with 'how'
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(q.title, r'(?i)^\s*how\b')
    -- OR title contains 'how to'
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(q.title, r'(?i)\bhow\s+to\b')
    -- OR body contains 'how to'
    OR REGEXP_CONTAINS(IFNULL(q.body, ''), r'(?i)\bhow\s+to\b')
  ) AS is_how_question
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
how_question_text_filter.description: Identify questions whose title or body indicates a 'how' question. This includes case-insensitive word-boundary matches for 'how' in the title, title starting with 'how', title containing 'how to', or body containing 'how to'. Do not apply any tag filters here.

questions_with_android_how_flags.name: questions_with_android_how_flags
questions_with_android_how_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.body AS body,
  q.tags AS tags,
  q.view_count AS view_count,
  -- Android tag membership: tags is a space-delimited string like "<android><java>"
  -- Detect presence of '<android>' (case-insensitive)
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(CAST(q.tags AS STRING)), r"<android>") AS has_android_tag,
  -- How-question detection: title starts with "how" or "how to" (case-insensitive), allowing optional punctuation
  REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(COALESCE(q.title, '')), r"^\s*how(\s+to)?\b") AS is_how_question
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
questions_with_android_how_flags.description: Denormalized view joining the base question rows with Android tag membership and how-question text flag to produce one row per question with boolean flags for 'has_android_tag' and 'is_how_question' along with title, tags and view_count for downstream sorting and selection.

question_base.name: question_base
question_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  -- canonicalize numeric view_count: leave NULLs as NULL; ensure INT64 type
  SAFE_CAST(q.view_count AS INT64) AS view_count,
  q.accepted_answer_id AS accepted_answer_id
FROM `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE q.post_type_id = 1
question_base.description: One row per question with canonicalized numeric view_count and essential question identifiers/owner; only include rows that are actual questions (filter by post_type_id). NULL view_count is left as NULL (caller may treat as 0).

answer_base.name: answer_base
answer_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.parent_id AS parent_id,
  a.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  a.score AS score
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  a.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  AND a.post_type_id = 2
answer_base.description: One row per answer with its parent question id, owner, and score; exclude answers without an owner (owner_user_id IS NULL).

question_answer_top_answers.name: question_answer_top_answers
question_answer_top_answers.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.parent_id AS parent_id,
  a.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  a.score AS score,
  DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY a.parent_id ORDER BY a.score DESC) AS score_rank_within_question
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
question_answer_top_answers.description: For each answer, compute its rank position within its question by answer score (dense ranking that allows ties at the cutoff); one row per answer with its per-question rank so callers can select top-N (including ties).

user_answers_filtered_by_date.name: user_answers_filtered_by_date
user_answers_filtered_by_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS id,
  a.parent_id AS parent_id,
  a.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id,
  a.creation_date AS creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
WHERE
  a.post_type_id = 2
  AND a.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
  AND a.creation_date >= TIMESTAMP(@creation_date_cutoff)
  AND a.owner_user_id = @owner_user_id
user_answers_filtered_by_date.description: All answer posts authored by a user (answers from the posts_answers table) filtered by author and a creation_date cutoff; one row per answer. This isolates the answer cohort to be analyzed.

question_tags_normalized.name: question_tags_normalized
question_tags_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  tag AS tag_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q,
  UNNEST(
    -- split tags like '<tag1><tag2>' into individual tag names
    REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(q.tags, r'<([^>]+)>')
  ) AS tag
question_tags_normalized.description: Normalize question tag strings into individual tag names. Takes question rows and expands the delimitered tags field (e.g. '<tag1><tag2>') into one row per question-tag pair with canonical tag_name.

answers_join_questions_tags_and_votes.name: answers_join_questions_tags_and_votes
answers_join_questions_tags_and_votes.body_sql:
SELECT
  a.id AS answer_id,
  a.parent_id AS parent_id,
  t.tag_name AS tag_name,
  v.vote_type_id AS vote_type_id,
  v.id AS vote_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
  ON a.parent_id = q.id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.tags` AS t
  ON TRUE
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.votes` AS v
  ON v.post_id = a.id
-- break out the question tags string into individual tag names by matching tag table entries
WHERE
  -- only keep tag rows whose tag_name appears in the question's tags field (tags are stored like "<tag1><tag2>")
  INSTR(q.tags, CONCAT('<', t.tag_name, '>')) > 0
answers_join_questions_tags_and_votes.description: Denormalized rows joining filtered user answers to their parent question's individual tags and to votes on those answers. One row per (answer_id, tag_name, vote); enables counting upvotes and accepted events per tag for the user's answers.

questions_base_37.name: questions_base_37
questions_base_37.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  creation_date,
  owner_user_id,
  title
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions`
WHERE
  creation_date IS NOT NULL
questions_base_37.description: One row per question post from the posts_questions table, filtered to valid (non-null) creation_date. This is a canonical question cohort (no year/date range applied here).

answers_base.name: answers_base
answers_base.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  parent_id,
  creation_date,
  owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers`
WHERE
  creation_date IS NOT NULL
  AND post_type_id = 2
answers_base.description: One row per answer post from the posts_answers table, filtered to valid (non-null) creation_date. Keep parent_id to link to question.

questions_with_answer_times.name: questions_with_answer_times
questions_with_answer_times.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS question_id,
  q.creation_date AS question_creation_date,
  a.id AS answer_id,
  a.creation_date AS answer_creation_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_answers` AS a
ON
  a.parent_id = q.id
questions_with_answer_times.description: For each question (one row per question-answer pair), join questions to answers that reference the question (denormalized pairs). Do not apply temporal window filtering here; include answer creation_date to enable later time-delta calculations.

question_base_40.name: question_base_40
question_base_40.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.id AS id,
  q.title AS title,
  q.body AS body,
  LENGTH(q.body) AS body_length,
  q.accepted_answer_id AS accepted_answer_id,
  q.owner_user_id AS owner_user_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.posts_questions` AS q
WHERE
  q.owner_user_id IS NOT NULL
question_base_40.description: One row per question with basic canonical fields needed for later joins: id, title, body, body_length (character length), accepted_answer_id, owner_user_id. Exclude questions with NULL owner_user_id so author metrics can be computed.

user_metrics.name: user_metrics
user_metrics.body_sql:
SELECT
  u.id AS id,
  u.reputation AS reputation,
  u.up_votes AS up_votes,
  u.down_votes AS down_votes,
  SAFE_CAST(u.up_votes - u.down_votes AS INT64) AS net_votes,
  COALESCE(b.badge_count, 0) AS badge_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.users` AS u
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT
    user_id AS id,
    COUNT(1) AS badge_count
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.stackoverflow.badges`
  WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY user_id
) AS b
ON u.id = b.id
user_metrics.description: One row per user with reputation, up_votes, down_votes, net_votes (up_votes - down_votes), and badge_count (count of badges the user has). Only include users that exist in the users table.

alive_patients.name: alive_patients
alive_patients.body_sql:
SELECT
  id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.patient`
WHERE
  -- alive = no deceased.dateTime recorded
  deceased.dateTime IS NULL

semantic_filters.patient.deceased.dateTime: IS NULL OR patient.deceased DOES NOT EXIST

alive_patients.description: One row per patient who is recorded in the patient table and is considered alive (no deceased.dateTime recorded).

patient_condition_flags.name: patient_condition_flags
patient_condition_flags.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.id AS id,
  c.subject.patientId AS subject_patient_id,
  -- diabetes if 'diabetes' appears in code text or any coding.code/display/system (case-insensitive)
  (
    IFNULL(
      REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(c.code.text, '')), r'diabetes'),
      FALSE
    )
    OR EXISTS(
      SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS coding
      WHERE (
        (coding.code IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(coding.code), r'diabetes'))
        OR (coding.display IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(coding.display), r'diabetes'))
        OR (coding.system IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(coding.system), r'diabetes'))
      )
    )
  ) AS is_diabetes,
  -- hypertension if 'hypertension' or 'hypertens' appears in code text or any coding.code/display/system (case-insensitive)
  (
    IFNULL(
      REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(IFNULL(c.code.text, '')), r'hypertens'),
      FALSE
    )
    OR EXISTS(
      SELECT 1 FROM UNNEST(c.code.coding) AS coding
      WHERE (
        (coding.code IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(coding.code), r'hypertens'))
        OR (coding.display IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(coding.display), r'hypertens'))
        OR (coding.system IS NOT NULL AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(coding.system), r'hypertens'))
      )
    )
  ) AS is_hypertension
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.condition` AS c
patient_condition_flags.description: One row per condition record normalized to link to the patient and with boolean flags indicating whether the condition represents Diabetes or Hypertension using case-insensitive substring matches on condition.code.text and any coding elements (coding.code, coding.display, coding.system).

patient_medication_active_counts.name: patient_medication_active_counts
patient_medication_active_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  mr.subject.patientId AS subject_patient_id,
  COUNT(DISTINCT identifier.value) AS distinct_active_medication_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fhir_synthea.medication_request` AS mr,
  UNNEST(mr.identifier) AS identifier
WHERE
  -- normalized_status logic lifted out of view; assume caller filters by normalized_status = 'active'
  TRUE
GROUP BY
  subject_patient_id
patient_medication_active_counts.description: One row per patient with the count of distinct active medication_identifiers derived from medication_request records (active determined from normalized_status). This is a grouped measure to be used for threshold filtering (e.g., >= 7 distinct active medications).

objects_core.name: objects_core
objects_core.body_sql:
SELECT
  object_id,
  -- canonical null-handling: empty string for textual NULLs
  COALESCE(title, '') AS title,
  COALESCE(object_name, '') AS object_name,
  COALESCE(department, '') AS department,
  COALESCE(artist_display_name, '') AS artist_display_name,
  COALESCE(medium, '') AS medium,
  object_end_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects`
objects_core.description: One-row-per-object core object records with canonical null-handling for textual fields. This view selects object rows and exposes primary object attributes for downstream filtering and joins.
validated_on: Retrieve the object id, title, and the formatted metadata date (as a string in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format) for objects in the "The Libraries" department where the cropConfidence is greater than 0.5, the object's title contains the word "book".

images_by_object.name: images_by_object
images_by_object.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(object_id AS STRING) || '_' || CAST(ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY object_id ORDER BY original_image_url) AS STRING) AS image_id,
  object_id,
  original_image_url
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images`
images_by_object.description: One-row-per-image (or per image record) exposing image URLs and linking images to their object by object_id. Provides original_image_url and other image metadata for join to objects.

objects_photographs_department.name: objects_photographs_department
objects_photographs_department.body_sql:
SELECT
  oc.object_id AS object_id,
  oc.title AS title,
  oc.object_name AS object_name,
  oc.artist_display_name AS artist_display_name,
  oc.medium AS medium,
  oc.object_end_date AS object_end_date,
  oc.department AS department
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS oc
WHERE
  oc.department = 'Photographs'
objects_photographs_department.description: Cohort of objects that belong to the 'Photographs' department — a reusable subset filtered by department (no other question-specific predicates).

objects_with_images_join.name: objects_with_images_join
objects_with_images_join.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id,
  o.title,
  o.object_name,
  o.artist_display_name,
  o.medium,
  o.object_end_date,
  i.original_image_url
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS o
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.images` AS i
ON
  o.object_id = i.object_id
objects_with_images_join.description: Denormalized join of objects to their images via object_id; one row per object-image combination providing object fields alongside image.original_image_url for easy projection.

objects_with_valid_period.name: objects_with_valid_period
objects_with_valid_period.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(object_id AS STRING) AS object_id,  -- carry key column (object_id) as required by view joinability
  period
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects`
WHERE
  period IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(period) <> ''
objects_with_valid_period.description: Subset of objects that have a non-null, non-empty period value. One row per object record preserving its period.

object_label_associations.name: object_label_associations
object_label_associations.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id AS object_id,
  o.period AS period,
  la.description AS label_description
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` v,
  UNNEST(v.labelAnnotations) AS la
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` o
ON
  v.object_id = o.object_id
WHERE
  la.description IS NOT NULL
  AND o.period IS NOT NULL
object_label_associations.description: Associations between objects (with period) and label descriptions by joining valid-period objects to flattened vision label annotations. One row per object_id and label_description pair for objects that have matching vision data.

objects_normalized_text.name: objects_normalized_text
objects_normalized_text.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id AS object_id,
  -- normalized lowercase title: prefer title from objects_core if available, else original title;
  -- trim whitespace and collapse internal whitespace to single space, then lower-case.
  LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(COALESCE(o.title, o.object_name, '')) , r'\s+', ' ')) AS title_lower,
  -- canonical metadata_date: if metadata_date present and valid timestamp, convert to DATE(); else NULL.
  -- Use SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP on the original metadata_date string if needed, but source schema has TIMESTAMP type,
  -- so we accept NULLs and cast to DATE safely.
  CAST(o.metadata_date AS DATE) AS metadata_date_canonical
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS o
objects_normalized_text.description: Normalize text fields from objects for case-insensitive search and canonical date formatting; produces a cleaned title_lower and a canonical metadata_date (DATE or NULL).

objects_with_vision.name: objects_with_vision
objects_with_vision.body_sql:
SELECT
  o.object_id AS object_id,
  o.title AS title,
  o.metadata_date AS metadata_date,
  -- max confidence among crop hints for this object (NULL if no cropHints)
  (SELECT MAX(ch.confidence) FROM UNNEST(v.cropHintsAnnotation.cropHints) AS ch) AS max_crop_hint_confidence,
  -- boolean flag whether any crop hint confidence > 0.5
  ((SELECT MAX(IFNULL(ch.confidence, -1)) FROM UNNEST(v.cropHintsAnnotation.cropHints) AS ch) > 0.5) AS has_crop_hint_confidence_gt_0_5,
  o.department AS department
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.objects` AS o
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.the_met.vision_api_data` AS v
ON
  o.object_id = v.object_id
objects_with_vision.description: Denormalized join of object rows with their vision crop-hints summary to enable final filtering by department/title and crop-hint confidence.

clean_valid_pitches.name: clean_valid_pitches
clean_valid_pitches.body_sql:
SELECT
  gameId AS game_pk,
  DATE(startTime) AS game_date,
  homeTeamId,
  awayTeamId,
  pitcherId,
  COALESCE(pitcherFirstName, '') AS pitcherFirstName,
  COALESCE(pitcherLastName, '') AS pitcherLastName,
  CAST(pitchSpeed AS INT64) AS pitchSpeed,
  homeFielder1,
  homeFielder2,
  homeFielder3,
  homeFielder4,
  homeFielder5,
  homeFielder6,
  homeFielder7,
  homeFielder8,
  homeFielder9,
  homeFielder10,
  homeFielder11,
  homeFielder12,
  homeBatter1,
  homeBatter2,
  homeBatter3,
  homeBatter4,
  homeBatter5,
  homeBatter6,
  homeBatter7,
  homeBatter8,
  homeBatter9,
  awayFielder1,
  awayFielder2,
  awayFielder3,
  awayFielder4,
  awayFielder5,
  awayFielder6,
  awayFielder7,
  awayFielder8,
  awayFielder9,
  awayFielder10,
  awayFielder11,
  awayFielder12,
  awayBatter1,
  awayBatter2,
  awayBatter3,
  awayBatter4,
  awayBatter5,
  awayBatter6,
  awayBatter7,
  awayBatter8,
  awayBatter9,
  lineupTeamId,
  lineupPlayerId
FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_wide`
WHERE
  -- Exclude missing/empty pitcherId
  pitcherId IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(pitcherId) <> ''
  -- pitchSpeed must be present and positive; cast-safe by requiring not null and > 0
  AND pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE_CAST(pitchSpeed AS NUMERIC) > 0
  -- Ensure pitcher name fields present (allow empty strings but coalesced above)
  AND (pitcherFirstName IS NOT NULL OR pitcherLastName IS NOT NULL)
  -- Normalize pitch types: keep common pitchType non-null (lift literals out of view as requested)
  -- (Caller can filter specific pitch types when querying this view)
clean_valid_pitches.description: Normalize and filter the unified pitch rows to canonical types and exclude pitches with missing/empty pitcherId or non-positive pitchSpeed. Convert pitchSpeed to integer and ensure pitcherId and pitcher name fields are present. Keep all team and lineup columns needed to validate pitcher-team association.

team_pitcher_max_speed.name: team_pitcher_max_speed
team_pitcher_max_speed.body_sql:
SELECT
  team_id,
  pitcher_id,
  ANY_VALUE(pitcher_first_name) AS pitcher_first_name,
  ANY_VALUE(pitcher_last_name) AS pitcher_last_name,
  MAX(pitchSpeed) AS max_pitch_speed
FROM (
  -- source 1: games_post_wide
  SELECT
    -- pitcher was on the home team for this pitch
    homeTeamId AS team_id,
    pitcherId AS pitcher_id,
    pitcherFirstName AS pitcher_first_name,
    pitcherLastName AS pitcher_last_name,
    pitchSpeed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_post_wide`
  WHERE pitcherId IS NOT NULL
    AND pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    -- pitcher was on the away team for this pitch
    awayTeamId AS team_id,
    pitcherId AS pitcher_id,
    pitcherFirstName AS pitcher_first_name,
    pitcherLastName AS pitcher_last_name,
    pitchSpeed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_post_wide`
  WHERE pitcherId IS NOT NULL
    AND pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- source 2: games_wide
  SELECT
    homeTeamId AS team_id,
    pitcherId AS pitcher_id,
    pitcherFirstName AS pitcher_first_name,
    pitcherLastName AS pitcher_last_name,
    pitchSpeed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_wide`
  WHERE pitcherId IS NOT NULL
    AND pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  SELECT
    awayTeamId AS team_id,
    pitcherId AS pitcher_id,
    pitcherFirstName AS pitcher_first_name,
    pitcherLastName AS pitcher_last_name,
    pitchSpeed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_wide`
  WHERE pitcherId IS NOT NULL
    AND pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- optional normalized view of validated pitches (if available)
  SELECT
    lineupTeamId AS team_id,
    pitcherId AS pitcher_id,
    pitcherFirstName AS pitcher_first_name,
    pitcherLastName AS pitcher_last_name,
    pitchSpeed
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.baseball.games_post_wide`
  WHERE pitcherId IS NOT NULL
    AND pitchSpeed IS NOT NULL
)
GROUP BY team_id, pitcher_id
team_pitcher_max_speed.description: For each team and pitcher pairing (one row per team_id and pitcher_id), compute the maximum observed pitchSpeed (integer) across all validated pitch records where the pitcher was playing for that team. This aggregates across both game sources.

photos_raw_rows.name: photos_raw_rows
photos_raw_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key/id columns to keep view joinable
  id,
  -- required output aliases for the view's category: 'user', 'clicks', '_TABLE_SUFFIX'
  user AS `user`,
  -- clicks is not present in source; lift as NULL so downstream can populate or join safely
  NULL AS clicks,
  _TABLE_SUFFIX
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.eclipse_megamovie.photos_v_0_*`
WHERE
  -- exclude rows with NULL user as requested
  user IS NOT NULL
  -- keep shards selection generic: caller should filter _TABLE_SUFFIX when querying the view
photos_raw_rows.description: Row-level selection of photos table rows from the photos_v_0_* shards with basic provenance; does not aggregate. Excludes rows with NULL user to keep downstream joins/aggregations valid.

sales_filtered_2019_2021.name: sales_filtered_2019_2021
sales_filtered_2019_2021.body_sql:
SELECT
  invoice_and_item_number AS sale_id,
  category_name,
  sale_dollars,
  volume_sold_liters,
  date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) BETWEEN 2019 AND 2021
  AND volume_sold_liters IS NOT NULL
  AND volume_sold_liters != 0
  AND sale_dollars IS NOT NULL
sales_filtered_2019_2021.description: Filtered cohort of sales transactions restricted to calendar years 2019-2021, excluding rows with NULL or zero volume_sold_liters or NULL sale_dollars. Keeps original transaction-level columns needed for price-per-liter calculation and category grouping.

sales_price_per_liter_txn.name: sales_price_per_liter_txn
sales_price_per_liter_txn.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through the unique transaction identifier
  invoice_and_item_number AS sale_id,
  -- canonicalize category_name: trim and title-case; if NULL or empty, set to 'Unknown'
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(category_name) = '' OR category_name IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
    ELSE INITCAP(TRIM(category_name))
  END AS category_name,
  -- compute price per liter; protect against division by zero or NULL volume
  CASE
    WHEN volume_sold_liters IS NULL OR volume_sold_liters = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE sale_dollars / volume_sold_liters
  END AS price_per_liter,
  date,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
sales_price_per_liter_txn.description: Normalized transaction-level view that computes per-transaction price_per_liter as sale_dollars / volume_sold_liters and canonicalizes category_name. One row per sales transaction.

category_yearly_avg_price.name: category_yearly_avg_price
category_yearly_avg_price.body_sql:
SELECT
  category_name,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) AS year,
  AVG(price_per_liter) AS avg_price_per_liter
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` s
-- use transaction-level price per liter computed as sale_dollars / NULLIF(volume_sold_liters, 0)
-- if a precomputed view is preferred, replace the FROM with the provided view `sales_price_per_liter_txn`
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([STRUCT(
  CASE
    WHEN s.volume_sold_liters IS NULL OR s.volume_sold_liters = 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE s.sale_dollars / s.volume_sold_liters
  END AS price_per_liter
)]) AS derived
WHERE
  s.category_name IS NOT NULL
  AND s.date IS NOT NULL
  AND derived.price_per_liter IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  category_name,
  year
category_yearly_avg_price.description: Aggregated average per-liter retail price per liquor category per calendar year. Uses transaction-level price_per_liter values and groups by category_name and year.

sales_filtered_by_date.name: sales_filtered_by_date
sales_filtered_by_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- row_id: use the invoice_and_item_number as a stable unique identifier for the raw sale row
  invoice_and_item_number AS row_id,
  date,
  item_number,
  item_description,
  sale_dollars
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE
  -- Lift year list out of view; include rows whose date year is in the years of interest.
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM date) IN (2022, 2023)
sales_filtered_by_date.description: Subset of sales rows restricted to relevant calendar date ranges. This view filters the sales table to include only rows whose date falls within the union of the years of interest (e.g., 2022 and 2023). It preserves each raw sale row for later aggregation.

item_calendar_year_sales.name: item_calendar_year_sales
item_calendar_year_sales.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.item_number AS item_number,
  s.item_description AS item_description,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM s.date) AS calendar_year,
  SUM(s.sale_dollars) AS sales_total
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` AS s
GROUP BY
  s.item_number,
  s.item_description,
  calendar_year
item_calendar_year_sales.description: Total sales dollars per item per calendar year. Aggregates sale_dollars from sales rows into one row per item_number, item_description, and calendar_year (extracted from date).

bourbon_whiskey_sales_events.name: bourbon_whiskey_sales_events
bourbon_whiskey_sales_events.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through unique id for the sale row
  invoice_and_item_number AS sale_id,
  -- normalize date to DATE type (already DATE in source)
  date AS sale_date,
  zip_code,
  county,
  category_name,
  item_description,
  -- ensure numeric sale_dollars
  SAFE_CAST(sale_dollars AS FLOAT64) AS sale_dollars
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE
  category = 'SEL'
  AND zip_code IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.item_is_bourbon_whiskey: derived (category_name indicates Bourbon Whiskey OR item_description contains both 'Bourbon' and 'Whiskey')

bourbon_whiskey_sales_events.description: All individual sales rows that correspond to Bourbon Whiskey items, with normalized sale_date and numeric sale_dollars; keep only rows with a non-null zip_code. Do not apply date or county limits here (those are applied later).

zip_population_21_plus_by_year.name: zip_population_21_plus_by_year
zip_population_21_plus_by_year.body_sql:
SELECT
  zipcode AS zip_code,
  CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
  SUM(IF(minimum_age IS NULL OR maximum_age IS NULL,
         0,  -- exclude rows that are totals/unknown age ranges
         IF(maximum_age >= 21 OR minimum_age >= 21, population, 0)
       )) AS population_21_plus
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_usa.population_by_zip_*`
GROUP BY
  zipcode,
  year

semantic_filters.population_source: ZIP-level population table(s) (population_by_zip_<N>) and normalized to population_21_plus; exclude rows where population_21_plus is NULL

zip_population_21_plus_by_year.description: ZIP-level population of residents aged 21 and older by year. Normalize/populate a single numeric population_21_plus column per (zip_code, year). Do not filter to any specific year here.

monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip.name: monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip
monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip.body_sql:
SELECT
  b.zip_code AS zip_code,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM b.sale_date) AS year,
  FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m', DATE_TRUNC(b.sale_date, MONTH)) AS year_month,
  SUM(b.sale_dollars) AS total_bourbon_sales_dollars
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales` AS s
-- identify bourbon whiskey by category_name containing 'Bourbon' OR item_description containing 'Bourbon' (lift literals out of view)
CROSS JOIN UNNEST([s.category_name]) AS cat_name WITH OFFSET AS off_unused
-- category_name is a top-level STRING in the DDL; UNNEST above is harmless if not repeated
JOIN (
  SELECT
    invoice_and_item_number,
    date AS sale_date,
    zip_code,
    category_name,
    item_description,
    sale_dollars
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
) AS b
ON s.invoice_and_item_number = b.invoice_and_item_number
WHERE
  -- filter for Bourbon Whiskey by checking category_name or item_description; the literal 'Bourbon' should be provided by the user at query time if they wish to change it
  (LOWER(COALESCE(b.category_name, '')) LIKE '%bourbon%'
   OR LOWER(COALESCE(b.item_description, '')) LIKE '%bourbon%')
GROUP BY
  zip_code,
  year,
  year_month
monthly_bourbon_sales_by_zip.description: Aggregate Bourbon Whiskey sale dollars to month-level totals per zip_code and year_month. Uses bourbon_whiskey_sales_events as input; does not restrict to county or year here.

dubuque_county_zip_codes.name: dubuque_county_zip_codes
dubuque_county_zip_codes.body_sql:
SELECT
  zip_code,
  county
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.iowa_liquor_sales.sales`
WHERE
  county = 'DUBUQUE'
GROUP BY
  zip_code,
  county

semantic_filters.county: Dubuque (this view lists ZIPs for Dubuque county; do not apply date or sales filters)

dubuque_county_zip_codes.description: List of ZIP codes that are associated with Dubuque county (one row per zip_code). Used to restrict analyses to ZIPs in Dubuque County.

taxonomy_code_canonical.name: taxonomy_code_canonical
taxonomy_code_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  code,
  NULLIF(TRIM(specialization), "") AS specialization
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.nppes.healthcare_provider_taxonomy_code_set_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '090' AND '170'
GROUP BY
  code,
  specialization
taxonomy_code_canonical.description: Canonicalize taxonomy code set rows: keep taxonomy code and its specialization text, with empty or whitespace-only specializations normalized to NULL. One row per taxonomy code.

female_name_state_year_cohort.name: female_name_state_year_cohort
female_name_state_year_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  state,
  year,
  name,
  gender,
  number AS count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
WHERE
  gender = 'F'
female_name_state_year_cohort.description: One row per name/state/year for female births: raw cohort of births filtered to female gender and a specific year, retaining counts by name and state.

name_year_total_across_states.name: name_year_total_across_states
name_year_total_across_states.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  name,
  SUM(number) AS total_count_all_states
FROM `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
GROUP BY year, name
name_year_total_across_states.description: Total count of births for each name and year across all states (sums counts from the state-level cohort).

wyoming_name_year_counts.name: wyoming_name_year_counts
wyoming_name_year_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  state,
  year,
  name,
  SUM(number) AS wy_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usa_names.usa_1910_current`
WHERE
  state = 'WY'
  AND gender = 'F'
GROUP BY
  state,
  year,
