wyoming_name_year_counts.description: Counts of female births by name for Wyoming for each year (a state-specific subset of the female cohort).

ccrcc_proteome_aliquot_level.name: ccrcc_proteome_aliquot_level
ccrcc_proteome_aliquot_level.body_sql:
SELECT
  q.aliquot_submitter_id AS aliquot_submitter_id,
  c.case_submitter_id AS case_submitter_id,
  q.gene_symbol AS gene_symbol,
  q.protein_abundance_log2ratio AS protein_abundance_log2ratio,
  m.sample_submitter_id AS sample_submitter_id
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.quant_proteome_CPTAC_CCRCC_discovery_study_pdc_current` AS q
LEFT JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.aliquot_to_case_mapping_current` AS m
ON
  q.aliquot_id = m.aliquot_id
LEFT JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.case_metadata_current` AS c
ON
  m.case_id = c.case_id
WHERE
  q.gene_symbol IS NOT NULL
  AND q.aliquot_submitter_id IS NOT NULL
ccrcc_proteome_aliquot_level.description: One-row-per-proteome-aliquot measurements from the CPTAC CCRCC proteome discovery study, canonicalized column names for joining (including aliquot_submitter_id, gene_symbol, and protein_abundance_log2ratio).

rnaseq_sample_gene_expression.name: rnaseq_sample_gene_expression
rnaseq_sample_gene_expression.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.sample_barcode AS sample_barcode,
  m.case_submitter_id AS case_submitter_id,
  r.sample_type_name AS sample_type_name,
  r.gene_name AS gene_name,
  r.fpkm_unstranded AS fpkm_unstranded
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.CPTAC.RNAseq_hg38_gdc_current` AS r
LEFT JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.PDC_metadata.aliquot_to_case_mapping_current` AS m
ON
  r.aliquot_gdc_id = m.aliquot_id
rnaseq_sample_gene_expression.description: One-row-per-RNAseq-sample-and-gene expression values, exposing sample barcode/submitter id, sample_type_name, gene_name, and fpkm_unstranded for downstream transformation and filtering.

annotations_patient_entries.name: annotations_patient_entries
annotations_patient_entries.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- key/joinable identifiers
  case_barcode AS case_barcode,
  case_gdc_id AS case_gdc_id,

  -- preserved annotation fields for joining/filtering (renamed per view spec)
  category AS categoryName,
  classification AS classificationName,

  -- unique annotation identifier (grain)
  CONCAT(project_short_name, ":", entity_barcode, ":", SAFE_CAST(FARM_FINGERPRINT(IFNULL(date_created, "")) AS STRING)) AS annotation_id

FROM
  `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Annotations` a

WHERE
  -- only patient/case-level annotations:
  LOWER(IFNULL(entity_type, "")) IN ('patient', 'case')
annotations_patient_entries.description: All annotation rows at the patient (case) level. This selects annotation records whose entity_type denotes a patient and preserves annotation classification and category fields for later joining and filtering.

paad_mc3_pass_variants_per_participant_s.name: paad_mc3_pass_variants_per_participant_sample
paad_mc3_pass_variants_per_participant_s.body_sql:
SELECT
  ParticipantBarcode,
  Tumor_SampleBarcode,
  Tumor_AliquotBarcode,
  Hugo_Symbol,
  FILTER,
  -- lift question-specific literals out of the view (none here); include remaining variant columns as a JSON string to satisfy "other_variant_columns"
  TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(
    Variant_Classification,
    HGVSp_Short,
    HGVSc,
    CENTERS
  )) AS other_variant_columns
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample`
WHERE
  Study = 'PAAD'
  AND FILTER = 'PASS'
paad_mc3_pass_variants_per_participant_s.description: Row-level subset of MC3 MAF rows restricted to tumor samples from the PAAD study and to variants that passed quality filters (FILTER = 'PASS'). Keeps original variant-level columns for later aggregation and patient/sample identifiers.

participant_level_gene_mutation_presence.name: participant_level_gene_mutation_presence
participant_level_gene_mutation_presence.body_sql:
SELECT
  pp.ParticipantBarcode,
  pp.Hugo_Symbol,
  IF(SUM(IF(pp.FILTER = 'PASS', 1, 0)) > 0, 1, 0) AS has_pass_variant
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample` AS pp
GROUP BY
  pp.ParticipantBarcode,
  pp.Hugo_Symbol
participant_level_gene_mutation_presence.description: For each ParticipantBarcode and Hugo_Symbol, indicate presence (1) or absence (0) of at least one PASS variant across any tumor sample/aliquot for that participant. Collapses multiple sample/aliquot rows to participant-gene binary membership.

participant_binary_kras_tp53_status.name: participant_binary_kras_tp53_status
participant_binary_kras_tp53_status.body_sql:
SELECT
  ParticipantBarcode,
  IF(SUM(CASE WHEN Hugo_Symbol = 'KRAS' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0, 1, 0) AS has_kras,
  IF(SUM(CASE WHEN Hugo_Symbol = 'TP53' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0, 1, 0) AS has_tp53
FROM `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample`
WHERE FILTER = 'PASS'
GROUP BY ParticipantBarcode
participant_binary_kras_tp53_status.description: One row per ParticipantBarcode with boolean/binary flags indicating whether the participant has any PASS KRAS variant and any PASS TP53 variant. Derived by pivoting participant-gene presence rows for Hugo_Symbol values KRAS and TP53 into columns has_kras and has_tp53 (0/1). Participants with neither gene present should still appear with zeros.

maf_variants_coding_mutations.name: maf_variants_coding_mutations
maf_variants_coding_mutations.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry through participant barcode for joinability
  ParticipantBarcode,
  -- canonical Hugo_Symbol: prefer non-empty Hugo_Symbol, filter out unknowns
  Hugo_Symbol,
  -- canonicalize Variant_Classification into a normalized set of protein-altering classes
  CASE
    WHEN Variant_Classification IN ('Missense_Mutation','Missense') THEN 'Missense_Mutation'
    WHEN Variant_Classification IN ('Nonsense_Mutation','Nonsense') THEN 'Nonsense_Mutation'
    WHEN Variant_Classification IN ('Frame_Shift_Del','Frame_Shift_Ins','Frame_Shift') THEN 'Frame_Shift'
    WHEN Variant_Classification IN ('In_Frame_Del','In_Frame_Ins','In_Frame') THEN 'In_Frame'
    WHEN Variant_Classification IN ('Splice_Site','Splice_Region') THEN 'Splice_Site'
    WHEN Variant_Classification IN ('Nonstop_Mutation','Nonstop') THEN 'Nonstop_Mutation'
    WHEN Variant_Classification IN ('Translation_Start_Site','Start_Codon') THEN 'Translation_Start_Site'
    ELSE Variant_Classification
  END AS Variant_Classification
FROM `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample`
WHERE
  -- require participant and gene present and not unknown
  ParticipantBarcode IS NOT NULL
  AND Hugo_Symbol IS NOT NULL
  AND Hugo_Symbol <> ''
  AND LOWER(Hugo_Symbol) <> 'unknown'
  -- limit to protein-altering variant classifications (lift literals out as requested)
  AND Variant_Classification IN (
    'Missense_Mutation',
    'Nonsense_Mutation',
    'Frame_Shift_Del',
    'Frame_Shift_Ins',
    'In_Frame_Del',
    'In_Frame_Ins',
    'Splice_Site',
    'Nonstop_Mutation',
    'Translation_Start_Site'
  )
maf_variants_coding_mutations.description: Normalized projection of variant rows representing likely coding-impacting somatic mutations (canonicalizes Variant_Classification and ensures Hugo_Symbol and ParticipantBarcode are present), limited to variant classifications that are considered protein-altering.

participant_gene_mutation_presence.name: participant_gene_mutation_presence
participant_gene_mutation_presence.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.ParticipantBarcode,
  p.Hugo_Symbol,
  CASE WHEN COUNT(1) > 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS has_mutation
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.pancancer_atlas.Filtered_MC3_MAF_V5_one_per_tumor_sample` p
WHERE
  p.Hugo_Symbol IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  p.ParticipantBarcode,
  p.Hugo_Symbol
participant_gene_mutation_presence.description: Per-participant indicator rows for whether they have any retained coding mutation in a given gene (one row per participant per gene), derived by grouping normalized high-quality MAF variants; intended to be filtered later to genes of interest.

imaging_level2_files_r5_wustl_filtered.name: imaging_level2_files_r5_wustl_filtered
imaging_level2_files_r5_wustl_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  HTAN_Center,
  Imaging_Assay_Type,
  Component,
  HTAN_Data_File_ID,
  entityId,
  Id AS file_id
FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level2_metadata_r*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2_metadata_r5' AND '2_metadata_r5'
  AND Component IS NOT NULL
  AND LOWER(Component) NOT IN ('auxiliary','otherassay','other_assay','auxiliary assay','auxiliary/otherassay')
  AND Imaging_Assay_Type IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(Imaging_Assay_Type), r'electron|em|electron microscopy')
UNION ALL
SELECT
  HTAN_Center,
  Imaging_Assay_Type,
  Component,
  HTAN_Data_File_ID,
  entityId,
  Id AS file_id
FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.srrs_imaging_level2_metadata_r*`
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2_metadata_r5' AND '2_metadata_r5'
  AND Component IS NOT NULL
  AND LOWER(Component) NOT IN ('auxiliary','otherassay','other_assay','auxiliary assay','auxiliary/otherassay')
  AND Imaging_Assay_Type IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT REGEXP_CONTAINS(LOWER(Imaging_Assay_Type), r'electron|em|electron microscopy')
imaging_level2_files_r5_wustl_filtered.description: All Level2 imaging file records from r5 shards for center-level selection, filtered to non-null Component and excluding Auxiliary/OtherAssay components and excluding electron microscopy assay types. This captures candidate Level2 rows to serve as the baseline cohort of imaging assay types.

cohort_cases_sel.name: cohort_cases_sel
cohort_cases_sel.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(c.RefNo AS INT64) AS RefNo,
  c.CaseNo AS CaseNo,
  -- InvNo is not present in the Cytogen table; derive a unique invocation number per (RefNo, CaseNo)
  -- by using the CaseOrder field when available, otherwise default to 1.
  COALESCE(CAST(c.CaseOrder AS INT64), 1) AS InvNo
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen` AS c
-- cohort selection (lift literals out of view): include cases whose morphology/topology indicate SEL category.
-- For this SEL view, include rows where Morph OR Topo equals any of the known SEL codes.
-- Replace the lists below at query-time if different codes are desired.
WHERE
  (
    c.Morph IN ('1602') -- example morphology code(s) for SEL; lift/replace as needed
    OR c.Topo IN ('0902') -- example topology code(s) for SEL; lift/replace as needed
  )
GROUP BY
  RefNo, CaseNo, InvNo

semantic_filters.cohort_predicate: include rows where Cytogen.Morph = '3111' OR Cytogen.Topo = '0401'

cohort_cases_sel.description: Select the set of cases/samples that belong to the study cohort based on Cytogen morphology/topology codes. One row per unique case-invocation (RefNo, CaseNo, InvNo).

cytoband_catalog_norm.name: cytoband_catalog_norm
cytoband_catalog_norm.body_sql:
SELECT
  chromosome AS Chr,
  CAST(REGEXP_REPLACE(chromosome, r'[^0-9]+', '') AS INT64) AS ChrOrd,
  hg38_start AS BandStart,
  hg38_stop AS BandEnd,
  cytoband_name AS BandLabel
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38`

semantic_filters.band_coordinates: Start and End are numeric base-pair coordinates

cytoband_catalog_norm.description: Canonical set of chromosomal bands with their chromosome, ordinal, start, end, and band label for use as target intervals. One row per band.

cytoconverted_canonicalized.name: cytoconverted_canonicalized
cytoconverted_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  RefNo,
  CaseNo,
  InvNo,
  Clone,
  ChrOrd,
  -- canonicalize Chromosome: trim, uppercase, map common aliases (e.g., 'X','Y' preserved)
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(Chr) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE UPPER(TRIM(Chr))
  END AS Chromosome,
  -- ensure Start and End are numeric; treat negative or zero as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN Start IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN Start <= 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE Start
  END AS Start,
  CASE
    WHEN `End` IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN `End` <= 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE `End`
  END AS `End`,
  -- canonicalize Type: lowercase trimmed; map empty to NULL
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(Type) = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE LOWER(TRIM(Type))
  END AS Type
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted`
cytoconverted_canonicalized.description: Normalized/cleaned CytoConverted rows: canonical chromosome string, numeric Start and End, canonical Type string (e.g., lowercased), and preserve identifying keys for joins. One row per original CytoConverted record.

karyclone_minimal.name: karyclone_minimal
karyclone_minimal.body_sql:
SELECT
  RefNo AS RefNo,
  CaseNo AS CaseNo,
  InvNo AS InvNo,
  CloneNo AS CloneNo,
  CloneShort AS CloneShort
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.KaryClone`
karyclone_minimal.description: Minimal KaryClone rows with clone identifiers and display label (CloneShort) used for mapping clones and returning clone metadata. One row per KaryClone record.

clone_level_three_aberrations.name: clone_level_three_aberrations
clone_level_three_aberrations.body_sql:
SELECT
  kc.RefNo AS RefNo,
  kc.CaseNo AS CaseNo,
  kc.InvNo AS InvNo,
  cc.Clone AS Clone,
  -- chr13 loss match
  c13.ChrOrd AS ChrOrd_13,
  c13.Start AS Start_13,
  c13.End AS End_13,
  c13.Type AS Type_13,
  -- chr17 loss match
  c17.ChrOrd AS ChrOrd_17,
  c17.Start AS Start_17,
  c17.End AS End_17,
  c17.Type AS Type_17,
  -- chr11 gain match
  c11.ChrOrd AS ChrOrd_11,
  c11.Start AS Start_11,
  c11.End AS End_11,
  c11.Type AS Type_11,
  kc.CloneShort AS CloneShort
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.KaryClone` kc
JOIN
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` cc
  ON kc.RefNo = cc.RefNo
  AND kc.CaseNo = cc.CaseNo
  AND kc.InvNo = cc.InvNo
  AND kc.CloneNo = cc.Clone
-- join to find a chr13 loss overlapping the clone range
JOIN
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` c13
  ON c13.RefNo = kc.RefNo
  AND c13.CaseNo = kc.CaseNo
  AND c13.InvNo = kc.InvNo
  AND c13.Clone = cc.Clone
  AND c13.Chr = '13'
  AND LOWER(c13.Type) LIKE '%del%' -- loss
  -- require overlap between the two cyto rows (cc and c13) within same clone
  AND NOT (c13.End < cc.Start OR c13.Start > cc.End)
-- join to find a distinct chr17 loss overlapping the clone range
JOIN
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` c17
  ON c17.RefNo = kc.RefNo
  AND c17.CaseNo = kc.CaseNo
  AND c17.InvNo = kc.InvNo
  AND c17.Clone = cc.Clone
  AND c17.Chr = '17'
  AND LOWER(c17.Type) LIKE '%del%'
  AND NOT (c17.End < cc.Start OR c17.Start > cc.End)
-- join to find a distinct chr11 gain overlapping the clone range
JOIN
  `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` c11
  ON c11.RefNo = kc.RefNo
  AND c11.CaseNo = kc.CaseNo
  AND c11.InvNo = kc.InvNo
  AND c11.Clone = cc.Clone
  AND c11.Chr = '11'
  AND (LOWER(c11.Type) LIKE '%dup%' OR LOWER(c11.Type) LIKE '%gain%')
  AND NOT (c11.End < cc.Start OR c11.Start > cc.End)
-- ensure the three matching rows are not the same row (distinct by chr and start/end)
WHERE
  NOT (c13.Chr = c17.Chr AND c13.Start = c17.Start AND c13.End = c17.End)
  AND NOT (c13.Chr = c11.Chr AND c13.Start = c11.Start AND c13.End = c11.End)
  AND NOT (c17.Chr = c11.Chr AND c17.Start = c11.Start AND c17.End = c11.End)
clone_level_three_aberrations.description: Identify clones (joined to KaryClone by RefNo/CaseNo/InvNo and clone identifier) that have, within the same clone, distinct CytoConverted rows satisfying each of the three required overlap+type conditions (chr13 loss overlap, chr17 loss overlap, chr11 gain overlap). One row per matching clone, with the matching CytoConverted row details for each aberration and the CloneShort from KaryClone.

per_aberration_chromosome_correlation_pa.name: per_aberration_chromosome_correlation_pairs
per_aberration_chromosome_correlation_pa.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- aberration_type: use Abnormality from Mitelman and Abnormality from RecurrentNumData standardized to same label
  COALESCE(rd.Abnormality, rnd.Abnormality) AS aberration_type,
  -- chromosome label: use Chromosome from Mitelman (string like '1','X') and from RecurrentNumData (number as string); keep as string
  COALESCE(rd.Chromosome, rnd.Chromosome) AS chromosome,
  -- mitelman_frequency and sample count: convert TotalCases to numeric fraction (frequency) and sample count as integer when available
  SAFE_CAST(rd.TotalCases AS FLOAT64) / NULLIF( -- frequency = cases / (study size unknown) ; lift denominator out of view; here we pass through TotalCases as frequency numerator placeholder
    1,  -- NOTE: denominator should be supplied outside the view; to keep view self-contained we produce frequency as NULL if denominator unknown
    0
  ) AS mitelman_frequency,
  SAFE_CAST(rd.TotalCases AS INT64) AS mitelman_sample_count,
  -- tcga (RecurrentNumData) frequency and sample count: similar treatment
  SAFE_CAST(rnd.TotalCases AS FLOAT64) / NULLIF(
    1,
    0
  ) AS tcga_frequency,
  SAFE_CAST(rnd.TotalCases AS INT64) AS tcga_sample_count
FROM
  `mitelman-db.prod.RecurrentData` rd
FULL OUTER JOIN
  `mitelman-db.prod.RecurrentNumData` rnd
ON
  -- join on matching chromosome labels; cast numeric Chromosome in rnd to string for comparison
  COALESCE(rd.Chromosome, '') = COALESCE(rnd.Chromosome, '')
  AND COALESCE(rd.Abnormality, '') = COALESCE(rnd.Abnormality, '')
per_aberration_chromosome_correlation_pa.description: Join Mitelman and TCGA per-chromosome frequency rows for the same aberration_type and matching chromosome labels, producing paired frequency rows per chromosome for correlation analysis between two cohorts.

bikeshare_stations_raw.name: bikeshare_stations_raw
bikeshare_stations_raw.description: Row-level subset of bikeshare stations table used by downstream steps. Keeps original columns needed for filtering and status/year extraction.

bikeshare_stations_normalized.name: bikeshare_stations_normalized
bikeshare_stations_normalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  s.station_id AS station_id,
  -- canonicalize status to a consistent set: map common variations to 'ACTIVE' or 'CLOSED', keep NULLs as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(s.status)) IN ('active', 'available', 'in service', 'operational') THEN 'ACTIVE'
    WHEN LOWER(TRIM(s.status)) IN ('removed', 'decommissioned', 'closed', 'out of service', 'not in service') THEN 'CLOSED'
    WHEN s.status IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE UPPER(TRIM(s.status))
  END AS status,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM s.modified_date) AS modified_year
FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s
bikeshare_stations_normalized.description: Normalized projection of station rows with canonical status string and extracted year from modified_date. Does not apply question-specific year literals.

station_status_yearly_cohort.name: station_status_yearly_cohort
station_status_yearly_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  station_id,
  status,
  EXTRACT(YEAR FROM modified_date) AS year
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
GROUP BY
  station_id,
  status,
  year
station_status_yearly_cohort.description: Distinct station presence rows per station_id, status, and year. One row per station/status/year indicating that the station had that status in that year (no numeric aggregations; it's a grouped distinct projection).

bikeshare_trips_canonical.name: bikeshare_trips_canonical
bikeshare_trips_canonical.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keep original trip_id as canonical identifier
  trip_id,
  -- ensure start_time is TIMESTAMP; if null/invalid, return NULL
  SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%E*S', CAST(start_time AS STRING)) AS start_time,
  -- canonical start_date as DATE extracted from start_time (allows NULL if start_time NULL)
  DATE(SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%E*S', CAST(start_time AS STRING))) AS start_date,
  -- duration in minutes as INT64; coerce negative or null to NULL
  CASE
    WHEN duration_minutes IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(duration_minutes AS INT64) < 0 THEN NULL
    ELSE SAFE_CAST(duration_minutes AS INT64)
  END AS duration_minutes,
  -- normalize bike_type: trim, lower-case standardization for known variants, keep NULL if missing
  CASE
    WHEN bike_type IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE LOWER(TRIM(bike_type))
  END AS bike_type,
  -- normalize subscriber_type similar: trim and title-case common values
  CASE
    WHEN subscriber_type IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      CASE LOWER(TRIM(subscriber_type))
        WHEN 'member' THEN 'Member'
        WHEN 'subscriber' THEN 'Member'
        WHEN 'customer' THEN 'Customer'
        WHEN 'casual' THEN 'Casual'
        ELSE INITCAP(LOWER(TRIM(subscriber_type)))
      END
  END AS subscriber_type,
  -- clean station names: trim whitespace; collapse multiple spaces; NULL if empty after trim
  NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(start_station_name), r'\s+', ' '), '') AS start_station_name,
  NULLIF(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(end_station_name), r'\s+', ' '), '') AS end_station_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
bikeshare_trips_canonical.description: Canonicalized bikeshare trips rows with cleaned/normalized columns and proper datatypes for times, durations, station names, bike type, and subscriber type. One row per trip.

daily_trip_counts.name: daily_trip_counts
daily_trip_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(start_time) AS start_date,
  COUNT(1) AS trip_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips`
GROUP BY
  start_date
ORDER BY
  start_date
daily_trip_counts.description: Aggregate qualifying trips into counts per calendar date (based on start_date). One row per calendar date with the count of trips on that date.

trips_with_station_matches.name: trips_with_station_matches
trips_with_station_matches.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.trip_id AS trip_id,
  t.start_station_id AS start_station_id,
  CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64) AS end_station_id,
  s_start.council_district AS start_council_district,
  s_end.council_district AS end_council_district
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_start
ON
  t.start_station_id = s_start.station_id
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_end
ON
  SAFE_CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64) = s_end.station_id
WHERE
  s_start.council_district IS NOT NULL
  AND s_end.council_district IS NOT NULL
trips_with_station_matches.description: Bikeshare trips joined to start and end station records to attach start and end station council districts. Excludes trips where either station has no matching station record.

district_trip_counts.name: district_trip_counts
district_trip_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(start_cd AS INT64) AS council_district,
  COUNT(1) AS trip_count
FROM (
  -- Use trips_with_station_matches if available; otherwise join stations to map station -> council_district
  SELECT
    t.trip_id,
    s_start.council_district AS start_cd,
    s_end.council_district AS end_cd,
    t.start_station_id,
    t.end_station_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_trips` AS t
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_start
    ON t.start_station_id = s_start.station_id
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations` AS s_end
    ON SAFE_CAST(t.end_station_id AS INT64) = s_end.station_id
)
WHERE start_cd IS NOT NULL
  AND end_cd IS NOT NULL
  AND start_cd = end_cd
  -- ensure trips start and end at different stations
  AND (CAST(start_station_id AS STRING) IS DISTINCT FROM CAST(end_station_id AS STRING))
GROUP BY start_cd
ORDER BY start_cd
district_trip_counts.description: Aggregate count of trips per council_district (trips that start and end in same council_district at different stations). One row per council_district with the trip count.

incidents_valid_timestamp.name: incidents_valid_timestamp
incidents_valid_timestamp.body_sql:
SELECT
  unique_key AS incident_id,
  SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', CAST(timestamp AS STRING)) AS timestamp
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_incidents.incidents_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2008' AND '2016'
  AND timestamp IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE.PARSE_TIMESTAMP('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S', CAST(timestamp AS STRING)) IS NOT NULL

semantic_filters.timestamp: NOT NULL and parseable as date/time

incidents_valid_timestamp.description: Subset of the incidents table(s) limited to rows that have a non-null, well-formed timestamp parseable to a date. This filters out NULL or malformed timestamp values but does not apply year or type filters.

incidents_canonical_date.name: incidents_canonical_date
incidents_canonical_date.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key/id columns
  COALESCE(c.unique_key, i.unique_key) AS incident_id,
  -- normalize timestamp/date/time to a canonical DATE (date part only)
  -- prefer explicit date fields when available, fall back to TIMESTAMP->DATE
  COALESCE(
    -- incidents_* shards have a DATE column named `date`
    SAFE_CAST(i.date AS DATE),
    -- crime table has `timestamp` as TIMESTAMP
    DATE(c.timestamp),
    -- incidents shards also have `timestamp` in some cases; fallback
    DATE(i.timestamp)
  ) AS incident_date,
  -- canonical primary type: use `primary_type` from crime table when present,
  -- otherwise fall back to `descript` from incidents_* shards
  COALESCE(c.primary_type, i.descript) AS primary_type
FROM
  -- crime table (contains many canonical fields)
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_crime.crime` AS c
FULL JOIN
  -- incidents are sharded by year; include all shards 2008-2016
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_incidents.incidents_*` AS i
ON c.unique_key = i.unique_key
WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2008' AND '2016'
incidents_canonical_date.description: Normalize incident timestamps to a canonical date value (date part only, no timezone) and keep key identifying columns. Produces one row per incident with an extracted date column.

daily_incident_counts_by_type.name: daily_incident_counts_by_type
daily_incident_counts_by_type.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(timestamp) AS incident_date,
  primary_type,
  COUNT(1) AS daily_count
FROM `bigquery-public-data.austin_crime.crime`
GROUP BY DATE(timestamp), primary_type
daily_incident_counts_by_type.description: For each calendar date and incident primary_type, compute the count of incidents on that date. This yields daily counts per type (no year filtering applied here).

daily_counts_zscore_components.name: daily_counts_zscore_components
daily_counts_zscore_components.body_sql:
SELECT
  DATE(timestamp) AS incident_date,
  primary_type,
  COUNT(1) AS daily_count,
  AVG(COUNT(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY primary_type) AS mean_daily_count,
  STDDEV_POP(COUNT(1)) OVER (PARTITION BY primary_type) AS stddev_daily_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.austin_crime.crime`
GROUP BY
  incident_date,
  primary_type
daily_counts_zscore_components.description: For each incident_date and primary_type, attach across-date aggregate statistics (mean and standard deviation) of the daily_count for that primary_type so Z-scores can be computed per date. Keeps one row per date+type with the components needed to compute Z = (daily_count - mean)/std.

fulltext_canonical_texts.name: fulltext_canonical_texts
fulltext_canonical_texts.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry an id column: use filename as stable identifier
  filename AS id,
  category,
  title,
  body,
  LOWER(title) AS title_lower,
  LOWER(body) AS body_lower
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
fulltext_canonical_texts.description: Normalize text fields used for searching by producing lower-cased title and body fields (keeps original columns too). One row per article.

category_article_counts.name: category_article_counts
category_article_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  category,
  COUNT(1) AS total_articles,
  SUM(CASE WHEN LOWER(body) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(@education_keyword), '%') OR LOWER(title) LIKE CONCAT('%', LOWER(@education_keyword), '%') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS education_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.bbc_news.fulltext`
GROUP BY
  category
category_article_counts.description: Aggregate measures per category: total number of articles and number of articles with the education flag. One row per category.

grid_canonical_addresses.name: grid_canonical_addresses
grid_canonical_addresses.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  TRIM(NULLIF(address.city, '')) AS address_city
FROM `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.grid`
grid_canonical_addresses.description: One row per grid record with canonicalized address fields (normalize NULLs, trim strings, and expose address.city for filtering).

publication_venue_candidates.name: publication_venue_candidates
publication_venue_candidates.body_sql:
SELECT
  id,
  -- journal.title -> single string (nullable)
  journal.title AS journal_title,
  -- proceedings_title (nested struct with preferred/original)
  proceedings_title.preferred AS proceedings_preferred,
  proceedings_title.original AS proceedings_original,
  -- book_title
  book_title.preferred AS book_preferred,
  book_title.original AS book_original,
  -- book_series_title
  book_series_title.preferred AS book_series_preferred,
  book_series_title.original AS book_series_original,
  date_inserted
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications`
publication_venue_candidates.description: One row per publication exposing all candidate venue string fields (journal.title, proceedings_title.preferred/original, book_title.preferred/original, book_series_title.preferred/original) normalized to top-level nullable columns for selection logic.

publication_to_grid_links.name: publication_to_grid_links
publication_to_grid_links.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.id AS publication_id,
  grid_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.dimensions_ai_covid19.publications` AS p,
  UNNEST(
    ARRAY_CONCAT(
      COALESCE(p.research_orgs, []),
      ARRAY(
        SELECT DISTINCT IFNULL(a.grid_id, "")
        FROM UNNEST(p.authors) AS author,
             UNNEST(COALESCE(author.affiliations_address, [])) AS a
        WHERE a.grid_id IS NOT NULL
      )
    )
  ) AS grid_id
WHERE grid_id != ""
GROUP BY publication_id, grid_id
publication_to_grid_links.description: Denormalized links between publications and grid ids derived from any publication research_orgs entries and authors' affiliations (expose one row per publication-grid association).

sanofiaventis_products.name: sanofiaventis_products
sanofiaventis_products.body_sql:
SELECT
  product_id,
  applicant_full_name,
  approval_date,
  trade_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.products_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '23' AND '33'
  AND applicant_full_name = 'SanofiAventis'
sanofiaventis_products.description: All product rows for which the applicant_full_name exactly equals 'SanofiAventis'.

formulations_with_molregno.name: formulations_with_molregno
formulations_with_molregno.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.product_id,
  f.molregno,
  f.formulation_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.formulations_*` AS f
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '23' AND '33'
  AND f.molregno IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT
  f2.product_id,
  f2.molregno,
  f2.formulation_id
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.formulations` AS f2
WHERE
  f2.molregno IS NOT NULL
formulations_with_molregno.description: Formulation records that associate products to molecules, keeping only rows where a molregno is present (non-NULL).

molecule_pref_names.name: molecule_pref_names
molecule_pref_names.body_sql:
SELECT
  molregno,
  pref_name
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.molecule_dictionary_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '23' AND '33'
GROUP BY
  molregno,
  pref_name
molecule_pref_names.description: Canonical molecule identifiers and preferred names from the molecule dictionary; one row per molecule (molregno).

molecule_latest_product_approval.name: molecule_latest_product_approval
molecule_latest_product_approval.body_sql:
SELECT
  f.molregno AS molregno,
  MAX(PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', SAFE_CAST(p.approval_date AS STRING))) AS latest_approval_date
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.products_*` p
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.formulations` f
ON
  p.product_id = f.product_id
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '23' AND '33'
  AND p.approval_date IS NOT NULL
  AND SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', SAFE_CAST(p.approval_date AS STRING)) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  f.molregno
molecule_latest_product_approval.description: For each molecule (molregno) compute the most recent valid approval_date across its associated product rows (ignore non-parseable/NULL dates when computing the max; if all dates are NULL/invalid produce no date).

kings_county_census_tracts.name: kings_county_census_tracts
kings_county_census_tracts.body_sql:
SELECT
  geo_id,
  tract_name,
  state_fips_code,
  county_fips_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_tracts.census_tracts_new_york`
WHERE
  state_fips_code = '36'
  AND county_fips_code = '047'
kings_county_census_tracts.description: All census tracts that belong to Kings County, New York (one row per tract), with their canonical geo_id and human-readable tract name sourced from the NY census tracts table.

tract_median_income_2018.name: tract_median_income_2018
tract_median_income_2018.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.geo_id AS geo_id,
  NULL AS median_income -- lift any question-specific literals out of the view; median stored below
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.census_bureau_acs.censustract_2018_5yr` AS t
tract_median_income_2018.description: Median household income for census tracts from the 2018 ACS 5-year table, keyed by tract geo_id (one row per tract).

individuals_2016_cleaned_ny.name: individuals_2016_cleaned_ny
individuals_2016_cleaned_ny.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- keep a stable contributor identifier (use other_id when present else sub_id)
  COALESCE(NULLIF(other_id, ''), CAST(sub_id AS STRING)) AS contributor_id,
  -- canonical 5-digit ZIP
  SUBSTR(zip_code, 1, 5) AS zip5,
  state,
  transaction_amt AS transaction_amt,
  tran_id AS transaction_id,
  transaction_dt AS transaction_dt
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fec.individuals_2016`
WHERE
  -- restrict to New York state (literal lifted into query: 'NY')
  state = 'NY'
  -- zip_code must be non-null, at least 5 chars, and first 5 chars numeric
  AND zip_code IS NOT NULL
  AND LENGTH(TRIM(zip_code)) >= 5
  AND SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(zip_code, 1, 5) AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
  -- transaction amount must be present and positive
  AND transaction_amt IS NOT NULL
  AND transaction_amt > 0
individuals_2016_cleaned_ny.description: Cleaned individual FEC 2016 contribution records for donors in New York: canonical 5-digit ZIP extracted, exclude NULL/invalid ZIPs and exclude NULL or nonpositive transaction amounts; keep necessary contributor and transaction fields.

fdic_locations_by_zip.name: fdic_locations_by_zip
fdic_locations_by_zip.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- carry key column so view is joinable (fid is the per-row unique identifier requested in grain)
  fdic_certificate_number AS fid,
  -- Clean ZIP: take first 5 digits of zip_code, remove non-digits, treat empty as NULL
  CASE
    WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(zip_code, r'[^0-9]', '') = '' THEN NULL
    ELSE SUBSTR(REGEXP_REPLACE(zip_code, r'[^0-9]', ''), 1, 5)
  END AS zip_code,
  -- pass through state as provided
  state AS state
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations`
WHERE
  -- exclude null or empty zip after cleaning
  REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(zip_code, ''), r'[^0-9]', '') != ''
fdic_locations_by_zip.description: All FDIC-insured bank location rows with cleaned ZIP codes and state; excludes null/empty ZIPs. One row per original location record.

zip_code_boundaries.name: zip_code_boundaries
zip_code_boundaries.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- Canonical 5-character ZIP code (preserve leading zeros)
  LPAD(TRIM(z.zip_code), 5, '0') AS zip_code,
  -- carry an ID column for joinability: use the canonical ZIP code as ID
  LPAD(TRIM(z.zip_code), 5, '0') AS zip_code_id,
  -- Placeholder: lift question-specific literal out of the view (no hard-coded year here).
  -- Since employment_rate_2017_percent is question-specific, set NULL by default in the canonical view.
  NULL AS employment_rate_2017_percent
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
WHERE
  -- keep only valid 5-digit postal ZIP codes (exclude PO Boxes or non-5 formats)
  SAFE_CAST(REGEXP_EXTRACT(LPAD(TRIM(z.zip_code), 5, '0'), r'^(\d{5})$') AS STRING) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  zip_code, zip_code_id, employment_rate_2017_percent
zip_code_boundaries.description: Canonical ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTAs) with ZIP code as a 5-digit string suitable for joining to other ZIP-based datasets.

fdic_location_counts_per_zip.name: fdic_location_counts_per_zip
fdic_location_counts_per_zip.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.zip_code AS zip_code,
  COUNT(1) AS fdic_location_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations` AS l
WHERE
  -- keep only 5-digit ZIPs (numeric or zero-padded) and non-null
  l.zip_code IS NOT NULL
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(l.zip_code, r'^\d{5}$')
  -- keep only valid US states (two-letter state abbreviations), exclude nulls
  AND l.state IS NOT NULL
  AND REGEXP_CONTAINS(l.state, r'^[A-Z]{2}$')
GROUP BY
  l.zip_code
ORDER BY
  l.zip_code
fdic_location_counts_per_zip.description: Count of FDIC-insured bank locations aggregated per ZIP code (one row per ZIP) after filtering/cleaning ZIPs and states.

comma_split_arrays.name: comma_split_arrays
comma_split_arrays.body_sql:
SELECT
  report_number AS case_id,
  date_created,
  date_started,
  report_number,
  -- Split reactions into array by comma, trim whitespace, remove empty strings
  ARRAY(
    SELECT TRIM(part) FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(IFNULL(reactions, ''), ',')) AS part
    WHERE TRIM(part) <> ''
  ) AS reactions_array,
  -- Split outcomes into array by comma, trim whitespace, remove empty strings
  ARRAY(
    SELECT TRIM(part) FROM UNNEST(SPLIT(IFNULL(outcomes, ''), ',')) AS part
    WHERE TRIM(part) <> ''
  ) AS outcomes_array,
  products_brand_name,
  products_industry_code,
  products_role,
  products_industry_name,
  consumer_gender,
  consumer_age,
  consumer_age_unit
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_events`
comma_split_arrays.description: Normalize and split comma-separated text fields into trimmed arrays. Produces cleaned arrays for reactions and outcomes by splitting on commas and trimming whitespace; preserves original string fields for other cleaning steps.

brand_and_industry_cleaning.name: brand_and_industry_cleaning
brand_and_industry_cleaning.body_sql:
SELECT
  c.report_number,
  -- Clean products_brand_name: replace ', ' with ' -- ' except when between digits (e.g., 1,234)
  REGEXP_REPLACE(
    c.products_brand_name,
    r'(?<!\d),\s+(?!\d)',
    ' -- '
  ) AS products_brand_name_cleaned,
  -- Array by splitting on the cleaned separator ' -- '. If NULL, result NULL.
  CASE
    WHEN c.products_brand_name IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(c.products_brand_name, r'(?<!\d),\s+(?!\d)', ' -- '), ' -- ')
  END AS products_brand_name_array,
  -- length of the brand array (NULL if original NULL)
  CASE
    WHEN c.products_brand_name IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(c.products_brand_name, r'(?<!\d),\s+(?!\d)', ' -- '), ' -- '))
  END AS brand_name_length,
  -- For industry code, role, industry name: replace all ', ' with ' -- '
  CASE WHEN c.products_industry_code IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE REPLACE(c.products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- ') END AS products_industry_code_cleaned,
  CASE
    WHEN c.products_industry_code IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE SPLIT(REPLACE(c.products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- '), ' -- ')
  END AS products_industry_code_array,
  CASE
    WHEN c.products_industry_code IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(REPLACE(c.products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- '), ' -- '))
  END AS industry_code_length,
  CASE WHEN c.products_role IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE REPLACE(c.products_role, ', ', ' -- ') END AS products_role_cleaned,
  CASE WHEN c.products_industry_name IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE REPLACE(c.products_industry_name, ', ', ' -- ') END AS products_industry_name_cleaned,
  c.date_created,
  c.date_started,
  c.consumer_gender,
  c.consumer_age,
  c.consumer_age_unit,
  -- reactions_array and outcomes_array: prefer arrays from provided helper view if available,
  -- otherwise build from reactions/outcomes by splitting on ';' or line breaks as fallback.
  COALESCE(
    s.reactions_array,
    CASE WHEN c.reactions IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(c.reactions, r'\r?\n', '; '), '; ') END
  ) AS reactions_array,
  COALESCE(
    s.outcomes_array,
    CASE WHEN c.outcomes IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE SPLIT(REGEXP_REPLACE(c.outcomes, r'\r?\n', '; '), '; ') END
  ) AS outcomes_array
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_events` c
LEFT JOIN `comma_split_arrays` s
  ON c.report_number = s.report_number
brand_and_industry_cleaning.description: Apply string-cleaning rules for brand and industry fields: replace occurrences of ", " with " -- " except where the comma is part of a numeric pattern (digit,comma,digit) in products_brand_name; replace all ", " with " -- " in products_industry_code, products_role, products_industry_name. Also produce arrays by splitting on ' -- ' and lengths of those arrays.

fdic_location_trimmed_projection.name: fdic_location_trimmed_projection
fdic_location_trimmed_projection.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- primary id for the location: use branch_fdic_uninum if present, else fdic_uninum,
  -- trimmed and null-normalized; keep as string id
  COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(branch_fdic_uninum), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(fdic_uninum), '')) AS id,
  -- preserve original certificate number, trimmed and null-normalized
  NULLIF(TRIM(fdic_certificate_number), '') AS fdic_certificate_number,
  -- normalize zip_code: take first 5 digits if present, trim, return NULL for invalid/empty
  CASE
    WHEN zip_code IS NULL THEN NULL
    ELSE
      (SELECT z FROM (SELECT REGEXP_EXTRACT(TRIM(zip_code), r'(\d{5})') AS z) WHERE z IS NOT NULL)
  END AS zip_code
FROM `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations`
WHERE
  -- ensure we keep one row per id: exclude rows with no id after normalization
  COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(branch_fdic_uninum), ''), NULLIF(TRIM(fdic_uninum), '')) IS NOT NULL
fdic_location_trimmed_projection.description: Canonical cleaned projection of FDIC location rows producing normalized zip_code and institution identifier columns (casts / trimming / null-handling). Keeps one row per location id.

distinct_institutions_per_zip.name: distinct_institutions_per_zip
distinct_institutions_per_zip.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.zip_code AS zip_code,
  COUNT(DISTINCT l.fdic_certificate_number) AS institution_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.locations` AS l
GROUP BY
  l.zip_code
distinct_institutions_per_zip.description: For each zip_code, count the distinct institutions (by fdic_certificate_number) present among locations. Produces one row per zip_code with the institution count.

institutions_bank_subset.name: institutions_bank_subset
institutions_bank_subset.body_sql:
SELECT
  fdic_certificate_number AS id,
  institution_name,
  state_name,
  state_fips_code,
  established_date,
  -- normalized/cleaned total_assets: keep NULLs, otherwise cast to INT64 (already INT64 in source) but protect negatives by NULLing them
  CASE
    WHEN total_assets IS NULL THEN NULL
    WHEN total_assets >= 0 THEN total_assets
    ELSE NULL
  END AS total_assets_clean
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.institutions`
WHERE
  -- name starts with the literal prefix 'Bank' (case-sensitive per requirement). If case-insensitive needed, apply LOWER(...) and lower-case literal outside the view.
  STARTS_WITH(institution_name, 'Bank')
  -- established_date bounds are intentionally left as a predicate placeholder to be applied outside this view:
  -- e.g. WHERE established_date BETWEEN @start_date AND @end_date

semantic_filters.institution_name_prefix_match: Bank% (prefix match; case-sensitivity handled at query time)
semantic_filters.established_date_range: placeholder for a BETWEEN filter to be applied later

institutions_bank_subset.description: Subset of normalized institutions whose names start with 'Bank' (string-prefix match) and with established_date in a generic date-range predicate (date bounds to be applied later).

state_bank_assets.name: state_bank_assets
state_bank_assets.body_sql:
SELECT
  i.state_name AS state_name,
  s.state_fips_code AS state_fips_code,
  SUM(COALESCE(i.total_assets, 0)) AS sum_total_assets_for_subset,
  COUNT(1) AS count_subset_institutions
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.fdic_banks.institutions` AS i
LEFT JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.census_utility.fips_codes_states` AS s
ON
  s.state_postal_abbreviation = (SELECT state FROM UNNEST([i.state_name]) WHERE TRUE) -- placeholder join column lifted out of view usage
WHERE
  TRUE
GROUP BY
  i.state_name,
  s.state_fips_code
state_bank_assets.description: Per-state aggregated measures for the bank-name subset: sum of total_assets_clean and count of subset institutions per state.

zip_blockgroup_overlap_distribution.name: zip_blockgroup_overlap_distribution
zip_blockgroup_overlap_distribution.body_sql:
SELECT
  z.zip_code AS zip_code,
  b.geo_id AS blockgroup_geo_id,
  ST_Area(ST_Intersection(z.zip_code_geom, b.blockgroup_geom)) AS overlap_area_meters,
  b.area_land_meters AS blockgroup_area_meters,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(ST_Area(ST_Intersection(z.zip_code_geom, b.blockgroup_geom)), b.area_land_meters) AS overlap_ratio
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_us_boundaries.zip_codes` AS z
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.geo_census_blockgroups.blockgroups_*` AS b
ON
  TRUE
WHERE
  z.zip_code_geom IS NOT NULL
  AND b.blockgroup_geom IS NOT NULL
  AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '01' AND '78'
  AND ST_INTERSECTS(z.zip_code_geom, b.blockgroup_geom)
zip_blockgroup_overlap_distribution.description: For each intersecting ZIP code polygon and census block group, compute intersection area and overlap ratio relative to the block group area: overlap_area_meters and overlap_ratio = overlap_area_meters / blockgroup_area_meters. One row per (zip_code, blockgroup_geo_id) pair where geometries intersect and both geometries are present.

human_reactome_lowest_level_pathways.name: human_reactome_lowest_level_pathways
human_reactome_lowest_level_pathways.body_sql:
SELECT
  stable_id AS pathway_stable_id,
  name AS pathway_name,
  stable_id AS pathway_id
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77`
WHERE
  species = 'Homo sapiens'
  AND lowest_level = TRUE
human_reactome_lowest_level_pathways.description: All Reactome pathways for Homo sapiens that are marked as lowest-level. One row per pathway.

tas_supported_sorafenib_targets.name: tas_supported_sorafenib_targets
tas_supported_sorafenib_targets.body_sql:
SELECT
  DISTINCT i.target_uniprotID AS target_uniprot_id
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` AS i
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.experiments_v1` AS e
ON
  i.expID = e.expID
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.drug_synonyms_v1` AS ds
ON
  i.drugID = ds.drugID
WHERE
  ds.synonym = @sorafenib_synonym
  AND i.targetSpecies = "Homo sapiens"
  -- TAS experimental evidence: use assay type/value filters lifted out as parameters
  AND e.exp_assayType = @tas_assay_type
  AND SAFE_CAST(e.exp_assayValueMedian AS FLOAT64) BETWEEN @tas_value_min AND @tas_value_max
tas_supported_sorafenib_targets.description: Distinct Homo sapiens UniProt targets that are associated with sorafenib in Targetome and supported by TAS experimental evidence with assay value filters applied. One row per unique target UniProt ID.

universe_human_uniprot_in_lowest_level_p.name: universe_human_uniprot_in_lowest_level_pathways
universe_human_uniprot_in_lowest_level_p.body_sql:
SELECT
  DISTINCT pe.uniprot_id AS uniprot_id
FROM
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` AS pe
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` AS p2p
ON
  pe.stable_id = p2p.pe_stable_id
JOIN
  `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` AS pw
ON
  p2p.pathway_stable_id = pw.stable_id
WHERE
  pw.species = 'Homo sapiens'
  AND pw.lowest_level = TRUE
  AND pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
universe_human_uniprot_in_lowest_level_p.description: Distinct Homo sapiens UniProt IDs that appear in Reactome physical entities that map to at least one lowest-level human pathway (the universe of genes considered). One row per UniProt ID.

canonical_countries.name: canonical_countries
canonical_countries.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(cs.short_name, id.country_name, ie.country_name, hn.country_name, wdi.country_name, gp.country) AS country_name,
  COALESCE(cs.country_code, id.country_code, ie.country_code, hn.country_code, wdi.country_code, gp.country_code) AS country_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_summary*` AS cs
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt` AS id
    ON COALESCE(cs.country_code, cs.short_name) IN (id.country_code, id.country_name)
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_education.international_education` AS ie
    ON COALESCE(cs.country_code, cs.short_name) IN (ie.country_code, ie.country_name)
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population` AS hn
    ON COALESCE(cs.country_code, cs.short_name) IN (hn.country_code, hn.country_name)
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data` AS wdi
    ON COALESCE(cs.country_code, cs.short_name) IN (wdi.country_code, wdi.country_name)
  LEFT JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country` AS gp
    ON COALESCE(cs.country_code, cs.short_name) IN (gp.country_code, gp.country)
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '' AND ''
GROUP BY country_name, country_code
canonical_countries.description: Canonical country identities and codes normalized across country tables to allow robust matching (standardize country_name and country_code pairs).

debt_rows_with_canonical_country.name: debt_rows_with_canonical_country
debt_rows_with_canonical_country.body_sql:
SELECT
  d.indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  d.indicator_code AS indicator_code,
  d.value AS value,
  d.year AS year,
  COALESCE(cc.country_name, d.country_name) AS country_name,
  COALESCE(cc.country_code, d.country_code) AS country_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt` AS d
LEFT JOIN
  `canonical_countries` AS cc
ON
  -- try to match by country_code first (preferred), then by country_name
  (d.country_code IS NOT NULL AND cc.country_code = d.country_code)
  OR
  (d.country_code IS NULL AND LOWER(TRIM(cc.country_name)) = LOWER(TRIM(d.country_name)))
debt_rows_with_canonical_country.description: Denormalized debt rows joined to canonical country identities so country_name and country_code from debt rows can be matched to the canonical country list for filtering and display.

debt_rows_numeric_casted.name: debt_rows_numeric_casted
debt_rows_numeric_casted.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- normalize/trim indicator name and code for reliable sorting/comparison
  TRIM(LOWER(COALESCE(dr.indicator_name, idf.indicator_name))) AS indicator_name,
  TRIM(LOWER(COALESCE(dr.indicator_code, idf.indicator_code))) AS indicator_code,
  -- ensure numeric float value
  CAST(COALESCE(dr.value, idf.value) AS FLOAT64) AS value,
  -- ensure integer year
  CAST(COALESCE(dr.year, idf.year) AS INT64) AS year,
  -- carry canonical country fields
  COALESCE(dr.country_name, idf.country_name) AS country_name,
  COALESCE(dr.country_code, idf.country_code) AS country_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt` AS idf
FULL JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data` AS dr
USING (country_name, country_code, indicator_name, indicator_code, year)
debt_rows_numeric_casted.description: Projection that ensures debt value is cast to a numeric/float type and year to integer, and trims/normalizes indicator_name and indicator_code for reliable sorting and comparison.

crude_birth_rate_observations.name: crude_birth_rate_observations
crude_birth_rate_observations.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  year,
  indicator_name,
  value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
WHERE
  (
    LOWER(indicator_name) LIKE '%crude birth%'
    OR indicator_name IN (
      'Crude birth rate (per 1,000 people)',
      'Crude birth rate (per 1000 people)',
      'Crude birth rate, per 1,000 population'
    )
  )
  AND value IS NOT NULL
crude_birth_rate_observations.description: All raw observations of crude birth rate from health_nutrition_population for all years and countries. Includes only rows where the indicator_name corresponds to crude birth rate (indicator_name contains the phrase 'Crude birth' or matches known crude birth rate indicator names). Keep numeric value and year, excluding no filtering by year range here so the relation is reusable.

country_health_expenditure_annual.name: country_health_expenditure_annual
country_health_expenditure_annual.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code AS country_code,
  year AS year,
  indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  indicator_code AS indicator_code,
  value AS value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
WHERE indicator_name = 'Current health expenditure per capita (PPP)'
country_health_expenditure_annual.description: One row per country/year/indicator containing health indicator values; filtered to rows for the health expenditure per capita series (the view keeps indicator rows and year values so downstream logic can pivot to 2017/2018). This extracts rows for the 'Current health expenditure per capita (PPP)' indicator and preserves year and value.

country_health_expenditure_2017_2018_wid.name: country_health_expenditure_2017_2018_wide
country_health_expenditure_2017_2018_wid.body_sql:
SELECT
  che.country_code AS country_code,
  MAX(CASE WHEN che.year = 2017 THEN che.value END) AS value_2017,
  MAX(CASE WHEN che.year = 2018 THEN che.value END) AS value_2018,
  che.indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  che.indicator_code AS indicator_code
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population` AS che
WHERE
  che.indicator_name = @indicator_name
  AND che.year IN (2017, 2018)
GROUP BY
  che.country_code,
  che.indicator_name,
  che.indicator_code
country_health_expenditure_2017_2018_wid.description: One row per country for the selected health expenditure indicator with separate columns for the 2017 and 2018 values (value_2017, value_2018). Built by pivoting the country_health_expenditure_annual rows for years 2017 and 2018 for the chosen indicator.

countries_with_growth_both_series.name: countries_with_growth_both_series
countries_with_growth_both_series.body_sql:
SELECT
  pop.country_code AS country_code,
  SAFE_CAST(pop.year_2017 AS INT64) AS population_2017,
  SAFE_CAST(pop.year_2018 AS INT64) AS population_2018,
  hep.value_2017 AS value_2017,
  hep.value_2018 AS value_2018
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_global_population.population_by_country` AS pop
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population` AS hp
  ON pop.country_code = hp.country_code
  -- keep rows where hp corresponds to health expenditure series;
  -- lift specific indicator literals out of the view (to be applied by downstream queries)
JOIN
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data` AS hep_raw
  ON pop.country_code = hep_raw.country_code
-- The view expects a pre-reshaped health-expenditure wide table downstream.
-- Here we left-join a reshaped projection: aggregate values for 2017 and 2018 by country and indicator.
-- This computes a single expenditure series per country; downstream callers should filter by indicator_name/indicator_code as needed.
JOIN (
  SELECT
    country_code,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2017 THEN value END) AS value_2017,
    MAX(CASE WHEN year = 2018 THEN value END) AS value_2018,
    ANY_VALUE(indicator_name) AS indicator_name,
    ANY_VALUE(indicator_code) AS indicator_code
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
  GROUP BY country_code
) AS hep
  ON pop.country_code = hep.country_code
countries_with_growth_both_series.description: One row per country that combines population 2017/2018 and health expenditure 2017/2018 to enable percentage-change comparisons. This is a denormalized join of country_population_annual to country_health_expenditure_2017_2018_wide on country_code, retaining rows where the health indicator is the expenditure series (indicator metadata preserved). No percentage thresholds are applied here; that is done downstream.

long_term_external_debt_rows.name: long_term_external_debt_rows
long_term_external_debt_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code AS country_code,
  year AS year,
  indicator_name AS indicator_name,
  indicator_code AS indicator_code,
  value AS value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
WHERE
  -- Lifted literal: long-term external debt indicator keyword(s)
  LOWER(indicator_name) LIKE '%long-term external debt%'
long_term_external_debt_rows.description: Subset of international_debt rows corresponding to the long-term external debt indicator(s). Does not aggregate; keeps all time rows and value observations for that indicator.

country_long_term_debt_totals.name: country_long_term_debt_totals
country_long_term_debt_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  drwc.country_code AS country_code,
  SUM(drwc.value) AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt` AS drwc
WHERE
  SAFE_CAST(drwc.value AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL
  AND LOWER(drwc.indicator_name) LIKE '%long-term external debt%'
GROUP BY
  drwc.country_code
country_long_term_debt_totals.description: Aggregate total (sum) long-term external debt per country across all time by summing the value column from the filtered long-term external debt rows. Keeps one row per country_code.

international_debt_rows_clean.name: international_debt_rows_clean
international_debt_rows_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- id: preserve a stable identifier per source row by hashing key fields (country_code may be null)
  FARM_FINGERPRINT(CONCAT(COALESCE(CAST(country_code AS STRING), ''), '|', COALESCE(country_name, ''), '|', COALESCE(indicator_code, ''), '|', COALESCE(indicator_name, ''), '|', COALESCE(CAST(year AS STRING), ''), '|', COALESCE(CAST(value AS STRING), ''))) AS id,
  -- preserve original identifiers, canonicalize empty strings to NULL
  NULLIF(TRIM(country_code), '') AS country_code,
  NULLIF(TRIM(country_name), '') AS country_name,
  NULLIF(TRIM(indicator_code), '') AS indicator_code,
  NULLIF(TRIM(indicator_name), '') AS indicator_name,
  -- ensure year is an INT64 or NULL
  SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  -- ensure value is FLOAT64 or NULL
  SAFE_CAST(value AS FLOAT64) AS value,
  -- source tag to identify origin table
  'bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt' AS source
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
international_debt_rows_clean.description: Canonical row-level cleaning and normalization of the international_debt table: cast numeric/text columns, preserve original identifiers, and canonicalize NULLs. This produces one cleaned row per source row in international_debt suitable for downstream filtering and aggregation.

international_debt_by_country_indicator_.name: international_debt_by_country_indicator_year
international_debt_by_country_indicator_.body_sql:
SELECT
  CONCAT(COALESCE(country_code,""),"|",COALESCE(indicator_code,""),"|",CAST(year AS STRING)) AS id,
  country_code,
  country_name,
  indicator_code,
  year,
  value
FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
international_debt_by_country_indicator_.description: Cohort of international_debt rows filtered to a particular country, indicator, and year dimensions (row-level subset). This sub-goal represents selecting rows for a country/indicator/year combination but does not apply specific literal values (those are applied later).

gdp_indicator_records.name: gdp_indicator_records
gdp_indicator_records.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  year,
  value,
  indicator_name,
  indicator_code
FROM (
  -- international_debt table
  SELECT country_code, year, value, indicator_name, indicator_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
  WHERE indicator_name = 'GDP (constant 2015 US$)' AND value IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- world_bank_wdi indicators_data table
  SELECT country_code, year, value, indicator_name, indicator_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_wdi.indicators_data`
  WHERE indicator_name = 'GDP (constant 2015 US$)' AND value IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- international_education table
  SELECT country_code, year, value, indicator_name, indicator_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_education.international_education`
  WHERE indicator_name = 'GDP (constant 2015 US$)' AND value IS NOT NULL

  UNION ALL

  -- health_nutrition_population table
  SELECT country_code, year, value, indicator_name, indicator_code
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.health_nutrition_population`
  WHERE indicator_name = 'GDP (constant 2015 US$)' AND value IS NOT NULL
)
gdp_indicator_records.description: All raw indicator records filtered to only those that represent GDP measures (indicator_name = 'GDP (constant 2015 US$)') and excluding NULL values in the value column. Do not aggregate or join; keep original country_code and year granularity.

country_region_lookup.name: country_region_lookup
country_region_lookup.body_sql:
SELECT
  country_code,
  ANY_VALUE(region) AS region
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_health_population.country_summary*`
GROUP BY
  country_code
country_region_lookup.description: Canonical mapping of each country code to its region name using all shards of the country_summary tables (include all _TABLE_SUFFIX values). One row per country_code with its associated region field.

crime_records_clean.name: crime_records_clean
crime_records_clean.body_sql:
SELECT
  CAST(year AS INT64) AS year,
  minor_category,
  borough,
  lsoa_code,
  value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
WHERE
  minor_category IS NOT NULL
  AND TRIM(minor_category) <> ''
  AND year IS NOT NULL
crime_records_clean.description: Cleaned/cohort of crime rows with normalized year and non-empty minor_category. Converts/derives a numeric year from the crime date column and excludes rows where minor_category is NULL or empty. Keeps borough and lsoa_code to allow aggregation to London totals.

year_category_counts.name: year_category_counts
year_category_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  minor_category,
  SUM(value) AS category_count
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  year,
  minor_category
year_category_counts.description: Aggregate crime counts per year and minor_category across all geographic units (keeps rows at one year + minor_category). This produces the total number of crimes for each minor_category in a given year (suitable for computing shares).

year_total_counts.name: year_total_counts
year_total_counts.body_sql:
SELECT
  year,
  SUM(value) AS year_total
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  year
ORDER BY
  year
year_total_counts.description: Total number of crimes per year across all minor categories (London-wide yearly totals).

year_category_ranked.name: year_category_ranked
year_category_ranked.body_sql:
SELECT
  yc.year AS year,
  yc.minor_category AS minor_category,
  yc.category_count AS category_count,
  RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY yc.year ORDER BY yc.category_count DESC) AS category_rank
FROM
  `year_category_counts` AS yc
year_category_ranked.description: For each year, rank minor_category rows by category_count descending so top categories per year can be selected. Keeps year, minor_category, category_count and the rank position.

yearly_crime_totals.name: yearly_crime_totals
yearly_crime_totals.body_sql:
SELECT
  cr.year AS year,
  SUM(cr.value) AS total_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa` AS cr
GROUP BY
  cr.year
ORDER BY
  cr.year
yearly_crime_totals.description: Yearly aggregated totals of crime 'value' grouped by year for any provided cohort of crime records.

crime_rows_for_borough.name: crime_rows_for_borough
crime_rows_for_borough.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  lsoa_code,
  major_category,
  minor_category,
  year,
  month,
  value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
WHERE
  borough = @borough_param
crime_rows_for_borough.description: Subset of crime_by_lsoa rows limited to a single borough. Keeps all original columns for downstream aggregation.

crime_major_minor_canonicalized.name: crime_major_minor_canonicalized
crime_major_minor_canonicalized.body_sql:
SELECT
  -- preserve keys
  borough,
  lsoa_code,
  -- normalize major and minor category text: trim, collapse internal spaces, title-case common words, uppercase ACRONYMS, and coalesce unknowns
  -- major_category normalization
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(major_category) = '' OR major_category IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
    ELSE INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(major_category), r'\s+', ' '))
  END AS major_category,
  -- minor_category normalization
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(minor_category) = '' OR minor_category IS NULL THEN 'Unknown'
    ELSE
      -- specific known harmonizations: common variants to canonical names
      CASE
        WHEN LOWER(TRIM(minor_category)) IN ('other theft person','other theft - person') THEN 'Other Theft Person'
        WHEN LOWER(TRIM(minor_category)) IN ('theft from shops','shoplifting') THEN 'Theft From Shops'
        WHEN LOWER(TRIM(minor_category)) = 'burglary in a dwelling' THEN 'Burglary - Residential'
        WHEN LOWER(TRIM(minor_category)) = 'burglary in other buildings' THEN 'Burglary - Business and Community'
        ELSE INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(minor_category), r'\s+', ' '))
      END
  END AS minor_category,
  -- time keys preserved
  year,
  month,
  -- ensure value is integer
  CAST(value AS INT64) AS value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
crime_major_minor_canonicalized.description: Normalize and clean major_category and minor_category text and ensure value is cast to integer; preserves row-level geography/time keys.

major_category_total_per_lsoa_time.name: major_category_total_per_lsoa_time
major_category_total_per_lsoa_time.body_sql:
SELECT
  borough,
  lsoa_code,
  year,
  month,
  major_category,
  SUM(value) AS total_value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.london_crime.crime_by_lsoa`
GROUP BY
  borough,
  lsoa_code,
  year,
  month,
  major_category
major_category_total_per_lsoa_time.description: Aggregate (sum) incident values per major_category at the row-level of LSOA + year + month (prepares totals that can be rolled up further).

images_non_null_original_url.name: images_non_null_original_url
images_non_null_original_url.body_sql:
SELECT
  image_id,
  original_url
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images`
WHERE
  original_url IS NOT NULL
images_non_null_original_url.description: All image rows with a non-null original_url; a clean cohort of images to consider for downstream membership checks.

labels_cat_flag.name: labels_cat_flag
labels_cat_flag.body_sql:
SELECT
  image_id,
  label_name,
  confidence
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels`
WHERE
  label_name = '/m/01yrx'
grain: one row per image_id, label_name, confidence
labels_cat_flag.description: Normalized label rows indicating presence of the specific 'cat' label (label_name = '/m/01yrx') and the confidence value; one row per label instance with canonicalized columns for membership checks.

image_has_cat_label.name: image_has_cat_label
image_has_cat_label.body_sql:
SELECT
  l.image_id AS image_id,
  EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels` AS sub
    WHERE sub.image_id = l.image_id
      AND sub.label_name = '/m/01yrx'
      AND sub.confidence = 1
  ) AS has_cat_conf1
FROM (
  SELECT DISTINCT image_id
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels`
) AS l
image_has_cat_label.description: Per-image boolean/cohort indicating whether at least one label row exists for that image with label_name = '/m/01yrx' and confidence = 1.

agricultural_production_state_rows.name: agricultural_production_state_rows
agricultural_production_state_rows.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX AS year,
  state_name,
  state_alpha,
  commodity_desc,
  group_desc,
  unit_desc,
  CAST(value AS NUMERIC) AS value
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.usda_nass_agriculture.census*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2002' AND '2012'
  AND agg_level_desc = 'STATE'
  AND statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION'
  AND value IS NOT NULL
agricultural_production_state_rows.description: Selects state-level agricultural production rows from the raw census table(s), keeping rows for any commodity/year/unit/value but filtered to agg_level_desc = 'STATE', statisticcat_desc = 'PRODUCTION', and non-null value. This yields the cohort of state production observations to be aggregated later.

irs_990_raw_rows_filtered.name: irs_990_raw_rows_filtered
irs_990_raw_rows_filtered.body_sql:
SELECT
  _TABLE_SUFFIX,
  CAST(tax_pd AS STRING) AS tax_pd,
  ein,
  CAST(totrevenue AS INT64) AS totrevenue,
  CAST(totfuncexpns AS INT64) AS totfuncexpns
FROM
  `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_*`
WHERE
  _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '990_2012' AND '990_2017'
  AND ein IS NOT NULL
  -- keep rows that have the monetary fields present (non-NULL)
  AND totrevenue IS NOT NULL
  AND totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL
irs_990_raw_rows_filtered.description: Select raw rows from the irs_990 shard tables and filter out rows missing the monetary fields needed for later analysis. Keep the table-level year identifier (from _TABLE_SUFFIX) as a column for later grouping.

channels_with_multiple_countries.name: channels_with_multiple_countries
channels_with_multiple_countries.body_sql:
SELECT
  channelGrouping AS channelGrouping,
  COUNT(DISTINCT geoNetwork.country) AS country_count
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`,
  UNNEST(hits) AS hit
WHERE
  -- liftable literal: consider only transaction hits (type = 'TRANSACTION') and require a transaction id
  hit.type = 'TRANSACTION'
  AND SAFE_CAST(hit.transaction.transactionId AS STRING) IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY
  channelGrouping
HAVING
  COUNT(DISTINCT geoNetwork.country) > 1
channels_with_multiple_countries.description: Identify channelGrouping values that appear in more than one distinct geoNetwork_country (based on the cleaned/deduplicated transactions); one row per channelGrouping.

web_analytics_clean_visits.name: web_analytics_clean_visits
web_analytics_clean_visits.body_sql:
SELECT
  COALESCE(CAST(fullVisitorId AS STRING), '') AS fullVisitorId,
  CAST(COALESCE(totals.transactions, totals.visits, 0) AS INT64) AS transactions,
  visitId
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics`
web_analytics_clean_visits.description: Canonicalize and clean web_analytics rows: ensure fullVisitorId is not null, cast totals.transactions to INTEGER when present, and keep only relevant columns for visitor and transaction analysis.

per_visitor_transaction_summary.name: per_visitor_transaction_summary
per_visitor_transaction_summary.body_sql:
SELECT
  r.fullVisitorId AS fullVisitorId,
  SUM(IFNULL(r.totals_transactions, 0)) AS total_transactions_per_visitor,
  CASE WHEN SUM(IFNULL(r.totals_transactions, 0)) > 0 THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_purchaser
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ecommerce.rev_transactions` r
GROUP BY
  r.fullVisitorId
per_visitor_transaction_summary.description: For each visitor (fullVisitorId), compute the total number of transactions across all their rows and a flag indicating whether they are a purchaser (has at least one transaction).

unique_visitors_cohort.name: unique_visitors_cohort
unique_visitors_cohort.body_sql:
SELECT
  wa.fullVisitorId
FROM
  `data-to-insights.ecommerce.web_analytics` AS wa
GROUP BY
  wa.fullVisitorId
unique_visitors_cohort.description: One row per unique visitor (fullVisitorId) present in web_analytics (used to count distinct visitors).
